body: Ties with new hometown sealed - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Society Home China Society Ties with new hometown sealed A chance encounter inspires a community to strengthen its bond with Keqiao By CHEN YE in Hangzhou | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-13 07:16 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Neeraj Punhani donates blood during the 9th Blood Donation Camp organized by the Indian community in Keqiao district, Shaoxing, Zhejiang province, on Nov 2, 2025. CHINA DAILY Rolling up his sleeves and extending his arm to donate blood has become a familiar ritual for Neeraj Punhani. For 12 years, the 49-year-old Indian has regularly joined blood donation drives in Keqiao district of Shaoxing, Zhejiang province, where he has lived for 23 years while running a textile import business that exports products to India. It all began with a 12-year-old girl nicknamed Jia Jia. In December 2014, she was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Doctors said she would need blood transfusions and chemotherapy for a long time. The need for blood, coupled with mounting medical expenses, pushed her father, Wei Baoshi, who supported a family of five through odd jobs, to the brink of despair. On Dec 22, 2014, Punhani saw a post on the social media app WeChat saying Jia Jia was urgently in need of blood. Moved by a photo of the girl who had lost her hair during chemotherapy, he decided to help. "I wanted to help this girl. It touched my heart because my brothers and sisters and I all have daughters. So I felt like our own daughter needed help." The next morning, Punhani brought 16 fellow Indians and three Chinese friends to Hangzhou, capital of Zhejiang, to donate blood. On Jan 3, 2015, more than 100 Indians arrived at a blood donation center in Keqiao, with 96 donating a total of 33.8 liters of blood. More Indians who had been away on business returned to donate the following day. The support went further than blood donations. Two weeks later, Punhani and his Indian friends raised 160,000 yuan ($23,800) to help cover Jia Jia's medical expenses. The experience prompted Punhani to turn a one-time act of kindness into a long-running tradition. He began promoting voluntary blood donations through WeChat and posters at Indian companies, restaurants and other places frequented by Indians. The effort was also rooted in an earlier experience. On May 9, 2013, an Indian man who worked in Keqiao fell seriously ill and urgently needed blood plasma. The Zhejiang Blood Center and Shaoxing Central Blood Station organized a campaign under the theme "love without borders, blood continues life", in which 76 Chinese people donated blood for him. He later recovered. "I thought to myself at the time that I must find an opportunity to do something for this city," Punhani said. Since then, Punhani and his fellow Indians in Keqiao have organized nine blood donation campaigns, involving 754 donations and collecting 278.7 liters of blood. The largest campaign attracted 141 Indian donors. "Since Punhani and his fellow Indians helped Jia Jia at the end of 2014, they have contacted us every year to inform Indian community members about the time and number of participants for their group blood donations," said Jin Danting, an official of Shaoxing Central Blood Station. "They have kept it up for 12 years. Their sincerity and self-lessness have deeply moved us. This kind of love that crosses national borders is truly precious." Jia Jia's father, Wei, said: "I'm grateful to everyone who helped us back then." He said the girl has made a very good recovery. Over the past 12 years, Wei has visited Punhani's company almost every year, sitting down with him to catch up and once again express his gratitude. "Although communication can sometimes be a little difficult, we have overcome the barriers of language and become good friends," Wei said. For Punhani and his fellow Indians, however, donating blood is about more than giving. "When we donate blood and feel that our blood may save someone's life, we feel from the bottom of our hearts that we are doing something for humanity, which has given us so much joy." Many Indian businesspeople have put down roots in Keqiao, home to China Textile City, a major global textile trading hub. Indian businesspeople began arriving in the area in the early 1990s, following historical routes of the Silk Road. Today more than 1,000 Indians live in Keqiao, making them the district's largest foreign business community. body: Alliance hails smart farming, rural growth - World - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE World Asia-Pacific Americas Europe Middle East Africa China-US China-Europe China-Japan China-Africa Home World / Asia-Pacific Home / World / Asia-Pacific Alliance hails smart farming, rural growth By ZHAO YIMENG | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-13 07:51 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE For Indian student Aarafat Chouhan, a visit to Qiantang district in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, offered a close look into how technology is improving rural life and agricultural practices. "Honestly, I was most excited to see smart farming and digital tech in action right here on the ground," he said. Chouhan is among dozens of international students who are members of the BRICS Youth Agricultural Development Promotion Alliance, which was officially launched in Qiantang in June. The alliance, comprised of 58 students from BRICS countries and partners, is focused on modern agriculture, rural governance and the integration of agriculture and tourism. The initiative is aimed at turning international students into observers and potential participants in rural development, granting them a firsthand experience in local agricultural projects and an opportunity to explore how China's rural vitalization practices can be replicated in other countries. Chouhan, a student at China Jiliang University in Hangzhou, highlighted how agriculture is deeply connected to people's lives and the economy in India, adding, however, that farmers continue to face significant challenges. "What really draws me to Qiantang is seeing how practical technology is put straight into the hands of everyday farmers," Chouhan said. "It's not just tech for the sake of tech, but actually improving real livelihoods. That's a model I really want to understand better." He is also interested in how the district is making rural areas more attractive to young entrepreneurs. It builds incubators, offers policy incentives and provides solid digital infrastructure so that starting an agricultural business actually makes financial sense, he said. According to local authorities, Qiantang has established 16 practice stations — for young people visiting rural areas for firsthand experiences — and cultivated 525 agricultural entrepreneurs. Chouhan said the approach has relevance for both China and India, where young people often move to big cities in search of employment. "Qiantang shows that if you modernize the countryside, young people will happily bring their talent back home," he added. For Zafarbek Abdullaev, an Uzbek student and member of the alliance, his interest is in how rural tourism drives local economies. "To be exact, I'm focused on how a normal farming village like Xinjiang (in Qiantang district) turns its land, its food, and its story into real income, and still keeps its young people at home," he said. He highlighted the role of young agricultural entrepreneurs who return to rural areas to start businesses, sell products online, develop brands and operate guesthouses. "Villages join together, share one brand, and bargain as a group. So one farmer does not stand alone against a big company. I believe this is the part most worth copying," he said. In Uzbekistan, rural communities have abundant cultural resources, traditional foods and handicrafts but are still struggling to find ways to generate more income locally, he said. The Qiantang fieldwork is being further supported by a rural vitalization competition among international students. As part of the competition, students from BRICS nations and countries involved in the Belt and Road Initiative are invited to conduct in-depth research into villages in Qiantang and document rural development through photographic, written and data works. "Being an observer is a great opportunity because it bridges the gap between theory and actual reality," Chouhan said. "It's one thing to read about rural development on paper, but using photos, videos, and real field data makes these lessons genuine and easy for other developing nations to learn from." Abdullaev said international students should go beyond simply describing China's achievements. "Our job is not to say 'China is amazing' and go home. It is to turn what we saw into something another country can actually use," he said. Teng Lingjian, chairman of the Hangzhou Qiantang Center for Contemporary Internationalization Studies, said agriculture provides common ground for cooperation among BRICS countries. "When international students take successful entrepreneurial experiences back to their countries, this kind of visible result is what makes technology sharing truly effective," Teng said. At the same time, the center plans to take a more proactive approach by sending its agricultural technologies, entrepreneurs and young talent to BRICS countries. "We hope to have deeper communication and cooperation with local agricultural projects and researchers," Teng said. The final goal is to address major issues of common concern among BRICS countries, such as food security, he added. Chen Ye in Hangzhou contributed to this story. body: Xi eyes BRICS' next 'golden decade' - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Latest Home China Latest Xi eyes BRICS' next 'golden decade' He hails past 20 years of growth and vitality, calls for promoting innovation, peace and stability By MO JINGXI in New Delhi | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-09-13 00:26 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE President Xi Jinping is warmly welcomed after he arrived on Saturday at an airport in New Delhi, India, to attend the 18th BRICS Summit at the invitation of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. XIE HUANCHI / XINHUA President Xi Jinping said on Saturday that China is ready to work with all parties to build consensus and usher in a third "golden decade" of BRICS cooperation, calling on the grouping to lead efforts to advance innovation, safeguard peace and stability, promote mutual learning among civilizations and improve global governance. Addressing Session I of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the capital of India, Xi said China will assume the rotating presidency of BRICS next year and host the 19th summit. China previously hosted BRICS summits in 2011, 2017 and 2022. This year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation, which emerged amid the collective rise of emerging markets and developing countries. Xi said solidarity and cooperation have remained the source of strength for BRICS throughout its two-decade journey. He urged members to treat one another with sincerity, seek common ground while respecting differences, and respect each other's core concerns. Members should deepen mutual understanding and properly manage differences through communication and dialogue to ensure the steady and long-term development of BRICS cooperation, he said. From its original four members, BRICS has grown into a family of 11 full members and 10 partner countries. Its members account for nearly half the world's population and over one-fourth of global trade. Xi said the grouping's historic expansion and comprehensive, multilevel cooperation framework have ushered in a new stage of high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation. With unilateralism and power politics undermining multilateralism and the international order, BRICS countries should stand firmly on the right side of history, steer the international order toward greater fairness and equity, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity, he said. On innovation-driven development, Xi welcomed BRICS countries' participation in the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, which was launched by China in July and is based in Shanghai, and proposed a BRICS initiative on using AI to advance new industrialization. On peace and stability, Xi noted that the situation in the Middle East remains complex and fluid, and said China will work with fellow BRICS members to play a due role in bringing peace and tranquility to the Middle East and the Gulf region. Xi also called for greater mutual learning among civilizations through the BRICS people-to-people exchanges forum, the sharing of governance experience, and deeper cooperation in the areas of culture, tourism and education, including more exchanges among young people. On global governance, he urged support for the multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core and called for opposition to all forms of protectionism. BRICS should help shape governance in emerging areas such as cyberspace, outer space and the deep sea, while strengthening the voice of the Global South, he said. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said BRICS has established a distinct identity on the global stage over the past 20 years by respecting different perspectives and moving forward through consensus. AI, cyberspace, outer space, biotechnology and critical technologies are shaping not only future opportunities, but also the rules that will govern the future, Modi said. "We must work to transform the Global South from rule-takers into rule-shapers," he said. The meeting participants highly commended the development achievements made by BRICS over the past two decades, saying that BRICS countries have a responsibility to speak out for the Global South, defend multilateralism and jointly address global challenges in the face of intensifying geopolitical conflicts and rising unilateralism. They said they appreciate China's important contribution to the development and expansion of the BRICS mechanism, and also support China in successfully hosting the 19th BRICS Summit during its presidency next year and working together to push BRICS cooperation to a new level. The summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration of the 18th BRICS Summit. China has been an important participant, builder and promoter of BRICS. Xi has, at different key stages, proposed a series of initiatives for the grouping's development. In 2014, he advocated the BRICS spirit of openness, inclusiveness and win-win cooperation. In 2017, he proposed the "BRICS Plus" cooperation approach, extending BRICS cooperation beyond its members to the broader Global South. In 2024, he called for a BRICS committed to peace, innovation, green development, justice and closer people-to-people exchanges. Lan Jianxue, director of the Department for Asia-Pacific Studies at the China Institute of International Studies, said these proposals have helped guide and broaden BRICS cooperation, extending it beyond economic ties into a more comprehensive framework. China could draw on its comprehensive industrial system, as well as BRICS' innovation and AI cooperation platforms, to share technologies, conduct joint research and provide training, Lan said. Such efforts could help partner countries develop digital industries and participate more fully in industrial and supply chains. Ayanda Holo, president of TV BRICS Africa, said he looks forward to covering next year's summit in China. Citing China's moves to offer zero-tariff access to African countries with which it has diplomatic relations, Holo said he hopes other BRICS members and partners could also gain greater access to the Chinese market and share in the opportunities created by China's development. During the meeting, leaders from BRICS countries also visited a photo exhibition, planted trees and posed for a group photo. President Xi Jinping on Tuesday delivered a speech at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Plus Meeting in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan. The following is the full text of the speech: Jointly Advocating an Equal and Orderly Multipolar World and Making Global Governance More Just and Equitable Statement by H.E. Xi Jinping President of the People's Republic of China At the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Plus Meeting Bishkek, September 1, 2026 Your Excellency President Sadyr Zhaparov, Colleagues, It gives me great pleasure to join fellow members and partners of the SCO family in celebrating the 25th anniversary of our organization. I wish to thank President Zhaparov for his kind invitation and the thoughtful arrangements by the government of Kyrgyzstan. The meeting today focuses on strengthening the role of the United Nations and building a multipolar world, and it demonstrates SCO's commitment to reforming and improving global governance as required by our times. Currently, major changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the globe. Hegemonism, unilateralism and protectionism are resurging against historical trends. Nevertheless, the overwhelming majority of the world do not condone power politics, conflict and confrontation, or isolation and backwardness. What they want instead is to hold a place on the world stage through national development and international cooperation. In recent years, the rise of the Global South is driving a profound shift in the international balance of power. The trend toward a multipolar world is irreversible. What kind of multipolarity does the world need? How are countries going to take part in and promote it? The international community should build consensus and make the right choice that can stand the test of practice and history. As a responsible major country, China advocates for an equal and orderly multipolar world. Sovereign equality and mutual respect are fundamental principles. The history of the world is written by all nations. Multipolarity, independent choice of development paths, and greater democracy in international relations are the right way forward. We should ensure equal rights, equal opportunities and equal rules for all countries, regardless of their size, strength and wealth. As an important part of a multipolar world and a key driving force behind it, the Global South countries ought to have greater representation and voice in international affairs. Balance, order and the rule of law are inherent requirements. The purposes and principles of the UN Charter set the basic norms of international relations, and serve as the bedrock of the postwar international order. We should promote the common values of humanity, reject double standards, exceptionalism, foreign interference, bullying and the law of the jungle, and advance the rule of law in international relations. Major countries in particular should take the lead in observing international norms and honoring the rule of law, and work together to tackle global challenges. Multilateralism, dialogue and consultation are essential pathways. The domination of international affairs by a few is an injustice left over from history, and global governance dictated by one, a few or a bloc of countries is not true multilateralism. World affairs should be discussed by all, and international norms should be set by all. The authority and vitality of the UN need to be restored. Multilateral mechanisms, global and regional, should enhance their coordination and improve their efficiency. Mutual benefit, win-win, and inclusiveness are the way forward for development. Countries are not isolated islands, but partners with intertwined interests and a shared future. Protectionism, decoupling and supply-chain disruption will lead nowhere. We should focus on the development agenda, uphold openness and cooperation, and bridge the digital and AI divides, so that technological revolution and development achievements can benefit all nations. Colleagues, After a 25-year journey, the SCO has successfully set a stellar example in conducting relations among big countries, among neighbors, and among countries of different sizes. It has successfully brought together half of the world's population and a quarter of the global economy, generating strong driving forces for development. A more united and vibrant SCO is fully capable of making greater contributions to an equal and orderly multipolar world. First, we should advance common prosperity in the vast continent straddling Asia and Europe with the SCO Strength. Cooperation within the SCO has been fruitful in political, security, economic, trade, people-to-people and cultural domains, and our organization is now a key platform for Eurasian countries to jointly pursue development and tackle challenges. We should continue to leverage our strengths, unlock our potential, and connect the multiple growth poles across the continent through high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. We should empower each other, help each other succeed, and work together to create new opportunities and promote shared prosperity. body: Payment, currency ties to boost BRICS - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Business Macro Companies Industries Technology Motoring China Data Finance Top 10 Home / Business / Policies Home Business Policies Payment, currency ties to boost BRICS Stronger cooperation among members seen as crucial to bolstering financial autonomy, resilience By Zhou Lanxu | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-13 07:17 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE WANG XIAOYING/CHINA DAILY Ongoing efforts by BRICS members to strengthen payment and currency cooperation are seen as crucial to bolstering their financial autonomy and resilience amid growing concerns over the dollar-centric international monetary system, experts said. Practical avenues include extending existing bilateral payment arrangements, expanding local currency settlements and broadening access to infrastructure such as the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) and the multilateral central bank digital currency (CBDC) platform mBridge, they said. Progress, however, is likely to be incremental, as monetary sovereignty remains a central consideration in coordinating rules across economies. Such cooperation is more likely to complement and help rebalance the existing global monetary system than to fundamentally reshape it in the near term, they added. The assessments come as BRICS leaders meet in India, against the backdrop of continuing efforts to explore greater connectivity among members' payment systems. At the July 2025 summit in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, members tasked finance ministers and central bank governors with continuing discussions on the BRICS Cross-Border Payments Initiative. The declaration also acknowledged the payment task force's progress in identifying possible pathways toward greater interoperability and welcomed a technical report on cross-border payments. Analysts said a more fragmented global economic and political landscape has strengthened the case for BRICS payment cooperation, as members seek greater financial autonomy and reduced vulnerability to financial surveillance and sanctions by the United States and other Western powers. Yang Tao, a council member of the National Institution for Finance & Development, highlighted in his remarks and writings that closer payment cooperation could reduce BRICS members' reliance on the US dollar and Western-dominated financial infrastructure, including SWIFT, while strengthening their financial autonomy and resilience to any possible sanctions. "The most realistic approach is to start bilaterally and move toward multilateral cooperation, gradually building on existing bilateral arrangements rather than trying to establish a unified system in one step," Yang said. Liu Xiaochun, vice-president of the Shanghai Finance Institute, said cross-border dollar payments and clearing routed through US-based clearing banks and the Clearing House Interbank Payments System, or CHIPS, fall within the reach of US regulatory oversight and sanctions enforcement, giving countries an incentive to diversify payment channels. Beyond dollar clearing, Liu highlighted the importance of access to financial messaging data. Following the 9/11, 2001, attacks, the US Treasury Department established the Terrorist Finance Tracking Program to obtain certain transaction records on SWIFT — the prominent global financial messaging network — for counter-terrorism investigations, which, in practice, gives US authorities a means to trace cross-border financial flows. According to Liu, BRICS countries seeking greater autonomy in cross-border payments need to consider three key questions: how to move from dollar dominance toward the use of multiple currencies; whether to develop financial messaging channels independent of SWIFT; and how digital currencies could bring the transfer of monetary value, payment messaging and settlement onto a common platform. Gradual approach Bilateral cooperation has been underway. The People's Bank of China, the country's central bank, has appointed local banks in Brazil, South Africa and Indonesia as renminbi clearing banks, providing infrastructure to facilitate the currency's use in bilateral trade and investment. In June, China and Indonesia have officially launched the China-Indonesia Cross-Border QR Code Payment Connectivity project. UnionPay International and ICBC Brazil also signed a memorandum last year to enable UnionPay participating wallets to scan QR codes and pay directly at merchants within Brazil's PIX network. The move illustrates how bilateral arrangements can underpin efforts to make cross-border payments more convenient, without requiring a common currency. Liu said that a common BRICS currency would be impractical under current conditions. In his assessment, differences among member economies and currency movements would make it difficult to coordinate an arrangement capable of maintaining a stable value and securing user confidence. Similarly, Liu said that expanding CIPS — the primary platform for cross-border yuan clearing and settlement — would be more practical than building a separate messaging network from scratch. Replicating SWIFT's messaging functions would be technically achievable, but a new network with much lower transaction volumes could struggle to cover its substantial costs. He cited CIPS' integrated messaging and clearing functions, modern messaging standards and access for foreign banks as direct participants as foundations for broader international use, suggesting that opening CIPS further to equity participation by foreign banks would strengthen its international appeal. By the end of 2025, CIPS had 193 direct participants and 1,573 indirect participants, according to its operator. It processed 180.2 trillion yuan ($26.9 trillion) in payments that year, up from 175 trillion yuan in 2024. Revised CIPS business rules, effective from February, allow overseas CIPS direct participants to appoint any qualified direct participant — not necessarily an onshore bank — as their custodian, a change analysts said will significantly lower entry barriers for foreign lenders. Digital currencies offer another avenue, although connecting platforms will require more than technological innovation, Liu said. "Cross-border CBDC payment arrangements would require detailed cooperation between bilateral regulators and alignment of rules, making their cross-border expansion a relatively lengthy process." Miao Yanliang, chief economist at China International Capital Corp, said, "The digital yuan has the potential to expand the RMB's role in international settlement and payments, with its programmability enabling fast and secure large-value cross-border transactions." One existing platform is mBridge, a project that explores a shared platform for cross-border payments and settlement using multiple CBDCs. The platform's cumulative transaction value had reached almost 500 billion yuan by end-2025, with more than 95 percent of the transactions made using e-CNY payment methods as of end-November 2025. Challenges remain Miao, however, said the key challenge is interoperability: Connecting payment infrastructure across jurisdictions while bridging differences in technical standards and compliance regimes. Overcoming those barriers would broaden the market access and users the digital yuan could serve. More broadly, Yang pointed to differences in members' financial systems, currencies and anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing requirements when advancing cross-border payment cooperation. The absence of common governance rules, compounded by geopolitical mistrust, could further slow implementation. Yang identified expanding local currency financing by the New Development Bank and advancing currency diversificat

body: China, US see success in fight against crime - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Society Home China Society China, US see success in fight against crime Two countries tightening controls on drug-related substances, chemicals By CAO YIN | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-12 08:52 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE A new transnational case involving the production and trafficking of precursor chemicals has been resolved, highlighting intensified counternarcotics cooperation between China and the United States. China's Ministry of Public Security said on Thursday that it had worked with the US Federal Bureau of Investigation to crack down on a cross-border case involving the production and trafficking of synthetic cannabinoid precursors. In early May, US authorities alerted China about two Chinese nationals, identified by their surnames as Xing and Song, according to the ministry. Further investigation found that they were connected to an ongoing domestic case in China, prompting the ministry to consolidate the investigations. By mid-August, coordinated efforts by police in Hebei province and other regions led to a unified operation that resulted in the capture of 21 suspects, including Xing and Song, and the seizure of various non-scheduled precursor chemicals that could be used in illicit drug production, the ministry said. US authorities had previously arrested two suspects linked to the case in the United States. The individuals had purchased non-scheduled precursor chemicals and manufactured drugs, which were then distributed to inmates in several federal and state prisons, the ministry said. The resolution of the case underscores the effective functioning of the China-US counternarcotics law enforcement cooperation mechanism and represents a significant achievement in the ongoing collaboration between Chinese and US counternarcotics agencies, the ministry added. In January 2024, the two countries launched the China-US Counternarcotics Working Group in Beijing, identifying priority areas for cooperation. On July 31 that year, a Chinese interdepartmental delegation visited the US for the first senior officials' meeting of the working group, helping build mutual trust and advance practical cooperation. Since then, China's Narcotics Control Bureau has maintained routine hotline contact and regular exchanges with US counternarcotics agencies, exchanging more than 100 intelligence leads. In July, China's Ministry of Public Security said that bilateral counternarcotics cooperation had become increasingly institutionalized, leading to joint investigations of several major transnational cases. Those cases include a drug smuggling and trafficking case involving suspects led by a man surnamed Guo, and a transnational new psychoactive substances trafficking case involving suspects led by a man surnamed Gong. The operations dismantled drug trafficking routes between China and the US, the ministry said. In August, a Chinese court sentenced a man and his son to prison and imposed fines for trafficking precursor chemicals abroad, as part of broader efforts by the two countries to combat narcotics. The ministry said the strengthened cooperation follows the important consensus reached by the two nations, reflecting renewed engagement in combating transnational crime and tightening controls on narcotics-related substances and chemicals. caoyin@chinadaily.com.cn Photo Heilongjiang begins autumn rice harvest across black soil fields Colorful activities mark Teachers' Day across China Snow leopard repeatedly spotted in Gansu's Qilian Mountains Evacuated residents returning home after Gyirong mudslide Neighbors give Lao hospitals healthy dose of support The commercial evolution of Yiwu Latest China, US see success in fight against crime China announces five-year action plan aimed at developing digital villages CPC expels former senior official of Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps Bots assemble in Shanghai Gansu's former vice-governor Lei Siwei expelled from CPC Taishan Mountain to host inaugural world robot competition State Council News Policies concerning expats, foreign enterprises in August 2026 China issues regulations to improve management of local market regulators Xi urges efforts to prevent major accidents after cargo ship fire in east China Exclusive Hands off! body: BRICS countries rally to counter shocks of power politics, unilateralism: China Daily editorial - Opinion - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Opinion Cartoons Editorials Global Lens We Comment Columnists Global Views Chinese Perspectives Opinion Line Home Opinion / Editorials Home / Opinion / Editorials BRICS countries rally to counter shocks of power politics, unilateralism: China Daily editorial chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-09-13 01:13 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE The 18th BRICS Summit, which opened on Saturday in New Delhi, the capital of India, is an opportunity for the participating countries to build consensus on development through strategic communication, improve the quality of development through practical cooperation, resolve differences through dialogue and consultation, and address risks and challenges through solidarity and collaboration. This year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation. Over the past two decades, the BRICS cooperation mechanism has become the world's most influential platform for cooperation among emerging markets and developing countries. In his speech at Session I of the summit, President Xi Jinping reviewed the development of BRICS cooperation over the past two decades, underscoring that it has been 20 years of self-reliance and self-strengthening, with the member countries standing together through thick and thin and engaging in fruitful cooperation. This has helped safeguard the common interests of the Global South, provided the world with stability and positive momentum, and ushered the grouping into a new stage of high-quality development with greater BRICS cooperation. BRICS has become a major force for advancing a multipolar world and greater democracy in international relations. The grouping's growing influence is reflected in its expansion to 11 member countries and 10 partner countries, and in its economic and demographic scale. BRICS countries now account for approximately 40 percent of global GDP at purchasing power parity and nearly half of the world's population. With the countercurrents of unilateralism and power politics surging, multilateralism and the international order are coming under strain, and the deficits in peace, development, security and governance continue to widen. That should further inspire the BRICS countries to stand firmly on the right side of history, strive to be pioneers of the times, steer the international order toward greater justice and equity, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity. To that end, Xi called on BRICS to be a pioneer in pursuing innovation-driven development, upholding peace and stability, facilitating mutual learning between civilizations, and reforming and improving global governance. Putting those proposals into action will help BRICS countries firmly seize the initiative in shaping their future. This will enable them to uphold a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, and play a constructive role in resolving hot spot issues by addressing both symptoms and root causes. It will also help them promote a fairer and more equitable global governance system. Xi also proposed an initiative to promote new industrialization through artificial intelligence among BRICS countries, and said that China is willing to work with all parties to deliver more outcomes in research, development and application, and deepen cooperation in industrial and supply chains. Xi also advocated efforts to deepen cooperation in culture, tourism and education, strengthen youth exchanges and promote more frequent interactions and closer bonds among the peoples. These all represent concrete actions in China's commitment to advancing BRICS development and playing an active role. Urging the group to deepen mutual understanding through communication and dialogue, Xi said that the BRICS countries should remain sincere and candid with one another, seek common ground while respecting differences, and respect each other's core concerns. Over an extraordinary two-decade journey, solidarity and cooperation have remained the driving force behind the BRICS cause, Xi stressed. China will take over as the rotating chair of BRICS and host its 19th summit next year, and the Chinese side stands ready to work with all parties to build consensus, create a better future and embark on BRICS' third "golden decade", jointly opening up a bright future of prosperity and progress. The leaders attending the summit reached a common understanding across a range of important areas, including security, cooperation and development, and adopted a joint declaration on Saturday. This demonstrates BRICS countries' clear-eyed assessment of the opportunities and challenges they face, as well as their shared willingness to build greater consensus on issues of common concern. This will help create favorable conditions for China, as the next rotating chair, to steer BRICS toward even greater development in the next stage. body: Hotel robots surprise visitors, streamline operations - Chinadaily.com.cn WS6aa122a5e4b06d4aa055d2b4 China Edition | Global Edition | ASIA | 中文 China Latest Society Innovation Education Cross-Strait HK/Macao Health Environment Military Video World Asia-Pacific Americas Europe Middle East Africa Business Policies Companies Industries Technology China Up-close China Data Motoring Video Culture Art Music and Theater Film and TV Books Heritage Events and Festivals People Cultural Exchange Video Photo Gallery Fashion Health Travel News City Tours Guides and Tips My Footprints Around the World Features Photo Video Food Sports Soccer Basketball Volleyball Tennis Golf Track and field Swimming Motor China Stars Opinion Cartoons Editorials Global Lens We Comment Columnists Global Views Chinese Perspectives Opinion Line Regional Newspaper China Daily PDF China Daily E-Paper China Daily Global PDF China Daily Global E-Paper Mobile CULTURE News Heritage Art Film Theater Fashion Cultural Exchange Books Photo Video HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE 中文 CULTURE News Heritage Art Film Theater Fashion Cultural Exchange Books Photo Video Home / Culture / China Vibes Hotel robots surprise visitors, streamline operations From pushy elevator companions to trusted delivery helpers, machines are winning over guests and staff alike By BAI SHUHAO | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-10 06:50 Share - WeChat When Ricky Colomer Goenaga, 32, a designer from Spain, looked around and noticed a delivery robot following him, he wasn't quite sure how to react. New to Shanghai and living at a hotel, he stepped into an elevator — and a white, waist-high box on wheels followed him in. The robot, in Goenaga's words, was rather assertive. It nudged him out of the middle of the elevator, nearly ran over his toes and rattled off something in Chinese he didn't understand. Then it pressed the button for its desired floor and rolled out as soon as the elevator doors opened. "I was like, 'what happened here?'" Goenaga recalled. He said that he wasn't quite sure what the machine even was — bigger and bulkier than, yet nothing like, the robotic vacuums he'd seen. One and a half years on, the sight of a robot gliding through hotel lobbies and corridors no longer fazes him. In March, on a business trip to Beijing, he keyed his room number into the order system and waited. Soon, the robot arrived at his door carrying his packed salad. This time, Goenaga was all grins. He posed for a photograph with the machine and posted it on social media, joking that after being "bullied" by the robot in Shanghai, the two had finally made peace. For many foreign visitors, the robot is among the first surprises they encounter in China. Social media are full of posts about their "meetings" with the machines in their hotels, with comments such as "I'm sharing the elevator with robots!" or "China is on another level of efficiency". In China, however, such robots are no longer a novelty. According to a report released in August by IIM, a Beijing-based industry research organization, the penetration rate of hotel service robots in China exceeded 30 percent in 2025 and is expected to surpass 50 percent by 2030. For hotels, the appeal is simple: Robots can handle repetitive tasks around the clock. "I think they are very useful. They save us plenty of time and improve the efficiency," said Wang Xinyu, a lobby manager at a budget hotel in Beijing. Open since January, the hotel operates three robots across six floors and 372 rooms. Wang said that more than half the guests order takeaway during mealtimes — and that last stretch, from front desk to door, is where the robots step in. A robot delivers takeout to a guest's room at a hotel in Shanghai on Feb 18. WANG LUXIAN/FOR CHINA DAILY When an order lands, the front desk tucks the food into the robot's compartment and punches in the room number. From there, the robot owns it — it hails the elevator, rolls to the door and pings the guest to come grab it. Between rushes, the machines remain parked in corners, charging their batteries. Autoxing Technology Co, the company that makes the robots, was founded in 2020 with ambitions to develop autonomous-driving technology for cars. But the bet proved expensive, prompting the company to narrow its focus. Two years later, it launched its hotel robots. The technology behind them is largely the same, enabling machines to move from one place to another without bumping into any obstacles. "The rapid development of autonomous-driving in China has, to some extent, boosted other robotic applications," said Yang Tianyun, a marketing manager at Autoxing. About 60 percent of Autoxing's business now comes from exports, although differences in regulations across countries can slow deployment. This helps explain why the robots can surprise foreign visitors like Goenaga. "We had never seen anything like that anywhere else in the world," Goenaga said. "I think a lot of people are not aware of how advanced the technology is here." As a designer, Goenaga also likes the robots' cute look. They do not need to look human, he said, adding that a friendly, approachable design is more fitting for hotels, where they interact with families and children. body: Beijing Xiangshan Forum brings people together for dialogue - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Military Home China Military Beijing Xiangshan Forum brings people together for dialogue chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-09-11 14:05 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Over the past 20 years, the Beijing Xiangshan Forum has expanded its international role, bringing together defense officials, experts and scholars from around the world for dialogue, according to Jean Christophe Baron von Pfetten, chairman of the UK's Royal Institute for East West Strategic Studies. He said the forum's unique value lies in bringing together people who rarely have the opportunity to meet. Recalling discussions among representatives from Ukraine, Russia and NATO at the 12th forum, he noted that China can provide an important platform for Track 1.5 and Track 2 dialogues. body: China launches AI-powered geological mapping and mineral exploration systems - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Innovation Home China Innovation China launches AI-powered geological mapping and mineral exploration systems By Li Menghan | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-09-11 14:55 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE China unveiled two geological mapping and mineral exploration systems powered by artificial intelligence technologies on Friday, marking a shift from decades of expert-driven fieldwork to more accurate, comprehensive, and efficient data-and-algorithm-based predictions. The two systems — AI-GeoMapping and AI-OreSeeking — were released by the China Geological Survey of the Ministry of Natural Resources at the 28th China Mining Conference and Exhibition in Tianjin, as the country pushes to secure critical mineral supplies. Geological mapping serves as a road map for the subsurface mineral realm, revealing how strata, structures, and rocks are distributed. It is the most fundamental and critical prerequisite work for discovering mineralization clues and delineating prospecting target areas, according to Li Fengdan, an official with the China Geological Survey who is responsible for AI-GeoMapping. After a decade of development work, the system has evolved from breakthroughs in core AI algorithms and specialized software platforms to a full-process intelligent ecosystem, Li added. Li said that the system addresses long-standing field challenges, such as inaccessible rugged terrain, limited rock exposure under forest, swamp, or desert cover, and the complexities of identifying geological units across extensive survey areas. "It identifies geological features with 90 percent accuracy and lifts data processing efficiency by more than half compared with conventional methods," Li said, noting that the system fuses satellite imagery, airborne geophysical surveys, and ground observations through AI. The research team overcame key technical hurdles, including AI-driven geological object recognition based on field route deep learning, as well as multimodal fusion of geological, geophysical, geochemical, and remote sensing data. The system has been tested on nearly 100 regional geological survey sheets at a 1:50,000 scale in places such as Yunnan, Anhui, and Qinghai provinces, and has been promoted to countries like Morocco, Laos, and Rwanda. "With multi-language support built in, the system will offer a Chinese solution for AI-powered geological surveying that can benefit the global community," Li added. Where mapping reveals the geological picture, AI-OreSeeking goes further — integrating not just mapped geological data, but also geophysical, geochemical, and remote sensing datasets to predict where mineral deposits may lie. Wang Bin, an official with the China Geological Survey who is responsible for the prospecting system, said the system was developed over three years to meet the demand for rapid prediction and evaluation of mineral resources. He likened the platform to an "intelligent brain" — a unified system that consolidates what was once a fragmented workflow spread across various stand-alone software packages. The platform comprises five core modules and more than 200 algorithms, covering the full chain from data management and interpretation through predictive evaluation, map production and report generation. It is built around a large prospecting model combined with knowledge graph constraints, fusing millions of geological knowledge entries to ensure predictions conform to established mineralization principles. With each drill hole costing millions of yuan, Wang said the system can effectively narrow down favorable exploration targets before expensive field verification, reducing the cost of blind field exploration. "It shifts mineral exploration from expert experience-driven to data- and knowledge-driven prediction, opening a new chapter in intelligent mineral exploration," Wang added. In trial runs across the Qinling Mountains, Jiaodong Peninsula, and Wuyi Mountains metallogenic belts, the system delineated a series of gold, copper, iron, and lead-zinc exploration targets. Taking the Zhaishang-Liba mining district in the West Qinling as an example, the system completed data processing and prediction for 32 survey sheets at a 1:50,000 scale in just five days, newly delineating two exploration targets that were subsequently verified by drilling — work that would typically take months using traditional methods. Wang said that trial applications across more than 100 projects in over 10 provincial-level regions have shown that the system can capture weak mineralization-related anomalies that are difficult for humans to detect, identifying new favorable exploration targets. "The overall efficiency has improved by more than 60 percent, pushing mineral exploration toward being comprehensive, fast, and precise," he said, highlighting its particular value for deep mineral exploration. The two systems come as China steps up efforts to apply AI to its new round of strategic mineral exploration, a campaign led by the Ministry of Natural Resources aimed at securing breakthroughs in domestic reserves of gold, copper, lithium, and other critical minerals. The goal is to identify a new batch of developable mineral sites by 2030 to ensure steady reserve growth at home and strengthen national energy and resource security. body: Interpol chief praises China's role in combating transnational fraud - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Society Home China Society Interpol chief praises China's role in combating transnational fraud By YANG ZEKUN in Lianyungang, Jiangsu | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-09-11 14:13 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Interpol Secretary General Valdecy Urquiza has called for stronger multilateral cooperation and coordination among law enforcement agencies as fraud, cybercrime, and other forms of transnational crime grow in scale and complexity. Speaking during the Global Public Security Cooperation Forum in Lianyungang, Jiangsu province, which ran from Sept 8 to 10, Urquiza said one defining feature of major crimes today is their increasingly transnational nature, with victims often located in one country while those behind the crimes operate from another. He highlighted China's role in international law enforcement cooperation, describing the country as a strong supporter and partner of Interpol, particularly in the fight against fraud. In recent years, China and Interpol have cooperated on capacity building and operations targeting fraud-related crime. Urquiza cited "Operation First Light" as one example, saying related efforts had led to the arrest of more than 11,000 suspects and the identification or seizure of more than $600 million linked to fraudulent activities. He also welcomed the establishment of the International Alliance Combating Telecom and Cyber Fraud, launched during the forum with the participation of 46 countries. Initiated by China, the alliance is designed to strengthen international coordination against cross-border telecom and cyber fraud. Urquiza said telecom and cyber fraud have become a major priority for Interpol member countries. From 2024 to 2025, the use of relevant Interpol tools and databases by member countries increased by 55 percent, reflecting the growing scale and complexity of such crimes. Such threats cannot be effectively tackled by any one country alone, he said, adding that countries need to pool resources, uphold multilateralism and coordinate their responses. Urquiza said initiatives such as the new alliance are therefore particularly important because fighting online fraud requires collaboration, coordinated action, and sustained multilateral cooperation. Urquiza also spoke highly of the Global Public Security Cooperation Forum, saying it provides an important platform for countries to exchange experience, share law enforcement practices, discuss emerging security threats, and develop joint responses. Interpol has actively participated in the forum. Urquiza said the organization would take the outcomes of the discussions back to its headquarters and use them to better tailor its capabilities and services to member countries. Having attended the forum several times, he said it had given him valuable insights into evolving threats in different parts of the world. Urquiza also stressed the importance of law enforcement capacity building for developing countries as criminal methods evolve rapidly. As the first Interpol secretary general from the Global South, Urquiza said countries need to strengthen professional training and make better use of new technologies as criminal methods evolve rapidly. Interpol's diversity, he added, helps it understand different regional challenges while bringing together expertise toward the common goal of fighting crime. The Interpol Global Academy Network is part of that effort. Urquiza said not all police agencies have equal access to technology, training and other resources, and the network seeks to bridge that gap by connecting police academies and law enforcement training institutions worldwide. The People's Public Security University of China joined the network last year. Urquiza said the partnership allows officers from other regions to benefit from the experience of Chinese law enforcement agencies and strengthen their professional capabilities. "We are very proud of this partnership," he said. More than 2,100 representatives from 139 countries, regions, and international organizations attended this year's forum. Andy Tsang Wai-hung, chair of the forum, said its international reach and influence have continued to grow over the past five years and that it has played an increasingly important role in building consensus and promoting practical cooperation. He described the launch of the anti-fraud alliance as one of the most significant outcomes of this year's gathering. Tsang said nontraditional security challenges — including telecom and cyber fraud, terrorism, drug crime, tourism safety, and cybersecurity — are increasingly crossing borders and interacting with one another, making dialogue and cooperation essential. The forum also released the 2026 Global Public Safety Index, whose research coverage expanded from 50 countries last year to 62 this year. The countries covered account for 82.73 percent of the world's population, 75.22 percent of its land area, and 87.47 percent of global GDP. The average score among the 62 countries stood at 72.56, slightly higher than last year. The report also found more positive public perceptions of international cooperation on public security, while drug crime, terrorism, cybercrime, and risks associated with artificial intelligence remained prominent challenges. Tsang said the forum will continue to promote policy coordination, information sharing, and joint action, while encouraging greater participation by developing countries and wider use of technology in public security governance. body: China offers new-tech preview in Berlin - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS LIFESTYLE CULTURE TRAVEL WATCHTHIS SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL FORUM NEWSPAPER MOBILE Home Business Technology Home / Business / Technology China offers new-tech preview in Berlin AI-powered appliances and hardware innovations cater to customer needs and provide companions By Julian Shea and Zheng Wanyin in Berlin | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-09-12 04:21 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE About 220,000 visitors and 2,000 exhibitors attended IFA, the world’s largest consumer electronics, home appliances, and future tech event, in Berlin this year. [Zheng Wanyin / China Daily] Representatives from leading technology companies gathered in Berlin last weekend for IFA, the world's largest consumer electronics, home appliances, and future tech event, with companies showcasing their latest products and innovations, and a large number of Chinese brands and manufacturers on display. The IFA stands for Innovation For All, and the event has been taking place for more than a century. German broadcaster rbb24 reported that 928 companies from the Chinese mainland took part, and a further 84 from Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. One of the most prominent Chinese brands at IFA this year was Haier, which has been the world's market leader for major home appliances, based on sales volume, for 17 years in a row. The company kicked off IFA 2026 in spectacular fashion by revealing it has signed up to become an official partner of the UEFA Champions League, one of the most watched soccer tournaments on the planet. The company's technology on display was similarly eye-catching, with much of it incorporating artificial intelligence, or AI. People play video games at Haier’s exhibition stand in Berlin at this year’s IFA show. [Provided to China Daily] Haier's latest smart fridge keeps an electronic eye on what food is inside and its state of freshness, even suggesting recipes to reduce food waste. Its revolutionary four-drum washing machine design, which transforms the shape, size, and function of the standard appliance, also drew admiring glances. Away from traditional core products, another piece of Haier hardware attracting attention was a wearable exoskeleton that can be strapped to the body, to help people with mobility issues to walk. Haier Europe's CEO Neil Tunstall told China Daily that AI was at the forefront of what the company was doing. "AI really is a massive change for home appliances. Instead of doing what you tell it, it can suggest things," he said. "AI is becoming more proactive, more than just reactive." He is equally proud of his hardware innovations, citing the four-drum washing machine design and wearable exoskeleton as key examples. "We've listened to consumers and we're creating new things — it's not all about AI, but it's also about physical products. "From being dumb things you switch on/switch off, we've moved to connectivity ... so, we're talking about things working together, an ecosystem rather than as individual products." These innovations, he added, were just a taster of where technology will go next. Visitors to IFA Berlin try Hisense ConnectLife, which is a unified smart home platform that links home appliances across all Hisense brands, simplifying daily tasks. [Provided to China Daily] Another world-famous Chinese brand taking part in IFA this year was Hisense, which unveiled its AI Companion Suite, a product range including refrigerators, ovens, wine cabinets, and washing machines. Bostjan Pecnik, vice-president of Hisense Europe, said the latest developments mean the home appliance industry "is at a turning point, with products evolving from devices that respond to commands into companions that proactively support users". "Hisense is helping lead this shift through both the underlying technology and solutions tailored to everyday life," Pecnik said. Chinese technology company Xiaomi displays its latest model of electric car. [Photo / IFA Berlin] Other Chinese exhibitors at the Berlin fair included TCL, Ecovacs, and Xiaomi, along with drone company DJI, which showed off a range of products, from pocket-sized devices to heavyweight agriculture-specific units. "New products, including the Osmo 360 II, Romo 2 Series, Osmo Pocket 4P, and Mic Mini 2S are expected to be highly well-received by the market because each uniquely elevates a different area of our users' daily lives," said a DJI representative. "The smaller devices offer high-definition video and crystal-clear audio from something that is pocket-sized, and items like the Romo 2 Series use drone perception and mechatronics to make household cleaning hands-free and worry-free." A child experiences a drone product at the Insta360 booth during IFA Berlin in Berlin, Germany on Sept 5. [Zhang Haofu / Xinhua] Eliane Fiolet, co-founder and editor of consumer technology news website Ubergizmo.com, has covered IFA for more than 10 years. She told China Daily the scale of Chinese participation at this year's event reflected the country's leading place in markets including household robots. "I am impressed by what Chinese companies are able to achieve in terms of quality, professionalism, and design excellence," she said. "I have seen the evolution. Five years ago, Chinese companies were (already) very present in consumer electronics. Ten years ago, a bit less, but now the dominance is really obvious." Another industry pundit, Chris Pereira, founder and CEO of iMpact, a New York-headquartered communications and business consulting company, said Chinese brands were "noticeably more confident" at IFA this year, and had taken on local representatives to sell more than just their hardware. "They've hired local European teams to represent them locally," he observed. "They're working with local partners to really tell a brand story and not just sell products ... they'll tell you about their mission, values, and what they're contributing to, helping in the local markets in Europe." Pereira said this was a wise approach to take, encouraging a more positive attitude on both sides. "A common discussion this year is how we can build a new level of relationship, not just business-wise, but also in terms of human-to-human trust," he added. A visitor simulates a boxing match with a robot made by Chinese company Engine AI at this year’s IFA show in Berlin. body: China firmly against US espionage activities - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Business Macro Companies Industries Technology Motoring China Data Finance Top 10 Home / Business / Policies Home Business Policies China firmly against US espionage activities By ZHONG NAN | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-12 09:43 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE China has the firm resolve and sufficient means to take necessary measures against the United States' espionage activities targeting China and Chinese companies in accordance with the Counter-Espionage Law and other regulations, the Ministry of Commerce said on Friday. The remarks came after a senior official from the Central Intelligence Agency reportedly said the US was conducting broader espionage activities against China to counter what Washington described as military and economic threats, with Chinese companies in sectors including artificial intelligence, semiconductors and biotechnology considered "legitimate intelligence targets". A Commerce Ministry spokesperson said the US remarks openly exposed its intention to use espionage activities against Chinese firms and reflected a continued expansion of the concept of national security into normal economic and commercial competition. Economic competition is a normal part of commercial activity, and technological advantages are built through innovation, talent and sustained investment. Interference by US intelligence agencies would disrupt normal business activities, undermine corporate confidence and damage a fair global market environment, said the spokesperson in an online statement. According to the information released by the Ministry of Commerce, the US has long accused other countries of using spying activities to harm US commercial interests, yet now seeks to portray its own espionage targeting economic competitors as legitimate. The commerce official stressed China's advances in AI, semiconductors, biotechnology and other fields are the result of sustained efforts by Chinese researchers and companies, rather than grounds for foreign intelligence operations. The spokesperson warned the US to immediately stop espionage activities targeting China, including Chinese companies, and cease all actions that harm China's sovereignty, security and development interests. zhongnan@chinadaily.com.cn Photo Pop Land City Carnival Tour arrives in Shanghai Gansu's traditional medicine industry embraces tech and global markets China International Big Data Industry Expo showcases data achievements in Guiyang World Humanoid Robot Games open in Beijing Tourists shop for Taiwan goods in Fujian The 'Vibrant China' media tour in Hunan: Changsha blends history with creativity Most Viewed in 24 Hours State Council News Policies concerning expats, foreign enterprises in August 2026 A look at China's economy in H1 of 2026 Top 10 Top 10 countries attracting Chinese tourists Business focus Manufacturing edge a win-win multiplier abroad 'New new three' power China's trade China Data China's CPI up 0.8% in August SOEs SOEs return more profits to State China's central SOEs invest 1.1t yuan in Xinjiang during 14th Five-Year Plan period Special 2026 CIFTIS China International Supply Chain Expo Top BACK TO THE TOP English 中文 HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Copyright 1994 - . body: China sets 2030 targets for smart, connected NEVs - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Business Macro Companies Industries Technology Motoring China Data Finance Top 10 Home / Business / Motoring Home Business Motoring China sets 2030 targets for smart, connected NEVs By Li Fusheng | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-09-11 10:51 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE A man experiences a new energy vehicle at a car dealership in Tengzhou city, East China's Shandong province, April 10, 2026. [Photo/Xinhua] China has unveiled a plan to further strengthen its advantages across the industrial chain of smart, connected new energy vehicles, with the country aiming to join the ranks of the world's leading automotive powers by 2030. By then, new energy passenger vehicles are expected to account for 70 percent of new vehicle sales in their segment in the domestic market, while the share for commercial vehicles is targeted at 40 percent, according to the plan released by nine ministries on Friday. The plan also calls for the large-scale application of vehicles equipped with automated driving functions, with highly automated driving expected to be available on highways, urban expressways and some urban roads. China aims to make further progress in key automotive technologies by 2030. The average fuel consumption of passenger vehicles is targeted at 3.3 liters per 100 kilometers, while the average electricity consumption of battery electric passenger vehicles is expected to fall to around 11.5 kilowatt-hours per 100 km. The industry is also expected to become more digitalized and intelligent, with labor productivity targeted to rise 15 percent from 2025 levels. The plan calls for the development of several vehicle manufacturers ranking among the world's top 10 by sales and auto parts suppliers entering the global top 100. It also seeks to promote a new phase of internationalization for China's auto industry, with companies expected to strengthen their global operating capabilities and Chinese automotive brands to build stronger reputations overseas. China's influence in the formulation of international automotive standards and regulations is also expected to increase. The plan further emphasizes the industry's economic and environmental contributions. The automotive sector is expected to reinforce its role as a pillar of the national economy, while achieving carbon peaking before 2030 and accelerating the green and low-carbon transformation of the automotive supply chain. On autonomous driving, the plan sets an ambitious safety target, saying the safety performance of vehicles equipped with automated driving systems should be significantly better than that of human-driven vehicles. [Photo/Xinhua] With a spotlight on him, a Chinese actor slowly descended from the stage and made his way through the aisles of a packed Cairo theater, delivering an anguished soliloquy amid warm applause. It was one of several moments when performers of Liaozhai: Purple Tail, an experimental Chinese Xiju opera production, moved beyond the stage and into the audience during their performance at the 33rd Cairo International Festival for Experimental Theatre. The Chinese production, presented by Wuxi Xiju Theatre, brought to life a story weaving together the human and supernatural worlds. body: Filmmaking promotes connection in Serbia - Chinadaily.com.cn WS6aa4be00e4b06d4aa055db02 China Edition | Global Edition | ASIA | 中文 China Latest Society Innovation Education Cross-Strait HK/Macao Health Environment Military Video World Asia-Pacific Americas Europe Middle East Africa Business Policies Companies Industries Technology China Up-close China Data Motoring Video Culture Art Music and Theater Film and TV Books Heritage Events and Festivals People Cultural Exchange Video Photo Gallery Fashion Health Travel News City Tours Guides and Tips My Footprints Around the World Features Photo Video Food Sports Soccer Basketball Volleyball Tennis Golf Track and field Swimming Motor China Stars Opinion Cartoons Editorials Global Lens We Comment Columnists Global Views Chinese Perspectives Opinion Line Regional Newspaper China Daily PDF China Daily E-Paper China Daily Global PDF China Daily Global E-Paper Mobile CULTURE News Heritage Art Film Theater Fashion Cultural Exchange Books Photo Video HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE 中文 CULTURE News Heritage Art Film Theater Fashion Cultural Exchange Books Photo Video Home / Culture / Film and TV Filmmaking promotes connection in Serbia Xinhua | Updated: 2026-09-12 10:50 Share - WeChat More than an hour before the launch ceremony for the Chinese Cinema screening event in the Serbian capital began last week, the Chinese Cultural Center, which seats about 150 people, was already packed. Serbian and Chinese filmmakers, officials, local Chinese culture enthusiasts, and film lovers from China and Serbia gathered for the launch ceremony. The event brought Chinese films to Serbian audiences and created opportunities for filmmakers from both countries to meet and exchange. For Chinese director Song Wen, however, the event meant more than the launch of a film program. Long before becoming a filmmaker, Song was a teenager captivated by cinema. One film that left a particularly deep impression on him was The Bridge, a Yugoslav classic that became familiar to generations of Chinese viewers. "I was fascinated by films when I was in middle school," Song recalls. "At that time, The Bridge was frequently shown on television. It was one of the films that had a particularly deep influence on me in my early years," Song adds. Decades later, Song came to Serbia not only to bring Chinese films to local audiences, but also to discover what a new generation of Serbian filmmakers has been creating. Zhang Zhe, charge d'affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Serbia, says Yugoslav classics such as The Bridge and Walter Defends Sarajevo are household film titles in China. Film, he says, is one of the most direct and vivid forms of cultural expression, a language that can cross borders and connect people from different nations. The launch of Chinese Cinema, he says, has built another "bridge of light and shadow" between the peoples of China and Serbia. Zhang Songwen, one of China's best-known actors, describes film as "an invisible road" that allows stories to travel through time and people's eyes to reach distant places. The opening of Chinese Cinema, the actor says, was not merely the establishment of a screening space, but also a window through which Serbian friends can learn about China. He hopes more Chinese films will be shown in Serbia, and that more Serbian films will reach Chinese audiences. The event concluded with a screening of Xie Fei's A Mongolian Tale, a 1995 film that tells a story of love, identity and life on the Inner Mongolian grasslands. Dragoljub Bajic, acting director of the National Theater in Belgrade, made the exchange event more tangible when he performed the famous song, Beautiful Night, with a distinct Serbian touch. The exchange continued beyond the screen. Song and other Chinese filmmakers traveled to Serbia's western city of Zlatibor to attend the second National Film and Television Festival, known as NAFFIT, last week. They also donated audiovisual materials to the Yugoslav Film Archive on Monday. "I hope to discover works by young Serbian students and young directors at the festival," Song says. "I would like to bring these works back to China, so that Chinese audiences can learn what young people in Serbia are interested in," Song adds. Miroljub Stojanovic, editor of publishing activities for the Film Center Serbia, says he looks forward to deeper exchanges and dialogue between the two sides, believing the visit would open broader space for cooperation in cinema. A Yugoslav film once opened a door into the world of cinema for a generation of young Chinese filmmakers, including Song. Decades later, Chinese films appear on Serbian screens, while Chinese filmmakers look for new Serbian stories to carry home. The bridge is now becoming a two-way exchange, with filmmakers, works and stories crossing borders in both directions. Highlights include a floor screen (top) dating to the 15th or 16th century and depicting a gathering of scholars. [Photo provided to China Daily] The extravagant lifestyle of the Jia family in the great 18th-century novel Dream of the Red Chamber comes vividly to life in its descriptions of feasting, dressing, travel, and domestic spaces. One chapter recounts the lavish gifts presented for the 80th birthday of Granny Jia, the family's emotional anchor and center of power. Among them is a 12-panel folding screen of exceptional craftsmanship, decorated with pictorial designs created using the costly kesi (cut-silk) tapestry technique. Granny Jia orders that the screen be carefully stored and not moved. When reading the novel, one can only imagine what such a screen might have looked like. Granny Jia calls it "of the finest quality". Today, visitors to the Tsinghua University Art Museum in Beijing can see a screen of a similar size and comparable magnificence. 1 2 3 4 5 6 Next >>| 1/6 Next Related Stories Lost painted sculptures donated by Taiwan group go on display in Shanxi A picture paints a thousand words Casting a lasting shadow Jade craftsmanship helps carve out more opportunities Showcasing a dynamic era Photo Gallery A rally of friendship A photographer's lifetime dedication to Huangshan Mountain College artists shine at National Fine Arts Exhibition in Beijing Tales and Trails Qingdao 'city drink': Brewing coastal charm China Vibes Bund lights beckon thousands daily in Shanghai 24 Solar Terms End of Heat Editor's Pick Serving up emotions: A chat with director Wen Muye A toast to tradition and innovation Video Mid-Autumn Festival brings nostalgia back to mooncakes Hotel robots surprise visitors, streamline operations Most Viewed in 24 Hours Chinaculture.org Five great Chinese love legends: Romance across millennia The Silk Road: a facilitator of cultural convergence Copyright 1994 - .
