Wang Yi said that under the leadership and guidance of the two heads of state, the two sides are working to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. It has been proven that improving and developing China-U.S. relations, coexisting peacefully on the basis of mutual respect, and then achieving win-win cooperation serve the fundamental interests of the two peoples and meet the common expectations of the international community. At the same time, China-U.S. relations still face various risks and challenges. The two sides should implement the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state, focus on a positive agenda, properly manage differences, remove disruptions and overcome obstacles for high-level exchanges, and promote the steady, healthy and sustainable development of China-U.S. relations. David Perdue said that the two heads of state have provided important strategic guidance for U.S.-China relations. President Donald J. Trump’s visit to China in May was very successful. Both sides are willing to strengthen communication, advance cooperation, prepare well for the next phase of important high-level interactions, and build a constructive U.S.-China relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect and reciprocity. David Perdue also expressed, on behalf of the U.S. side, condolences over the casualties caused by the mudslide disaster affecting Gyirong Port in Xizang.

body: Eight Points of Outcomes and Consensus for the 25th Round of Talks Between Special Representatives of China and India on the Boundary Question_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China IPC Visas English EN 简体中文 Français Español Русский عربي HOME THE MINISTRY Main Responsibilities The Minister Principal Officials Departments Related Agencies NEWS Top Stories Speeches Diplomatic Schedule New Ambassadors MFA News Spokesperson’s Remarks News from Overseas Missions RESOURCES Communiqués Foreign Policies In Focus Diplomatic History Diplomatic Figures Protocol Affairs Map of China OVERSEAS MISSIONS Chinese Embassies Chinese Consulates General Chinese Missions to International Organizations and Representative Offices Abroad COUNTRIES AND REGIONS Asia Africa Europe North America South America Oceania ABOUT CHINA Home Minister’s Activities Eight Points of Outcomes and Consensus for the 25th Round of Talks Between Special Representatives of China and India on the Boundary Question Updated: August 26, 2026 23:31 On August 25, 2026, the 25th Round of Talks Between the Special Representatives (SR) of China and India on the Boundary Question was held in Beijing, China. H.E.Wang Yi, Special Representative of China, Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, and H.E. Ajit Doval, Special Representative of India and National Security Advisor, had a candid and in-depth exchange of views on the China-India boundary question and reached eight points of outcomes and consensus as follows: 1.The two sides reaffirmed their commitment to uphold the guidance received from the leaders of the two countries, maintain peace and tranquility in the border areas and create an atmosphere for healthy and steady development of bilateral relations. 2.The two sides underlined their commitment to advancing negotiations on a framework for the settlement of the boundary question in accordance with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the China-India Boundary Question signed in 2005 and the consensus reached in subsequent SR talks, in pursuit of a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution. 3.The Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation and Working Group on Border Management under the WMCC would respectively advance discussions on an Early and Substantial Harvest of boundary delimitation and Border Management. The first task for both these groups would be to agree on their respective Terms of Reference. 4.The two sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander-level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC. The two sides discussed ways to improve understanding of the LAC in appropriate areas for better border management. 5.With the objective to improve the border management measures, an additional two meeting points were agreed for holding the General Level Mechanism/Senior Highest Military Commander meeting(SHMC). Similarly two additional channels of border military hotline in the Eastern and Middle Sectors were agreed. 6.Both sides noted the progress on trans-border cooperation. The Indian side appreciated the efforts made by the Chinese side to increase the number of batches of Indian official pilgrimage to Mount Gang Renpoche and Lake Mapam Yun Tso in Xizang Autonomous Region of China. Both sides appreciated the reopening of the three designated border trading points. The two sides agreed to strengthen exchanges and cooperation in border trade, pilgrimage and other areas, with the view of working together to create an atmosphere featuring dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation in the border areas. 7.The two sides agreed to hold the next meeting of the China-India Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers in September and maintain communication on issues including hydrological data sharing, and renewal of relevant MoUs. 8. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th Round of SR Talks in India in 2027.
title: Eight Points of Outcomes and Consensus for the 25th Round of Talks Between Special Representatives of China and India on the Boundary Question

body: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 11, 2026_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China IPC Visas English EN 简体中文 Français Español Русский عربي HOME THE MINISTRY Main Responsibilities The Minister Principal Officials Departments Related Agencies NEWS Top Stories Speeches Diplomatic Schedule New Ambassadors MFA News Spokesperson’s Remarks News from Overseas Missions RESOURCES Communiqués Foreign Policies In Focus Diplomatic History Diplomatic Figures Protocol Affairs Map of China OVERSEAS MISSIONS Chinese Embassies Chinese Consulates General Chinese Missions to International Organizations and Representative Offices Abroad COUNTRIES AND REGIONS Asia Africa Europe North America South America Oceania ABOUT CHINA Home News Spokesperson’s Remarks Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 11, 2026 Updated: September 11, 2026 19:26 People’s Daily: The Chinese side has announced that President Xi Jinping will attend the 18th BRICS Summit. Could you share China’s expectations for this event? Mao Ning: BRICS is the key platform for solidarity and cooperation among emerging markets and developing countries. Guided by the BRICS Spirit of openness, inclusiveness and win-win cooperation, BRICS countries have been committed to upholding multilateralism, defending fairness and justice, and pursuing common development ever since the grouping was formed. Today, BRICS has grown into a real force standing at the forefront of the Global South. China sets great store by and actively participates in BRICS cooperation. President Xi will attend and address the upcoming summit, have in-depth exchanges with other leaders on major issues including the current international situation, the development of BRICS mechanisms, and deepening practical cooperation, and put forward China’s important initiatives and propositions, charting the course for the high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation. China is ready to work with fellow BRICS countries for steady and sustained progress in greater BRICS cooperation to contribute to building a community with a shared future for humanity. AFP: U.S. artificial intelligence firm Anthropic said in a report yesterday that it has shut down multiple operations that are believed to be linked to the Chinese government. The report said that the actors were using its chatbot Claude to gather information on various targets, including overseas religious communities, Uyghurs in Syria and Chinese diaspora groups. Does the foreign ministry have any comment on this? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with the specifics. China advocates AI for good. We firmly oppose attempts to throw mud at China by distorting facts. Shenzhen TV: According to WIPO’s latest Global Innovation Index, China leads the innovation cluster count for a fourth consecutive year with 25 top 100 innovation clusters. Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou tops the global rankings for a second consecutive year. Some say innovation has become a major driver of China’s development and the world should recognize the dividends and opportunities generated by China’s innovation. What’s your comment? Mao Ning: I noticed the announced rankings. Innovation is key to China’s sustained economic performance and soaring industrial competitiveness. Chinese innovation creates opportunities for all countries. More and more foreign firms choose to do R&D and innovate in China and excel in global competition by tapping into China’s mega-market. For China, innovation is never about monopoly. We are committed to sharing innovation dividends with the world to thrive together. The Hindu: Another question on President Xi’s visit to India for the BRICS Summit. This will also be the first meeting between President Xi and Prime Minister Modi since Tianjin last year. What are China’s expectations for this meeting between the two leaders and what role does Beijing see this meeting between the leaders is having on the ongoing normalization in relations? Mao Ning: China and India are arranging for the bilateral meeting between President Xi and Prime Minister Modi. This will be the third year in a row for the two leaders to meet with each other, following their meetings in Kazan and Tianjin. China will work with India to act on the strategic guidance of the two leaders, handle the bilateral relations from a strategic height and long-term perspective, step up communication, enhance cooperation, properly handle differences, and be friends enjoying good-neighborliness and partners helping each other succeed. PTI: Can you please share some details about President Xi’s delegation? How many members? There are reports that it is quite a large delegation, especially quite a number of heads of businesses are going to attend the BRICS Business Forum. Second question, this BRICS Summit is a bit different, as it is taking place amid two bitter conflicts, one in the Middle East and another is the Ukraine-Russia conflict. To stretch further, can you elaborate more on what China’s expectations as well as China’s priorities are as far as this particular BRICS Summit in Delhi? Mao Ning: On your first question, there will be timely updates on President Xi Jinping’s trip to India for the BRICS Summit. On your second question, China advocates a common, comprehensive, cooperative, and sustainable approach to security. We are committed to promoting the political settlement of hotspot issues through dialogue. We look forward to working with fellow BRICS countries to promote dialogue and negotiation to resolve differences and jointly safeguard regional and global peace and stability. Reuters: The Taiwanese official Hsiao Bi-khim is in Italy. Does China have a response to this? Mao Ning: China has lodged serious protests with Italy and the EU side on the “Taiwan independence” politicians’ attendance at the conference in Italy. The DPP authorities and individual politicians from Taiwan are making every attempt to grab attention and solicit external support for their separatist agenda under the pretext of “democracy” and “freedom.” Their moves are truly despicable and simply futile. Let me reiterate that there is but one China in the world, and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory. China firmly opposes official interactions of any form between China’s Taiwan region and countries having diplomatic ties with China. The one-China principle is a widely-recognized norm in international relations and a prevailing international consensus. It is also the political foundation of China-Italy relations and China-EU relations. We urge relevant parties to honor the one-China principle with real action. CCTV: We noted that individual politicians from the U.S. and other Western countries have repeatedly expressed so-called “concern” over the “Hong Kong Alliance” case. Today, a Hong Kong court announced the sentence regarding the case. What is your comment? Mao Ning: China has made clear its just position on the “Hong Kong Alliance” case. The rule of law is upheld in Hong Kong. The central government firmly supports the Hong Kong SAR in lawfully safeguarding national security and fighting activities endangering national security. Relevant parties need to earnestly respect China’s sovereignty and the rule of law in Hong Kong, stop making irresponsible remarks on the SAR’s handling of judicial cases, and stop interfering in Hong Kong’s judicial affairs, which are China’s internal affairs, in any form. Kyodo News: Could you please comment on China’s announcement to increase visa fees for Japanese citizens travelling to China? Mao Ning: The Chinese Embassy in Japan has issued a notice. The adjustment was made based on the principle of reciprocity. Reuters: The Kremlin’s Aide Yuri Ushakov said on Tuesday that the three heads of state of China, the U.S. and Russia may hold a trilateral meeting at the next APEC Forum in November. Can China confirm or comment on this
title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 11, 2026 September 11, 2026

body: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 10, 2026_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China IPC Visas English EN 简体中文 Français Español Русский عربي HOME THE MINISTRY Main Responsibilities The Minister Principal Officials Departments Related Agencies NEWS Top Stories Speeches Diplomatic Schedule New Ambassadors MFA News Spokesperson’s Remarks News from Overseas Missions RESOURCES Communiqués Foreign Policies In Focus Diplomatic History Diplomatic Figures Protocol Affairs Map of China OVERSEAS MISSIONS Chinese Embassies Chinese Consulates General Chinese Missions to International Organizations and Representative Offices Abroad COUNTRIES AND REGIONS Asia Africa Europe North America South America Oceania ABOUT CHINA Home News Spokesperson’s Remarks Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 10, 2026 Updated: September 10, 2026 17:46 AFP: Will Chinese leader travel to India this weekend for the BRICS Summit? Guo Jiakun: On this question, I have no information to share at the moment. Reuters: India’s Serious Fraud Office has recommended that China’s Xiaomi be investigated for alleged irregularities in its business model and compliance with foreign investment law. Does the foreign ministry have any comment on that? Guo Jiakun: I’m not familiar with the specifics. China-India economic and trade cooperation is mutually beneficial in nature. We hope India will provide a fair, just, transparent and non-discriminatory environment for the investment and operation of companies of all countries in India. NBC: At his meeting with the U.S. Ambassador David Perdue the other week, Foreign Minister Wang Yi urged both sides to “eliminate interference and overcome obstacles” for high-level engagements between the two countries. Is there any example of “obstacle” that the Chinese side believes is within the U.S. ability to tackle or otherwise, in general, are both sides, from their most recent communications, making some progress in dealing with these “obstacles”? Guo Jiakun: China released a readout on Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s meeting with U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue. Head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance to bilateral relations. China and the U.S. are in communication regarding interactions between the two heads of state within the year. Global Times: It is reported that in a media briefing, the U.S. embassy in Panama introduced a pilot AI supply chain credentialing and provenance platform in Panama, the first of its kind in the world. The U.S. said the project was under evaluation. Some media commented that by verifying the origin, custody, and compliance status of cargo for AI infrastructure, semiconductors, and critical minerals, the project in essence serves the U.S. control of tech industrial and supply chains and tech blockade of China. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: We noticed relevant reports. The development of AI bears on the common welfare of all humanity. All parties should jointly promote the open and inclusive development of AI for good and for all. Exclusive groupings and geopolitical calculations are not conducive to technological development and progress in LAC countries and the rest of the Global South. China will work with LAC countries and other parties to jointly build a just and equitable global AI governance system, and develop AI for the good of people worldwide. Reuters: Nepal is planning to ask wealthier countries and agencies for financial help this week. It has said that they should contribute to the US$5 billion that’s needed for the rebuilding following the flooding. Has Nepal asked China for financial help and does China have any plans to contribute? Guo Jiakun: After the sudden mudslide struck the China-Nepal border areas, while urgently carrying out rescue and relief efforts at home, China immediately reached out to Nepal to support its emergency response and disaster relief. China and Nepal are traditional friends and close neighbors. We stand ready to assist Nepal in post-disaster reconstruction to the best of our capability based on its needs. We believe the Nepali people will overcome difficulties and rebuild their homes soon under the leadership of their government.
title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 10, 2026

body: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 9, 2026_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China IPC Visas English EN 简体中文 Français Español Русский عربي HOME THE MINISTRY Main Responsibilities The Minister Principal Officials Departments Related Agencies NEWS Top Stories Speeches Diplomatic Schedule New Ambassadors MFA News Spokesperson’s Remarks News from Overseas Missions RESOURCES Communiqués Foreign Policies In Focus Diplomatic History Diplomatic Figures Protocol Affairs Map of China OVERSEAS MISSIONS Chinese Embassies Chinese Consulates General Chinese Missions to International Organizations and Representative Offices Abroad COUNTRIES AND REGIONS Asia Africa Europe North America South America Oceania ABOUT CHINA Home News Spokesperson’s Remarks Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 9, 2026 Updated: September 09, 2026 17:34 Xinhua News Agency: We noted recent comments saying China only cares for its own development while “pulling up the ladder” for the development of other Global South countries. What is your comment? Mao Ning: China never pulls up the ladder from any country. Rather, China has long been building up ladders so that countries could reach higher together. Through high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, for instance, China has been helping partner countries bridge the infrastructure gap. By providing Global South countries with affordable industrial equipment and tech products and sharing experience and expertise, China has helped lower the cost for these countries’ industrial growth. China’s zero-tariff policy and “Export to China” initiative generate profits and market opportunities that enable Global South countries to better integrate into the global supply chains and enhance growth resilience. For China, cooperation with other countries has always been about mutual success. The “pulling-up-the-ladder” narrative has zero resonance with Global South countries. China will always pursue mutual benefit and common development, be a reliable partner of Global South countries, and contribute to the prosperity of the Global South through China’s own development. AFP: U.S. cyber security firm Calif said yesterday that it has built an AI-assisted hacking tool that can access the personal accounts and private information on the Chinese app WeChat. Tencent has said that the security risk has been fixed after being notified by Calif. But as a matter of cyber security, does the foreign ministry have comments on this? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with the specifics. China stands for promoting AI for good and preventing the abuse and malicious use of AI. AFP: Yesterday, the U.S. Cyber Defense Agency accused top Chinese AI labs, including DeepSeek and Moonshot of stealing the capabilities of U.S. models. It said that these campaigns “form the core” of China-based AI companies’ strategies. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on this? Mao Ning: The development of AI in China comes from greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology, and is fueled by China’s vision of extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit and commitment to open cooperation. We believe all parties need to make sure AI development is open and inclusive and promotes the well-being of humanity as a force for good and for all. We hope the U.S. side will earnestly act on the important common understandings reached between the two presidents and stop leveling false allegations to smear China. As two major powers in AI, China and the U.S. should step up cooperation. NHK: The BRICS Summit will be held in India this weekend. Who will lead the Chinese delegation? Mao Ning: We will release timely information if there is any update. Please stay tuned. AFP: At an international forum yesterday, the Defense Secretary of the Philippines Gilberto Teodoro Jr. criticized what he called a violation of UNCLOS and “coercion, bullying and aggression” by China in response to him being handed a piece of paper stating China’s position on the South China Sea. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on the situation or a response to the remarks by the Philippines’ Defense Secretary? Mao Ning: I’m not sure what exactly happened at the event, but China’s position has always been clear on the so-called “South China Sea arbitration”. The Philippines unilaterally initiated the case, which is a distortion and abuse of the UNCLOS dispute settlement mechanism. It is the Philippine side who has violated UNCLOS and undermined its integrity and authority. We urge the certain individual of the Philippine side to cut the provocations and theatrics, and stop undermining China-Philippines relations and stability in the South China Sea.
title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 9, 2026

body: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 8, 2026_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China IPC Visas English EN 简体中文 Français Español Русский عربي HOME THE MINISTRY Main Responsibilities The Minister Principal Officials Departments Related Agencies NEWS Top Stories Speeches Diplomatic Schedule New Ambassadors MFA News Spokesperson’s Remarks News from Overseas Missions RESOURCES Communiqués Foreign Policies In Focus Diplomatic History Diplomatic Figures Protocol Affairs Map of China OVERSEAS MISSIONS Chinese Embassies Chinese Consulates General Chinese Missions to International Organizations and Representative Offices Abroad COUNTRIES AND REGIONS Asia Africa Europe North America South America Oceania ABOUT CHINA Home News Spokesperson’s Remarks Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 8, 2026 Updated: September 08, 2026 17:05 CCTV: Could you update us on China’s assistance for Nepal’s disaster relief efforts? Mao Ning: To support Nepal’s rescue and relief efforts, China sent out this morning the fourth batch of emergency relief supplies, including equipment for transportation and lighting and mortuary supplies. Across China, help is on the way to Nepal. China Foundation for Rural Development has sent people to the affected communities in Nepal to set up temporary shelters and provide daily necessities and basic medical services. The Chinese Enterprises Association in Nepal recently delivered the first batch of funds donated for relief operations. China will continue standing firmly with Nepal to overcome this challenging time together. RT: The Japanese government recently asked Russia to remove a monument commemorating the victory over Japan’s militarism, saying that this issue affects the feelings of the Japanese people. And Japan also claimed that the “Enemy State Clauses” in the UN Charter are obsolete. How does China view these comments made by the Japanese government on WWII history and postwar international order? Mao Ning: To view and treat history correctly is a key gauge of Japan’s commitment to peaceful development. Japan joined the UN after admitting to its militarist crimes and recognizing the UN Charter in its entirety. The “Enemy State Clauses” in the Charter, a special set of rules for WWII defeated states, are still valid today. This year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials. The Japanese side should use history as a mirror, make a clean break with militarism, and earn trust from its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions. China-Arab TV: Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Qatar Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani is on a visit to China from September 7 to 8. Can you elaborate on the goals and significance of this visit? Specifically, how does China view the timing of this visit, and what are the outcomes of the bilateral talks? Mao Ning: China and Qatar are strategic partners. China highly values its relations with Qatar. Qatari Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani is on a visit to China. Yesterday, Premier Li Qiang met with him for in-depth exchange of views on issues of mutual interest. China looks to the visit as an opportunity to work for new progress in bilateral relations. On more details about the visit, we will release timely readouts. Please check back for updates. Beijing Youth Daily: We noted that China is hosting a Workshop on AI Capacity-Building in Beijing. Could you share with us more details? What’s China’s view on AI capacity-building? Mao Ning: At the 2026 World AI Conference & High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance, President Xi Jinping announced that in the next five years, China will provide developing countries with 5,000 opportunities in AI training and seminar programs. To ensure its early implementation, China is hosting once again a Workshop on AI Capacity-Building in Peking University from September 7 to 12. As part of the continued efforts to implement the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All, China established the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, in an effort to make relevant technologies and services more accessible, and help Global South countries find a path to AI development suited to their needs. We will work with various parties to make AI a lasting source of benefits and a major driving force for the welfare of all humanity. AFP: India is scheduled to host a BRICS summit this weekend. Can the foreign ministry confirm who will be attending on China’s behalf? Secondly, what are China’s expectations for this BRICS summit? Mao Ning: China sets great store by BRICS cooperation. We support India in hosting a successful BRICS summit this year. For your specific questions, I don’t have more information to offer at the moment. China Daily: It’s reported that Lai Ching-te claimed at an event that China is contorting UNGA Resolution 2758. Taiwan is a “sovereign independent nation.” The resolution only addresses the People’s Republic of China’s representation at the UN and has nothing to do with Taiwan. What is China’s comment on this? Mao Ning: There is but one China in the world, and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory. This is an unshakable fact grounded in both history and law. The Cairo Declaration issued by China, the U.S. and the UK in 1943 stated in explicit terms that Taiwan is a territory that Japan had stolen and shall be restored to China. The Potsdam Proclamation in 1945 reaffirmed that the terms of the Cairo Declaration shall be carried out. This series of instruments with legal effect under international law have all clearly affirmed China’s sovereignty over Taiwan. UNGA Resolution 2758 solemnly reaffirmed the one-China principle, which “decides to restore all its rights to the People’s Republic of China and to recognize the representatives of its Government as the only legitimate representatives of China to the United Nations.” From political, legal and procedural aspects, the resolution resolved once and for all the question of the representation of the whole of China, including Taiwan, in the UN. It made clear that there is only one seat of China in the United Nations, and there is no such thing as “two Chinas” or “one China, one Taiwan.” Taiwan has never been a country and will never be a country. The Lai Ching-te authorities’ deliberate distortion of UNGA Resolution 2758 once again revealed their separatist nature for “Taiwan independence.” Their rhetoric will not change the historical and legal fact that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait belong to one and the same China, nor will it undermine the international community’s steadfast commitment to one China.
title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 8, 2026

body: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 7, 2026_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China IPC Visas English EN 简体中文 Français Español Русский عربي HOME THE MINISTRY Main Responsibilities The Minister Principal Officials Departments Related Agencies NEWS Top Stories Speeches Diplomatic Schedule New Ambassadors MFA News Spokesperson’s Remarks News from Overseas Missions RESOURCES Communiqués Foreign Policies In Focus Diplomatic History Diplomatic Figures Protocol Affairs Map of China OVERSEAS MISSIONS Chinese Embassies Chinese Consulates General Chinese Missions to International Organizations and Representative Offices Abroad COUNTRIES AND REGIONS Asia Africa Europe North America South America Oceania ABOUT CHINA Home News Spokesperson’s Remarks Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 7, 2026 Updated: September 07, 2026 17:24 CGTN: We noted that a delegation from the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) visited China and inspected facilities for the disposal of Japan’s abandoned chemical weapons (ACWs). Could you please provide more information on the visit? Mao Ning: From August 31 to September 5, the Director-General of the OPCW, the Chairperson of the Executive Council, as well as permanent representatives and senior diplomats from 12 countries to the OPCW, visited China upon invitation. During the visit, they travelled to Hunchun, Dunhua and Haerbaling in Jilin Province to inspect the excavation, recovery and destruction of Japan’s ACWs. The delegation’s visit coincided with China’s annual commemoration of the victory of the Chinese People’s War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. Japan’s militarist aggression inflicted immense humanitarian catastrophes on China and left behind the menace of ACWs. Through the visit, the delegation gained a deeper understanding of the grave harm posed by Japan’s ACWs to the lives and property of the Chinese people and to the country’s ecological environment, and expressed support for the OPCW, in accordance with the Chemical Weapons Convention, in urging the Japanese side to earnestly fulfill its obligations by completely and thoroughly destroying its ACWs in China without further delay, so as to restore a safe habitat for the Chinese people at an early date and realize the noble goal of a world free of chemical weapons as envisaged by the Convention. Reuters: We spoke to the Philippines’ defense secretary earlier today and he said China could use recently scaled-down U.S.-South Korean military exercises as an opportunity to assert itself in the Indo-Pacific region. Do you have anything to say to that comment? Mao Ning: China is always committed to maintaining peace and stability in the Asia Pacific, and does not engage in major-country confrontation. We hope other regional countries will also play a positive role for peace and stability in the region. China News Service: According to the Solomon Star, Taiwan increased its annual aid to Palau from US$18 million last year to US$25 million this year, apparently in an effort to secure political backing at the Pacific Islands Forum. The Taiwan authorities also allocated nearly US$281,000 in direct cash gifts for Palau’s former president, incumbent political figures, and individual lawmakers. The report commented that Taiwan’s taxpayers’ hard-earned money is not being spent on people’s livelihoods. What’s your comment? Mao Ning: The report is yet another example of the Lai Ching-te authorities’ expensive dollar diplomacy using the hard-earned money of the people in Taiwan—a combination of corruption, fraudulence, bribery and power-for-money deals—to serve “Taiwan independence” separatism and their personal political agenda. For certain countries like Palau, having Taiwan as a “diplomatic ally” is not about delivering for the country and the people, but to line the pockets of the very few people who profit from it. EFE: Venezuela says its agreements with China will be respected and Chinese joint ventures will continue operating. Has Caracas given Beijing specific assurances that Chinese oil interests will not be affected by the new U.S.-Venezuela agreement? Mao Ning: Cooperation between China and Venezuela is under the protection of international law and laws of both countries. It has nothing to do with any third party and should not be disrupted by any third party. China’s lawful rights and interests in Venezuela must be protected. AFP: The United States and China will hold talks on AI safety risks in coming weeks. This is according to a recent report by Reuters. Can the foreign ministry confirm these talks? They will reportedly take place in mid-September. What are Chinese expectations for these discussions? Mao Ning: China and the U.S. maintain communication on AI. DPA: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) won the election in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. In an interview with Phoenix TV, the AfD lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund said that for Germany’s better development in the future, Germany needs China from a long-term perspective. What’s China’s take on this election result? Will China enhance communication with the AfD? Mao Ning: Regional elections in Germany are its domestic affair. China will not comment on that. China’s position on developing its relations with Germany is consistent. The Paper: We’ve learned that a group of foreign journalists were allowed by China to gain access to the disaster-hit area in Gyirong for interviews. Can you share more details on that? Mao Ning: The mudslide in Gyirong has drawn close attention from the international media, who hope to enter the area for reporting and interviews. With roads having just been cleared after non-stop repair work, China invited journalists from eight foreign media outlets, including the NBC, CNN, Reuters, RT and PTI, to enter the core area to learn about the impact of the disaster and progress in rescue, recovery and reconstruction. They also attended the group interview for journalists held by Xizang Autonomous Region. I believe you have seen the media reports from these outlets. China will continue its all-out search and rescue efforts to deal with the aftermath. We will provide timely updates on the situation on the ground and rescue operations.
title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 7, 2026

More than 30 participants attended the event, including former Minister of Justice and Public Order Anna Koukkides-Procopiou, President of the UN International Law Commission Andreas Mavroyiannis, Chief of Asia and Oceania Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs George Georgiou, as well as experts, scholars and journalists. Ambassador Yang gave a comprehensive introduction to the background, core principles and significance of the Global Governance Initiative. He noted that over the past year since its inception, the GGI has evolved from a Chinese proposal into international practice and demonstrated strong vitality and broad appeal. China stands ready to work with Cyprus and the international community to jointly promote a more just and equitable global governance system. Participants spoke highly of the GGI, noting that it brings valuable stability and certainty to a world undergoing turbulence and transformation, responds to the aspirations of small and medium-sized countries for equal participation in global governance, and provides an important platform for strengthening multilateral cooperation and improving the global governance system. Ambassador Yang also had in-depth exchanges with the participants on topics such as sovereign equality, the role of the UN, and global governance on artificial intelligence.

Jessica Alupo, Vice President of Uganda. Mr. Karugaba, Director General of International Political Affairs at Uganda’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and others were present. Ambassador Wu said that under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, the China-Uganda comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership has continued to deepen, with steadily stronger political mutual trust, fruitful practical cooperation and renewed vitality in the traditional friendship. Chen briefed Mayor Tepania on the latest progress in practical cooperation between China and New Zealand across various fields. He noted that subnational cooperation is an important component of the China-New Zealand Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. As an important birthplace of Māori culture, the Far North District is richly endowed with natural resources. It established a sister-city relationship with China’s Liaoning Province as early as 2000, and the two sides enjoy strong economic complementarity. The Consulate-General stands ready to serve as a bridge and facilitate greater exchanges and cooperation between the Far North District and China in such areas as tourism, science and education, agriculture and infrastructure. Mayor Tepania welcomed CG Chen and his delegation. He said that the Far North District attaches great importance to its sister relationship with Liaoning Province and looks forward to the opportunity to visit China and further explore new opportunities for cooperation. During the visit, Chen also visited forest plantations in the Far North owned by China Forestry Group New Zealand Company. He learned about the company’s workplace safety and business operations, and expressed his hope that it would actively expand its business, uphold compliance in its operations, and make greater contributions to promoting China-New Zealand economic and trade cooperation.

body: Chinese Ambassador to the Maldives Kong Xianhua Publishes Signed Article Titled “The Darkness Before Dawn Will Eventually Be Overcome” in Leading Maldivian Media_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China IPC Visas English EN 简体中文 Français Español Русский عربي HOME THE MINISTRY Main Responsibilities The Minister Principal Officials Departments Related Agencies NEWS Top Stories Speeches Diplomatic Schedule New Ambassadors MFA News Spokesperson’s Remarks News from Overseas Missions RESOURCES Communiqués Foreign Policies In Focus Diplomatic History Diplomatic Figures Protocol Affairs Map of China OVERSEAS MISSIONS Chinese Embassies Chinese Consulates General Chinese Missions to International Organizations and Representative Offices Abroad COUNTRIES AND REGIONS Asia Africa Europe North America South America Oceania ABOUT CHINA Home Resources In Focus Chinese Chiefs of Mission On the Governance of China From Ambassadors Chinese Ambassador to the Maldives Kong Xianhua Publishes Signed Article Titled “The Darkness Before Dawn Will Eventually Be Overcome” in Leading Maldivian Media Updated: August 20, 2026 12:21 (From Chinese Embassy in Maldives) On August 17, H.E. Mr. Kong Xianhua, Ambassador of China to the Maldives, published a signed article titled “The Darkness Before Dawn Will Eventually Be Overcome” in major Maldivian media outlets, including MMTV and Sun. The article elaborates on the concept of building a community with a shared future for humanity. The full text is as follows: The Darkness Before Dawn Will Eventually Be Overcome By H.E. Mr. Kong Xianhua The world stands at a new historical crossroads. The conflict in the Middle East continues to spill over, the Ukraine crisis drags on, trade protectionism and unilateral sanctions keep surfacing, and new technologies such as artificial intelligence are creating huge opportunities while posing new governance challenges. The international community has more technological power and material wealth than ever before, yet it still faces growing conflict, uneven development and a governance deficit. Why, then, has a world that is more closely connected than ever not become safer? Why have stronger international rules not brought more fairness and trust? At the root of these problems is the shadow of the old order that still hangs over the world. The logic of old colonialism still lingers. Colonialism as a system ended long ago, but its political legacy and ways of thinking have not truly disappeared. For too long, the international political and economic order has reflected the interests of a small number of developed countries, while developing countries remain underrepresented and have too little say in global governance, the distribution of development resources and the making of international rules. Some countries still treat the Western path to modernization as the only model, and frequently invoke democracy, human rights and the rule of law to interfere in the internal affairs of other countries, while applying international rules selectively. The United States, for example, has yet to ratify the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, but repeatedly invokes the so-called “South China Sea arbitration award” to interfere in regional affairs. It has long imposed unilateral sanctions without UN authorization, yet continues to portray itself as a defender of the international order. Putting one’s own will above international rules is, in essence, an expression of the arrogance of old colonialism. It not only undermines the authority of international law, but also deepens mistrust among countries. Common challenges require shared responsibility. The world today is an increasingly interconnected community in which interests are intertwined and security is shared. Climate change, energy and food security, public health, and artificial intelligence governance have all long crossed national borders. No country can tackle them alone. In the face of such challenges, countries cannot focus only on their own interests. They must shoulder their shared responsibilities, safeguard a peaceful and stable environment for development, and work toward a fairer and more reasonable international order. Developing countries are not bystanders in international affairs. They are important participants in global development and a major force in reshaping the international order. Whether it is China, with its vast territory, or the Maldives, with its vast ocean, countries may differ in their circumstances and stages of development, but peace, development and the environment know no borders. Only by strengthening solidarity and cooperation, respecting differences while expanding common interests, can countries turn common challenges into opportunities for shared development and achieve greater common security through shared development. A community with a shared future for humanity points the way to a common future. The more interdependent the world becomes, the more we need to move beyond zero-sum thinking and respond to common challenges through cooperation. President Xi Jinping put forward the concept of building a community with a shared future for humanity as a profound insight into the trend of our times and a positive response to its challenges. It does not call on countries to follow the same path or adopt the same political system. Rather, it advocates mutual respect, fairness and justice, win-win cooperation, and the principle of extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit. It seeks to build a world that is more peaceful, secure, prosperous and open. At its core, the concept seeks the greatest common ground while respecting each country’s right to choose its own path. It links the development of individual countries with global development and better aligns national interests with the common interests of humanity. China’s efforts to advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, as well as its Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative, Global Civilization Initiative and Global Governance Initiative, have enriched and expanded the concept of building a community with a shared future for humanity in different ways. Together, they offer answers to a defining question of our time: What kind of world should we build, and how should we build it? A shared vision requires shared action. The strength and vitality of the concept of building a community with a shared future for humanity lie not only in its forward-looking ideas, but also in the fact that it follows the reality of growing global interdependence and offers a practical way for countries to manage differences and disagreements. The concept does not ignore differences in development or conflicts of interest among countries. Instead, it respects each country’s national conditions and development path while encouraging countries to find room for cooperation in areas of common interest and pursue mutual benefit and win-win outcomes in an interdependent world. This is fundamentally different from the old logic of the strong bullying the weak and zero-sum competition. A community with a shared future for humanity sees countries not as rivals whose gains must come at each other’s expense, but as partners capable of growing together. It does not seek to make the world uniform, but to achieve common progress while seeking common ground and respecting differences. As more countries see opportunities in cooperation and gain tangible benefits from shared development, building a community with a shared future for humanity will become more than an idea. It is becoming a practical choice through which countries can shape their future together. The world will not remain trapped forever in conflict and confrontation, nor will it remain bound forever by zero-sum thinking. body: Remarks by Chinese Consul General in Chicago Wang Baodong at the U.S.-China Soybean Industry Partnership Breakfast_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China IPC Visas English EN 简体中文 Français Español Русский عربي HOME THE MINISTRY Main Responsibilities The Minister Principal Officials Departments Related Agencies NEWS Top Stories Speeches Diplomatic Schedule New Ambassadors MFA News Spokesperson’s Remarks News from Overseas Missions RESOURCES Communiqués Foreign Policies In Focus Diplomatic History Diplomatic Figures Protocol Affairs Map of China OVERSEAS MISSIONS Chinese Embassies Chinese Consulates General Chinese Missions to International Organizations and Representative Offices Abroad COUNTRIES AND REGIONS Asia Africa Europe North America South America Oceania ABOUT CHINA Home Resources In Focus Chinese Chiefs of Mission On the Governance of China From Consuls General Remarks by Chinese Consul General in Chicago Wang Baodong at the U.S.-China Soybean Industry Partnership Breakfast Updated: August 20, 2026 04:12 (From Chinese Consulate General in Chicago) Distinguished guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good morning! It gives me great pleasure to join friends, both old and new, to attend the U.S.-China Soybean Industry Partner Breakfast, to exchange views on issues of mutual interest. On behalf of the Chinese Consulate General in Chicago, I would like to particularly extend my warmest welcome to the representatives of Chinese companies who have traveled afar from China to participate in today’s event. Today, August 7, marks the Start of Autumn (Liqiu), one of the 24 solar terms in China. For farmers, this is a crucial period that not only signals the time for harvesting crops but also serves as an optimal juncture for planning agricultural trade. Therefore, this partners’ breakfast meeting is perfectly timed. For many years, soybeans have served as an important bridge in China-U.S. agricultural cooperation, and soybean trade has been a cornerstone of the broader bilateral economic and trade relationship. China is home to the world’s biggest market for agricultural products, while the U.S. is a top agricultural producer and the largest exporter. High-quality U.S. soybeans can help meet the growing demand of Chinese consumers, while the Chinese market generates income and supports jobs for American farmers and rural communities. China-U.S. agricultural cooperation used to enjoy “good old days”. According to statistics released by the General Administration of Customs of China, China’s imports of U.S. agricultural products reached a record high of $40.9 billion in 2022, and Soybeans alone accounted for $17.8 billion—nearly half of China’s total agricultural imports from the U.S.—setting a historical record by far. Even according to statistics from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, which placed total U.S. agricultural exports to China and soybean exports at $4.5 billion and $1.4 billion lower than the Chinese figures respectively, 2022 still marked the highest level ever for U.S. agricultural and soybean exports to the Chinese market. Regrettably, however, the “good old days” came to an abrupt halt last year. The U.S.government launched the tariff and trade war against China, and China was compelled to take necessary countermeasures. As a result, soybean trade between our two countries was disrupted for a period of time, and American farmers became a victim and bore much of the cost, which was never an outcome China wished to see. Encouragingly, the summit meeting between our two Presidents in Busan last October put the bilateral relations back on the right track. Economic and trade cooperation regained positive momentum, and the soybean trade resumed. This tortuous experience once again shows that unilateralism and protectionism serve no one’s interests, and there are no winners in tariff or trade wars. Equality, mutual respect, and mutual benefit remain the right way for China and the U.S. to get along with each other and achieve win-win cooperation. Ladies and gentlemen, This year is a big year for China-U.S. relations. President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump held a successful summit meeting in Beijing in May and agreed to build “a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability”, providing strategic guidance for the future development of the most important bilateral relations in the world and charts the course for closer exchanges and cooperation between the business communities of our two countries. The two Presidents also agreed that President Xi will pay a state visit to the United States this fall. The diplomatic, economic, and trade teams of both sides are actively making preparations for the visit. We are confident that this landmark visit will inject more impetus into the continued growth of China-U.S. relations. This year is also a major year on the domestic political calendars of both China and the United States. In July, the U.S. celebrated the 250th anniversary of its founding, while the Communist Party of China marked its 105th anniversary. These two important milestones reflected the remarkable histories and development journeys of our two countries. Although China and the U.S. have different national conditions and governance systems, our people share common aspirations for a better life, social stability, and economic prosperity. As President Xi Jinping pointed out, the realization of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the vision of “Make America Great Again” can go hand in hand and achieve mutual success. President Trump also stated that China is America’s biggest partner, and that by working together, the two countries can accomplish many great things in the world and achieve greater success through future cooperation. Our two sides should work together to translate the important common understandings reached by the two Presidents into concrete actions, expand the cooperation list, shorten the negative list, and properly handle sensitive issues, particularly the Taiwan question, so as to bring greater benefits to both countries and contribute to a better world. Ladies and gentlemen, This year also marks the beginning of China’s 15th Five-Year Plan period. China is firmly advancing high-quality development and high-standard opening up, while continuing to improve its business and investment environment. As the living standards of the Chinese people continue to rise, China’s demand for agricultural products from around the world, including the U.S., will continue to grow. The prospects for high-quality U.S. soybean exports to China remain promising. However, at the same time, it is disturbing that the U.S. side continues taking measures to create obstacles to China-U.S. economic and trade cooperation. In particular, overstretching the concept of national security and the excessive application of restrictive and discriminatory measures against Chinese companies’ agricultural investment and technological cooperation in the U.S. are harmful to stronger agricultural collaboration between our two countries, which has continued to cast a shadow over the bilateral agricultural trade. What is worse is that anti-China forces label China as an adversary and view it as a threat. That is fundamentally wrong, and we cannot turn a blind eye to it. Currently, China-U.S. economic and trade ties are navigating a landscape of both opportunities and challenges. In May, the economic and trade teams of our two countries reached positive understandings on addressing certain non-tariff barriers and market access issues related to agricultural products. The two sides agreed in principle to include relevant agricultural products in a framework arrangement for reciprocal tariff reductions and set guiding objectives for expanding two-way agricultural trade. Under the new circumstances, China-US agricultural trade cannot return to the past, but it can have a better future. Our two sides should uphold opennes

body: Chinese Ambassador to Myanmar Ma Jia Publishes a Signed Article Titled “Fostering Unity Through the Rule of Law and Advancing Shared Prosperity Through Development” in Myanmar’s Official Media_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China IPC Visas English EN 简体中文 Français Español Русский عربي HOME THE MINISTRY Main Responsibilities The Minister Principal Officials Departments Related Agencies NEWS Top Stories Speeches Diplomatic Schedule New Ambassadors MFA News Spokesperson’s Remarks News from Overseas Missions RESOURCES Communiqués Foreign Policies In Focus Diplomatic History Diplomatic Figures Protocol Affairs Map of China OVERSEAS MISSIONS Chinese Embassies Chinese Consulates General Chinese Missions to International Organizations and Representative Offices Abroad COUNTRIES AND REGIONS Asia Africa Europe North America South America Oceania ABOUT CHINA Home Resources In Focus Chinese Chiefs of Mission On the Governance of China From Ambassadors Chinese Ambassador to Myanmar Ma Jia Publishes a Signed Article Titled “Fostering Unity Through the Rule of Law and Advancing Shared Prosperity Through Development” in Myanmar’s Official Media Updated: August 07, 2026 12:23 (From Chinese Embassy in Myanmar) On August 5th, Ambassador Ma Jia published a signed article titled “Fostering Unity Through the Rule of Law and Advancing Shared Prosperity Through Development” in Myanmar’s official media, including Global New Light of Myanmar and Myanma Alinn Daily. The full text is as follows: On July 1 this year, the Ethnic Unity and Progress Promotion Law of the People’s Republic of China came into force. The law marks three historic firsts. For the first time, it incorporates General Secretary Xi Jinping’s important thought on strengthening and improving work on ethnic affairs into national legislation. For the first time, it clarifies in legal terms such as fostering a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation and advancing the building of a community for the Chinese nation. For the first time, it defines in law the framework for work on ethnic affairs in the new era. It is a successful example of translating the major theoretical achievements and practical experience in work on ethnic affairs into the will of the state through legislation, providing a solid legal foundation for promoting ethnic unity and progress in the new era. I would like to take this opportunity to introduce to our friends from all sectors in Myanmar the law’s guiding principles, institutional framework, and practical results, and to share China’s experience and thinking on promoting ethnic unity and progress through the rule of law. First, the law establishes the fundamental principles for work on ethnic affairs by upholding equality among all ethnic groups and fostering a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation. From the outset, it makes equality among all ethnic groups the basic principle governing work on ethnic affairs and explicitly prohibits all forms of ethnic discrimination and oppression. It provides legal guarantees for the equal participation of all ethnic groups in state governance and for sharing the benefits of development. It upholds the combination of national unity and regional ethnic autonomy, as well as the combination of ethnic factors and regional factors, while safeguarding the equal rights of ethnic minorities in political, economic, cultural, and other fields. Regardless of population size, every ethnic group is an equal member of the Chinese nation, united by a shared future. Guided by the goal of fostering a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation, the law fully respects cultural diversity. It protects by law the freedom of all ethnic groups to use and develop their own spoken and written languages, and the freedom to preserve or reform their customs and traditions. It uses the rule of law to uphold harmony among diverse cultures while enabling every ethnic culture to flourish in its own way. Second, the law promotes integration and shared development by creating more opportunities for interaction and integration among all ethnic groups, encouraging people to live, study, work, and enjoy life together. Promoting extensive interaction and integration among ethnic groups is a central task set out in a dedicated chapter of the law. Today, two-way population mobility has become the norm in China. More than 33 million ethnic minority people live and work away from their registered hometowns, and over one-third of the ethnic minority population now resides in urban and dispersed areas. The pattern of “overall integration, local concentration, mutual interaction” continues to deepen. The law sets out detailed measures covering education, culture and tourism, sports, employment, and community development. It includes specific provisions for building integrated communities and promoting interaction and integration through education, cultural activities, sports, and tourism. These measures help people of different ethnic groups deepen mutual understanding, strengthen mutual respect, bridge differences, build consensus, and make the concept of the Chinese national community part of everyday life. Third, the law focuses on improving people’s well-being through balanced development so that all ethnic groups can share the benefits of Chinese modernization. It is designed to promote common prosperity and development for all ethnic groups. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the combined GDP of China’s five ethnic autonomous regions has grown from RMB 3.25 trillion to RMB 8.66 trillion in recent years, more than doubling in size, while regional development gaps have continued to narrow. From the northern frontier to the south, and from the plateau to the border regions, ethnic minority areas have made major advances in transport, energy, communications, and other fields. Public services in education, healthcare, housing, and social security have continued to improve. Behind these steady gains are real improvements in people’s sense of fulfillment and well-being. The best way to assess a country’s ethnic policy and governance is to look at the facts, examine its development, and see whether people’s lives have truly improved. In China’s ethnic minority areas, high-speed railways have reached border regions, highways now extend to remote villages, and power grids cover even mountainous areas. Schools have been built close to where people live, hospitals are equipped with advanced facilities, and housing conditions have improved greatly. Traditional cultures are also thriving. Ancient epics continue to be passed down, traditional festivals are celebrated with renewed vitality, and intangible cultural heritage is being preserved from generation to generation. In Xinjiang, GDP reached RMB 2.14 trillion in 2025, more than doubling compared with 2012. Xinjiang produces over 90 percent of China’s cotton and has more than 22 million mu of vineyards, jujube orchards, and other specialty fruit plantations. Installed new energy capacity has exceeded 100 million kilowatts, providing strong momentum for economic transformation. The region has more than 8,000 schools of all types, with over six million students enrolled, while access to education continues to improve. Primary healthcare services now cover the entire region. At the same time, the Uyghur Muqam art form and the “Manas” epic have been inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The lawful use of ethnic languages is fully protected, and traditional music, dance, and handicrafts are being systematically preserved. In Xizang, GDP exceeded RMB 300 billion in 2025, nearly tripling compared with 2012. Major infrastructure projects, including the Qinghai-Xizang Railway, the Lhasa-Xigaze Railway, and the Ya’an-Xigaze section of the Sichuan-Xizang Railway, continue to advance. The region’s highway network now exceeds 120,000 kilometers. The co

body: The Keynote Speech by Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia Ouyang Yujing at UTM_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China IPC Visas English EN 简体中文 Français Español Русский عربي HOME THE MINISTRY Main Responsibilities The Minister Principal Officials Departments Related Agencies NEWS Top Stories Speeches Diplomatic Schedule New Ambassadors MFA News Spokesperson’s Remarks News from Overseas Missions RESOURCES Communiqués Foreign Policies In Focus Diplomatic History Diplomatic Figures Protocol Affairs Map of China OVERSEAS MISSIONS Chinese Embassies Chinese Consulates General Chinese Missions to International Organizations and Representative Offices Abroad COUNTRIES AND REGIONS Asia Africa Europe North America South America Oceania ABOUT CHINA Home Resources In Focus Chinese Chiefs of Mission On the Governance of China From Ambassadors The Keynote Speech by Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia Ouyang Yujing at UTM Updated: August 05, 2026 18:16 (From Chinese Embassy in Malaysia) On August 5, Ambassador Ouyang Yujing delivered a keynote speech titled “Innovation, Partnership and Shared Prosperity: China-Malaysia Community with a Shared Future in a Changing World” at UTM. The full text is as follows: Professor Dr. Mohd Shafry Mohd Rahim, Vice-Chancellor of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia, Excellencies and members of the diplomatic corps, Assoc. Prof. Ts. Dr. Mohd Ariffin Abu Hassan, Director of UTM International, Distinguished guests, Ladies and gentlemen, Dear students, Good morning! It gives me great pleasure to visit the beautiful campus of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia. I would like to thank Vice-Chancellor Shafry for his kind invitation. This is my first visit to UTM, yet to China, UTM has long been a familiar and trusted friend. The University has established a strategic partnership with Huawei and developed cooperation with a number of Chinese universities, including the establishment of a Joint Artificial Intelligence Laboratory with Zhejiang University and intelligent manufacturing cooperation with Wuhan University of Technology. Innovation has always been a defining feature of UTM’s cooperation with China. Innovation is the primary driving force for development. Throughout the history of human progress, innovation has always been an important force propelling a country and a nation forward, as well as a powerful force advancing human society as a whole. More than 600 years ago, Admiral Zheng He led the world’s most advanced fleet on seven voyages to the Western Seas. His five stopovers in Malacca were a glorious chapter in the history of China–Malaysia relations. The fleet relied on monsoon winds for navigation. At that time, inviting a Chinese scholar to deliver a lecture at UTM would probably have required a journey of two to three months. More than a century ago, around the time UTM was founded, steamships had become a common means of travel between China and Malaysia. No longer constrained by the monsoon winds, a Chinese scholar could complete the voyage in approximately two weeks. Today, it takes only about six hours to fly from China to Malaysia. An online lecture can be held face to face with just a mobile phone. Even when participants do not speak the same language, artificial intelligence (AI) can provide real-time interpretation. This demonstrates in very tangible ways how scientific and technological innovation is transforming our lives. Today, a new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation is advancing at a faster pace. Information technologies such as AI, quantum information and the Internet of Things are making production and daily life increasingly intelligent. New energy technologies, including new energy vehicles and photovoltaic power generation, are facilitating the global energy transition. Technologies related to commercial aviation and deep-sea development are expanding the frontiers of human survival and development. Never before has science and technology had such a profound impact on the future of nations. Never before has it so profoundly affected the well-being and lives of every individual. In the face of this historic trend, only by accurately grasping the pulse of our times can we secure leadership in development. The Asian continent, one of the important birthplaces of human civilisation, has created splendid civilisations throughout history. Yet, following the Industrial Revolution, Asian countries missed the opportunity presented by technological and institutional transformation. Many countries and regions, including China and Malaysia, were consequently reduced to colonies or semi-colonies of Western powers. Since the end of the Second World War, China and Malaysia have successively achieved national independence. Together with other Asian countries, we have embarked on an Asian path of development characterised by independence and self-reliance, mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, openness and inclusiveness. Since the founding of the People’s Republic of China, and particularly since the beginning of reform and opening up, China and the Chinese people have continued to explore new practices, and achieved the two miracles of the modern world: rapid economic development together with long-term social stability. Malaysia, meanwhile, has demonstrated tremendous economic vitality through its strong development in emerging sectors such as semiconductors and data centers. Today, China is advancing the cause of building a great country and achieving national rejuvenation on all fronts through Chinese modernisation. By 2035, China aims to significantly increase its economic strength, scientific and technological capabilities and overall national strength; achieve greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology and join the ranks of the world’s most innovative countries. China also aims to build a modernised economy and form a new pattern of development; basically modernise the system and capacity for governance; and broadly establish eco-friendly ways of work and life. Chinese modernisation is underpinned and driven by the development of new quality productive forces. The development and leapfrog of new quality productive forces is also a defining feature of China’s advancement of Chinese modernisation on all fronts. New quality productive forces are an advanced form of productive forces in which innovation plays the leading role. They transcend traditional economic growth models and conventional paths of productive-force development and are characterised by high technology, high efficiency and high quality. Developing new quality productive forces, of course, does not mean neglecting or abandoning traditional industries. Rather, it means taking an initiative to foster new industries, new models and new growth drivers, upgrading traditional industries with new technologies, and actively promoting the high-end, intelligent and green transformation of industries. In the first half of this year, China made new breakthroughs in developing new quality productive forces. New growth drivers represented by high-end manufacturing, smart economy and modern services contributed more than 40% to China’s economic growth, becoming a key force in promoting higher-quality and innovation-driven economic development. In the past, the term “new trio” was often used in connection with “Made in China”, referring to new energy vehicles, lithium-ion batteries and photovoltaic products. After years of development, new energy vehicles now account for more than 50% of new vehicle sales in the Chinese market. China has also built the world’s largest and fastest-growing renewable-energy system. It supplies more than 80% of the world’s photovoltaic modules and 70% of its wind-power equipment, while helping to drive down the cost of renewable energy continuously over the past decade. body: Chinese Ambassador to the Federated States of Micronesia Wu Wei Publishes An Article in The Kaselehlie Press_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China IPC Visas English EN 简体中文 Français Español Русский عربي HOME THE MINISTRY Main Responsibilities The Minister Principal Officials Departments Related Agencies NEWS Top Stories Speeches Diplomatic Schedule New Ambassadors MFA News Spokesperson’s Remarks News from Overseas Missions RESOURCES Communiqués Foreign Policies In Focus Diplomatic History Diplomatic Figures Protocol Affairs Map of China OVERSEAS MISSIONS Chinese Embassies Chinese Consulates General Chinese Missions to International Organizations and Representative Offices Abroad COUNTRIES AND REGIONS Asia Africa Europe North America South America Oceania ABOUT CHINA Home Resources In Focus Chinese Chiefs of Mission On the Governance of China From Ambassadors Chinese Ambassador to the Federated States of Micronesia Wu Wei Publishes An Article in The Kaselehlie Press Updated: July 29, 2026 06:57 (From Chinese Embassy in the Federated States of Micronesia) On 28, July 2026, an article by Ambassador Wu Wei titled “Upholding the One-China Principle to Open a New Chapter in China-Pacific Cooperation” was published in The Kaselehlie Press, the bi-weekly newspaper in the FSM, in its Vol. 26 Issue No. 17. The full text is as follows: On July 15, Papua New Guinea officially announced the closure of the “Chinese Taipei Economic Office in PNG.” Following its decision to shut down the “PNG Trade Mission in Taiwan” in January 2023, this latest move once again underscores PNG’s steadfast commitment to the one-China principle. More importantly, it sends a clear message across the Pacific that mutual respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, non-interference in the internal affairs of other countries, and other fundamental norms governing international relations must be upheld, while reaffirming PNG’s resolve to stand firmly on the right side of history. As PNG’s Foreign Minister Tkatchenko stated, this administrative action underscores the Government’s unwavering commitment to honoring, respecting, and upholding PNG’s foundational one-China policy. The PNG Government views this administrative alignment as a vital and necessary step toward deepening state-to-state trust, reinforcing our shared values, and elevating the bilateral relationship between PNG and the People’s Republic of China to unprecedented levels. PNG’s decision also illustrates an undeniable truth: upholding the one-China principle is where international public opinion trends and the arc of history bends. Any attempt to challenge this principle or create “two Chinas” or “one China, one Taiwan” is doomed to fail. The just cause of the Chinese people in opposing “Taiwan independence” separatist activities and realizing national reunification will continue to gain broader understanding and stronger support from the international community. There is but one China in the world. Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory. The Government of the People’s Republic of China is the sole legal government representing the whole of China. The one-China principle is a universally recognized basic norm governing international relations and a prevailing international consensus. The UNGA Resolution 2758 in 1971 solemnly confirms and fully embodies the one-China principle. It was clearly stated in the official legal opinions of the Office of Legal Affairs of the U.N. Secretariat that “the United Nations considers ‘Taiwan’ as a province of China with no separate status.” To date, China has established diplomatic relations with 183 countries, all of which have made solemn political commitments in their joint communiqués with China to abide by the one-China principle. In 1989, the Government of the People’s Republic of China and the Government of the Federated States of Micronesia signed the Joint Communiqué on the Establishment of Diplomatic Relations, under which the FSM recognizes the Government of the People’s Republic of China as the sole legal government of China. Since then, the traditional friendship between the two countries has entered a new stage of development. Over the past 37 years, China and the FSM have consistently supported each other on issues concerning their respective core interests and major concerns, continuously deepened political mutual trust, steadily expanded practical cooperation across various fields, and advanced the China-FSM Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. Across the Pacific, the overwhelming majority of island countries have seen clearly the trend of history, upheld justice, and embraced a brighter future of friendly cooperation with China. In recent years, the Solomon Islands, Kiribati, and Naoero have successively established or resumed diplomatic relations with China, removing the political barriers to comprehensive cooperation. President Xi Jinping presented China’s policy toward Pacific Island countries, namely China fully respects the sovereignty and independence of Pacific Island countries, fully respects their will, fully respects their cultural traditions and fully respects their effort to seek strength through unity. Guided by the “four full respects,” China and these Pacific Island countries have witnessed flourishing exchanges at all levels and across various sectors, signed Belt and Road cooperation documents, achieved substantial early outcomes in mutually beneficial cooperation, and opened up broad new prospects for common development. Regrettably, certain Pacific Island countries—including Palau, the Marshall Islands, and Tuvalu—remain blinded and utilized by the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities in Taiwan and continue to maintain so-called “diplomatic relations” with Taiwan, placing themselves outside the international consensus on the one-China principle. In an attempt to drill through the rock-solid international commitment to the one-China principle, the DPP authorities have coerced or cajoled the said countries through dollar diplomacy and bribes. They have gone to great lengths to expand their presence in the Pacific Island region, even seeking to participate in regional intergovernmental meetings under various pretexts to enlarge their so-called “international space.” Their ultimate and ulterior objective is to tie Pacific Island countries to the war chariot of “Taiwan independence.” Support for “Taiwan independence” means interference in China’s internal affairs and attempts to abet “Taiwan independence” mean destabilizing the Taiwan Strait. China’s reunification is an irreversible trend, and the DPP authorities’ futile attempts amount to nothing more than self-deception having little support in the Pacific islands region and will ultimately end in humiliation. Facts speak louder than rhetoric, and genuine cooperation always outweighs political opportunism. As the world’s second-largest economy and one of its fastest-growing major economies, China offers tremendous development opportunities and vast prospects for mutually beneficial cooperation. Standing with China and adhering to the one-China principle is the natural choice for Pacific Island countries that seek to keep pace with the times, advance the well-being of their peoples, and stand on the right side of history. In fact, China has remained Palau’s largest single source of tourists for many consecutive years. According to statistics released by Palau, visitors from the Chinese mainland accounted for 36 percent of all arrivals in the first quarter of 2026, directly boosting tourism, hospitality, catering, and related service industries while providing strong support for economic recovery, job creation, and income growth. In the Marshall Islands, entrepreneurs in the local Chinese community have long contributed to the local economy by expanding the supply of goods, invigorating commerce, improving people’s livelihoods, and supporting sustainable ec
