body: Движение «Ансар аллах» (хуситы) продолжает наступать в Йемене / Mohammed Huwais / AFP Боевые действия в Йемене между проиранским движением «Ансар аллах» (хуситы) и силами просаудовского правительства продолжаются. 13 сентября представитель хуситов Яхья Сари заявил, что движение нанесло удар по военной базе Шарура на юге Саудовской Аравии. Целями операции хуситов, по словам Сари, стали саудовские склады оружия, а также командные и контрольные центры. Удары были нанесены с использованием баллистических ракет и беспилотников, о чем Сари сообщил в своем аккаунте в Х. Хуситы заверили саудовскую сторону в том, что удары вглубь территории королевства продолжатся, если Эр-Рияд не откажется от «агрессии». Ранее, 12 сентября, правительственные войска Йемена при поддержке саудитов нанесли серию ударов по позициям хуситов. При этом президент США Дональд Трамп 12 сентября, отвечая на вопросы журналистов в Дублине, заявил, что движение не хочет воевать с Америкой: «Хуситы позвонили нам. Они не хотят сражаться с нами. Они дали нам это знать». По словам Трампа, хуситов не устраивает только Саудовская Аравия, которая поддерживает враждующее с «Ансар аллах» официальное правительство Йемена. При этом и сами американцы тоже не горят желанием ввязываться в полномасштабный конфликт с хуситами. Как сообщал ранее американский портал Axios, фактический руководитель Саудовской Аравии кронпринц Мухаммед бен Салман Аль Сауд дважды по телефону просил Трампа нанести удар по позициям хуситов. Президент США отказал наследному принцу в прямой военной помощи, мотивировав это необходимостью Вашингтона сосредоточиться на конфликте с Ираном. Посольство США в Йемене, на самом деле расположенное в саудовской столице Эр-Рияде, ограничилось заявлениями в Х в поддержку «йеменского правительства и йеменского народа перед агрессией хуситов». Не заявили о военной помощи своими войсками Саудовской Аравии и Турция с Пакистаном, заключившие с ней в начале августа военный союз. Американская позиция в отношении конфликта вокруг Красного моря не столь выразительна по ряду причин, поясняет научный сотрудник Центра североамериканских исследований ИМЭМО РАН Алексей Юрк. Во-первых, администрация Трампа в 2025 г. уже пробовала разгромить хуситов, что закончилось тактическим выигрышем в виде перемирия и гарантий ненанесения хуситами ударов по американским кораблям при отсутствии каких-либо стратегических успехов. Более того, кампания стала первой ласточкой в череде военных неудач текущей администрации, продемонстрировав ограниченность военных инструментов США. Во-вторых, все имеющиеся ресурсы пока сконцентрированы вокруг Ирана. Наконец, в-третьих, обострившийся конфликт между хуситами и Саудовской Аравией теоретически дает возможность Трампу впоследствии втянуть Эр-Рияд в прямое противостояние с Тегераном. Хуситы продолжают удерживать контроль над важной транспортной артерией – Баб-эль-Мандебом. Просаудовские войска Совета президентского правления Йемена после потери стратегического порта Моха покинули также 11 сентября острова Перим, Зукар и архипелаг Ханиш, что фактически передало пролив под контроль хуситов. Они, в свою очередь, заявили, что судоходство в проливе для всех коммерческих судов, кроме саудовских, полностью безопасно. Баб-эль-Мандебский пролив использовала Саудовская Аравия для перевозки своей нефти, разгружая танкеры в порту Янбу на берегу Красного моря после блокады Ормуза. Из-за атак беспилотников в районе Эр-Рияда и Медины был остановлен нефтепровод «Восток – Запад», сообщило саудовское государственное информагентство SPA. Именно через него идут поставки нефти из района Персидского залива после блокады Ормуза. Повреждения получили насосные станции, в результате чего вспыхнул пожар и пострадали люди. По мнению саудовской стороны, удары по нефтепроводу были нанесены с территории Ирака. Текущий нефтяной кризис в Баб-эль-Мандебском проливе и в южной части Красного моря после проблем с Ормузом выходит за пределы нефтяной и транспортной отрасли, отмечает энергоэксперт Кирилл Родионов. Сам Баб-эль-Мандеб до кризиса в Ормузе имел для нефтетранспортной отрасли меньшее значение – в 2025 г. через него проходило в среднем 4 млн барр./сутки против ормузских 20 млн барр./сутки. Но в ситуации кризиса вокруг Ирана в Персидском заливе значение этого пути выросло – этот маршрут в основном сейчас и используется для поставок как в сторону Азии, так и в Европу, указывает эксперт. Как мировые СМИ оценивают последствия наступления хуситов для рынков нефти и США Политика / Международные новости Происходящее, отмечает Юрк, явно выгодно Ирану, поскольку оно неизбежно отвлекает арабские, израильские и потенциально американские ресурсы от него самого и в очередной демонстрирует всему миру неспособность США достичь нужных результатов военным путем. Все это вместе, по мысли Тегерана, должно подтолкнуть если не Вашингтон, то как минимум его союзников к переговорам с ним. В то же время, отмечает эксперт, не стоит забывать, что очередному обострению конфликта способствовали именно саудиты, нанесшие в июле удар по аэропорту, в который должна была прибыть иранская делегация. Этот шаг дал Ирану отличный повод обострить конфликт вокруг Баб-эль-Мандебского пролива. «Ансар аллах» – хуситы по факту являются самой боеспособной и организованной силой в Йемене, что они неоднократно доказывали и ранее, говорит старший научный сотрудник Центра анализа стратегий и технологий Юрий Лямин. У хуситов мощная идеологическая основа и талантливый лидер в лице Абдул-Малика аль-Хуси. Причем на подконтрольных им территориях живет оценочно от 70% и более населения Йемена, что обеспечивает хуситам огромный мобилизационный потенциал, которым они весьма эффективно распоряжаются. Иранская поддержка предоставила им ракетные, беспилотные и прочие технологии. В свою очередь, противостоящие им в Йемене силы, несмотря на военную, финансовую и прочую поддержку со стороны Саудовской Аравии, мало того что имеют намного меньший мобилизационный потенциал – фактически представляют собой конгломерат разнородных формирований и группировок со своими лидерами и целями. Хуситы уже имеют опыт крупных наступательных операций, грамотно комбинируя использование ракет, БПЛА и удары своей высокомотивированной легкой и моторизованной пехоты в условиях противодействия вражеской авиации. Без саудовской авиаподдержки хуситы давно бы одержали победу в войне, считает Лямин. С другой стороны, у этой поддержки есть серьезные ограничения. Так, саудовская авиация за все годы войны так и не научилась оперативно оказывать поддержку просаудовским силам на земле, говорит Лямин. body: Андрей Гордеев / Ведомости В январе – августе 2026 г. в России было произведено 27 614 грузовых вагонов, следует из данных ассоциации «Объединение производителей железнодорожной техники» (ОПЖТ). Это значение на 27% ниже, чем за восемь месяцев 2025 г. Наиболее массовой номенклатурой в отчетном периоде стали цистерны: всего было выпущено 12 390 таких вагонов, на 7% больше, чем годом ранее. Также предприятия произвели 9924 полувагона (-42% г/г), 3266 крытых вагонов (+49%), 1207 хопперов (-52%), 524 платформы (в 8 раз меньше), 205 изотермических вагонов (+5%) и 95 вагонов-самосвалов. В общем объеме выпуска 10 527 вагонов пришлось на так называемые инновационные полувагоны с нагрузкой 25 тонна-сил (ТС) против стандартных 23,5 ТС. Это на 21% меньше, чем годом ранее. body: Валерий Шарифулин / ТАСС В последнюю неделю до единого дня голосования суды будут рассматривать апелляции партий и кандидатов на решения, позволяющие снять их с выборов. С административными проблемами продолжают сталкиваться КПРФ, «Яблоко» и «Справедливая Россия» (СР). 9 сентября стало последним днем, когда подобные иски можно было подавать, но их рассмотрение продолжалось. Один из самых громких процессов проходил 11 сентября в Коми. В Верховном суде республики рассматривался иск кандидата от «Зеленых» Семена Кулешова о снятии с выборов действующего депутата Госдумы (ГД) Олега Михайлова (КПРФ). Истец указывал на нарушение коммунистом авторских прав: например, он не указал автора памятника, на фоне которого записал видео, а в другом случае «незаконно» использовал логотип Wildberries. Как пояснил «Ведомостям» Михайлов, в одном из роликов он выступил в защиту селлеров напротив пункта выдачи заказов маркетплейса. Рассмотрение началось с того, что представитель Кулешова отозвал его. По словам Михайлова, тот предложил не тратить «время и нервы» на взаимные иски. Наблюдая за тем, как в регионах пытаются снять с выборов коммунистов за нарушения авторских прав, КПРФ подала несколько исковых заявлений по тем же основаниям к кандидатам от «Зеленых», «Коммунистов России», «Новых людей» и др., сказал депутат «Ведомостям». Шаги к избирателю Мнения На попытки снять с выборов Михайлова реагировал в своем заявлении 17 августа председатель ЦК КПРФ Геннадий Зюганов . Из упоминавшихся в его заявлении регистрацию все же потерял «красный» блогер Николай Бондаренко, а депутат ГД Михаил Матвеев добился восстановления на выборах в ГД. «Яблоко» 11 сентября понесло очередную потерю на выборах в заксобрания. По иску ЛДПР отменена регистрация списка партии в Томской области. Основаниями стали нарушение авторских прав и правил финансирования избирательной кампании, сообщили в пресс-службе «Яблока». Аналогичные претензии фигурировали в иске «Родине» для отмены регистрации списка партии на выборах в ГД. В «Яблоке» будут обжаловать решение Томского областного суда. Только в одном из восьми регионов, где партия выдвигала список в парламенты субъектов, она его сохранила – в Новгородской области. При этом 9 сентября избирком этого региона отменил регистрацию лидера списка на выборах в облдуму и депутата Думы Великого Новгорода Анны Черепановой. Наиболее конкурентные кампании 2026 года: грядущие выборы в цифрах и графиках Политика / Демократия В этот же день суд в Челябинской области снял всех пятерых кандидатов, выдвинутых на выборы в ГД по округам. Истцом выступила партия «Зеленые». Также была снята с выборов 11 сентября кандидат-одномандатник в Смоленской области Лариса Должикова (округ No 176). Иск вновь подал оппонент из «Зеленых» Дарья Шаврикова. По этому же округу избирается вице-спикер ГД Александр Бабаков (СР). СР тоже столкнулась с проблемами – в Санкт-Петербурге задержали и составили протокол по ст. 20.3 КоАП (демонстрация экстремистской символики) на кандидата в заксобрание Нэлли Вавилину. Приговор по этой статье лишает кандидата права участвовать в выборах в течение года, но решение еще не вступило в силу. Справороссы находятся в конфликте с городским руководством. Накануне задержания Вавилина разместила в соцсетях «семь «невопросов» губернатору Александру Беглову с критикой решений властей Петербурга. ЦИК пригласил на сентябрьские выборы 12 международных миссий Политика / Демократия Для всех участников выборов этот электоральный цикл оказался сложнее с точки зрения «нападения» юристов из конкурирующих штабов друг на друга, отмечает политолог Константин Калачев. «Роль юристов в кампаниях растет от цикла к циклу. Это повод задуматься о тех проблемах избирательного законодательства, из-за которых их роль становится гипертрофированной», – сообщил он «Ведомостям». Самые большие проблемы на выборах 2026 г. возникли у «Яблока»: потеря федерального списка на выборы в ГД, снос списков в субъектах и отмена регистраций у одномандатников, напоминает политолог Дмитрий Еловский. Ситуация с СР связана с локальными разборками в Петербурге, полагает он. «Ведомости» направили запрос в ЦИК с просьбой сообщить, сколько всего кандидатов снято с выборов в ГД с момента их регистрации. body: Татьяна Голикова поздравила Московскую консерваторию им. П.И.Чайковского со 160-летием 13 сентября 2026 21:15 Работа Правительства: Театр. Музыка. Изобразительное искусство Заместитель Председателя Правительства Татьяна Голикова поздравила Московскую консерваторию им. П.И.Чайковского со 160-летием со дня основания: «Дорогие друзья! От всей души поздравляю вас со 160-летием Московской государственной консерватории имени П.И.Чайковского. Это значимое событие для всей отечественной культуры: 160 лет служения высокому искусству и воспитанию талантов, чьи имена навсегда вписаны в историю мирового творческого наследия. За более чем полтора века консерватория прошла путь от музыкальных классов, созданных по инициативе Николая Рубинштейна, до одного из ведущих музыкальных вузов России и мира. Здесь преподавали такие яркие деятели, как Пётр Чайковский, Иосиф Венявский, Фердинанд Лауб, Людвиг Минкус. А среди выпускников – те, чьи имена известны всему миру: Сергей Рахманинов, Александр Скрябин, Святослав Рихтер, Мстислав Ростропович и многие другие выдающиеся мастера. Сегодня, как и прежде, в атмосфере высочайшей требовательности и искренней любви к музыке в консерватории трудятся педагоги, бережно передающие традиции русской исполнительской школы новым поколениям студентов. Можно с полной уверенностью сказать, что мечта Николая Рубинштейна сбылась: выпускников Московской консерватории ждут на лучших сценах, а их искусство служит приумножению славы России! В этот праздничный день искренне желаю студентам, выпускникам и всему коллективу консерватории вдохновения, неиссякаемой энергии и реализации всех творческих планов. Пусть музыка, рождённая в этих стенах, всегда звучит проникновенно, трогая души миллионов слушателей». Работа Правительства: Театр. Музыка. body: Xi charts course for high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation, Chinese FM says-Xinhua Xi charts course for high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation, Chinese FM says Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-14 00:15:00 BEIJING, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping's attendance at the BRICS summit in India is of strategic significance for steering the high-quality development for greater BRICS cooperation, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said Sunday. The South Asian trip also promoted strength through unity among Global South countries, Wang said. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks while briefing reporters on Xi's visit to India to attend the 18th BRICS Summit on Saturday and Sunday. First, Xi's visit injected fresh impetus into BRICS cooperation. The Chinese president summed up the development of BRICS over the past two decades with three key phrases: self-reliance and self-strengthening, standing together through wind and rain, and fruitful outcomes, Wang said. Standing at a new historical starting point, Xi called on BRICS countries to be pioneers in advancing innovation-driven development, upholding peace and stability, facilitating mutual learning between civilizations, and reforming and improving global governance, Wang said. In 2027, the BRICS will usher in its fourth "China Year." Xi announced that China will take this opportunity to work with all parties to build consensus, open up prospects for the future, and embark on the third golden decade of BRICS cooperation, Wang said. Second, Xi's visit empowered the Global South, Wang said. Xi put forward four important proposals to strengthen the Global South: jointly defending the rule of law in international affairs and ensuring that international law and international rules are applied to all; holding high the banner of multilateralism and upholding the authority and role of the United Nations; staying committed to a people-centered development philosophy and striving to deliver on the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development; and jointly advancing security governance and tackling both traditional and nontraditional security threats, Wang said. Focusing on the new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation, Xi proposed initiatives including the BRICS initiative of AI-empowered new industrialization, the open source and inclusive AI initiative, the digital industry cooperation initiative, and the intelligent manufacturing cooperation initiative, Wang said. Third, Xi's visit guided China-India relations, Wang said. Xi and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi conducted a candid and in-depth exchange of views on strategic, long-term and directional issues concerning China-India relations, Wang said, noting that the most important consensus they reached was that China and India should be partners. The Chinese president said China and India can draw on each other's strengths, support one another, help each other succeed and pursue common development, Wang said. The leaders of the two countries agreed to jointly maintain peace and tranquility in border areas, while the two countries will support each other as rotating chair of the BRICS, Wang said. ■ Xi charts course for high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation, Chinese FM says

body: Major trade fair deepens consensus on global services cooperation-Xinhua Major trade fair deepens consensus on global services cooperation Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-13 22:36:15 Visitors tour the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) at Shougang Park in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 12, 2026. The 2026 CIFTIS is open to the general public from Sept. 12 to 13. (Xinhua/Zhang Chenlin) BEIJING, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS), held in the Chinese capital of Beijing from Sept. 9 to 13, has deepened consensus on strengthening cooperation in the services sector. Fruitful outcomes were achieved during the fair, which saw the holding of nearly 100 conferences and forums as well as over 100 matchmaking and promotion events, said Zhu Guangyao, an official with China's commerce ministry, at a press conference on the conclusion of the fair. Zhu said the successful event sent a clear signal to the world that China will unswervingly expand high-standard opening up and promote high-quality development. According to Lu Huiling, deputy head and spokesperson of the Beijing municipal commerce bureau, the 2026 CIFTIS has achieved more than 1,200 outcomes in seven categories, effectively promoting resource matching, exchanges and cooperation. As the guest country of honor, Norway signed six cooperation agreements with Chinese enterprises and institutions, she said. This year's fair gained rising popularity, drawing an increasing number of visitors to Shougang Park, the event's venue. As of Sunday noon, the core areas of CIFTIS had received nearly 420,000 visits, up 36.6 percent year on year, Lu said. Visitors tour the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) at Shougang Park in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 13, 2026. The 2026 CIFTIS concluded in Beijing on Sunday. (Photo by Liang Jiayuan/Xinhua) Themed "Global Services, Shared Prosperity," the event saw more than 1,800 enterprises exhibit on site, including over 470 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry-leading enterprises. Exhibitions showcased new technologies, solutions, and achievements in services trade, including information and communication, fintech, digital and intelligent healthcare, smart education, energy conservation and environmental protection. According to Zhu, China will continue to deepen international cooperation in services trade, innovate cooperation models, expand cooperation areas, tap cooperation potential, align with the development strategies and cooperation initiatives of various countries, and use major exhibition platforms such as CIFTIS as a bridge to promote mutually beneficial cooperation among countries. "We welcome service enterprises from around the world to explore the Chinese market and share the opportunities of China's super-large market," Zhu said. Trade in services, a key component of international trade, is playing an increasingly important role in driving global economic growth and industrial upgrading. According to guest speakers at the fair, services are becoming an increasingly integral part of global supply chains, supporting not only production but also design, management, logistics, and distribution. The CIFTIS, as one of the world's largest platforms for trade in services, embodies a vision of openness, cooperation and shared development, according to Burundian President Evariste Ndayishimiye, who also serves as the current chairperson of the African Union. By bringing together governments, international organizations and investors, this fair provides a unique opportunity for exchange, sharing of experiences, and the creation of opportunities, he said. ■ You may like Two teachers devote their lives to a remote mountain village Chinese dance drama "A Dream of Red Mansions" makes U.S. debut in New York A glimpse of Yinxu Museum in Anyang, China's Henan EcoChina | A scenic drive into Hainan's rainforest InPics | Shougang Park reinvents itself as vibrant urban destination Pinglu Canal to become operational on Sept. 16 More from GLOBALink BRICS cooperation: Shared prosperity for half of world's population What BRICS family saw at CIFIT: markets, investment and new partnerships How AI is reshaping everyday services at CIFTIS

body: China broadens tourism appeal with easier travel, richer experiences-Xinhua China broadens tourism appeal with easier travel, richer experiences Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-14 12:51:30 Visitors tour the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) at Shougang Park in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong) BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- For an overseas visitor to Beijing, a day of sightseeing no longer has to end at the Forbidden City or the Great Wall. The city's tourism map is expanding. In the outer districts, a countryside stay can be paired with a scenic train ride or a visit to a major scientific facility, while old towns and modern industries are making their way onto international visitors' itineraries. "China offers not only inspiring historical landscapes but also innovative tourism products and services," said Australian tour operator Manuel Condoleon, adding that his clients are increasingly seeking personalized experiences and homestays. Safety, he noted, is another major advantage drawing international visitors to China. That changing landscape was at the heart of the 2026 World Conference on Tourism Cooperation and Development, held during the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) in Beijing. The conference released 121 detailed scoring criteria supporting ISO 11778 on tourism city brand evaluation. Led by the World Tourism Cities Federation (WTCF), ISO 11778 is the world's first international standard dedicated specifically to evaluating tourism city brands. The new scoring rules build on eight top-level indicators and 53 secondary indicators in the standard, covering areas including tourism resources, infrastructure, service convenience, environmental sustainability, safety, stakeholder evaluation, visitor numbers and financial performance. Dai Bin, president of the China Tourism Academy, said quantitative indicators such as visitor numbers and tourism revenue remain important, but greater weight should be given to how tourists actually experience a destination. A report released during CIFTIS by the institute of international trade in services under the Chinese Academy of International Trade and Economic Cooperation pointed to a similar challenge. It found that growing inbound visitor numbers have yet to be fully converted into tourism spending in China, and that among five dimensions examined, improvements in service quality and visitor experience had the strongest effect on unlocking further growth potential. Across China, efforts are underway to make travel easier while offering visitors more reasons to stay longer and explore more deeply. A child views the scenery of the Great Wall via a VR device at the themed exhibition area for culture and tourism services during the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) at Shougang Park in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Zheng Huansong) SMOOTHER JOURNEYS For international visitors, planning a trip to Beijing can now start long before arrival. A new digital platform, launched by China Daily and the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism during the conference, brings itinerary planning, flight and train bookings, accommodation, translation, transport, currency conversion and online payment services into one place. International visitors can access it either by visiting www.chinabound.cn/beijing or searching for "ChinaBound" in Alipay. "Beijing is leveraging digital technologies to enhance tourism services and improve the experience of international visitors," said Zheng Fang, deputy director of the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism. The platform also features an AI assistant that answers questions and helps plan trips, serving as a digital guide for first-time visitors. At CIFTIS, exhibitors showcased AI-powered multilingual guides and AR translation glasses designed to make on-the-go communication easier. One system used at the tourism conference displayed real-time translations directly in the wearer's field of vision, while other devices supported real-time translation in dozens of languages. "Language used to be the biggest problem, but it is increasingly less of an issue," Condoleon said. "Technology, including AI, has made it much easier for today's travelers to get around China than it was ten or twenty years ago." Chinese online travel platform Trip.com Group said inbound visitors still encounter difficulties with language, understanding tourism products, coordinating itineraries and dealing with unexpected situations, with problems during a trip particularly prominent. The company has helped more than 170 scenic spots launch multilingual websites and deployed multilingual self-service ticket machines at nearly 300 attractions. Using AI, it also provides product information in up to 16 languages for more than 8,000 scenic spots and 450,000 hotels. The demand keeps climbing. Latest data shows that foreign nationals made nearly 61.29 million border crossings in the first eight months this year, up 19.5 percent year on year. Visa-free entries by foreign nationals totaled 23.72 million, accounting for 77.6 percent of all inbound foreign visitors to China, up 26.8 percent year-on-year. Tourists from Egypt take selfies in front of the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests at the Temple of Heaven Park in Beijing, capital of China, July 28, 2026. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong) BEYOND THE LANDMARKS The World Tourism Cities Development Report (2025-2026), also released at the conference, ranked Beijing fifth among 100 global tourism cities, behind New York, Tokyo, Paris and London. The remaining top 10 spots were rounded out by Shanghai, Hong Kong, Milan, Istanbul and Dubai. For Beijing, expanding inbound tourism increasingly means giving visitors more choices beyond its best-known landmarks. A scenic train route offers another way to explore Yanqing in the city's northwest. In Huairou, visitors can see major national scientific facilities and a science city, while Shunyi offers a look at modern logistics and service industries. "Beijing has not only history and the past, but also the present and the future," Dai said. He said inbound tourism in the new era should go beyond a single historical narrative and give overseas visitors greater access to contemporary life, technological innovation and popular culture, alongside traditional attractions. Foreign visitors are already traveling farther from Beijing's urban core. Platform data show that overseas tourists have booked homestays in all 10 of Beijing's suburban districts this year, with bookings in Yanqing up more than 50 percent year-on-year and in Huairou up 14 percent. Courtyard homestays have proven especially popular, with bookings from foreign visitors rising 50 percent. The trend extends well beyond the capital. First-tier and new-first-tier cities remain the main gateways for foreign visitors, but more travelers are now venturing inland to smaller destinations. Data from homestay platform Tujia showed that Gansu, Xinjiang, Ningxia, Qinghai and Shanxi were among the provincial-level regions recording the fastest growth in homestay bookings by foreign tourists in the first half of the year. "The travel footprint of inbound visitors is expanding, and their pace is slowing down, as they take time to seek out more authentic cultural experiences, like browsing local markets, trying street food, exploring ancient architecture or trying their hand at intangible cultural heritage crafts," said Ma Yiliang, vice president of the China Tourism Academy. China's tourism development plan for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) calls for further improving services for inbound travelers, building tourism networks around major gateway cities and developing products centered on areas ranging from traditional crafts and historical culture to technology, study tours, festivals and shopping. body: World's first museum devoted to prehistoric flying reptiles opens in NW China's Xinjiang-Xinhua World's first museum devoted to prehistoric flying reptiles opens in NW China's Xinjiang Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-14 09:43:15 Visitors view pterosaurs replicas at a science museum in Hami, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Sept. 13, 2026. (Photo by Polat Niyaz/Xinhua) URUMQI, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- A science museum focused on pterosaurs, a winged reptile closely related to dinosaurs, opened on Sunday in Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region in northwest China. The world's first of its kind, this museum is located in a national geopark in Xinjiang's Hami region, a location renowned for abundant pterosaur fossil discoveries. With an exhibition area of about 4,600 square meters, the Hami Pterosaur Museum consists of six oval-shaped halls in a staggered layout. Seen from above, it resembles a clutch of pterosaur eggs resting in the desert. This video screenshot shows a science museum focused on pterosaurs in Hami, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Sept. 12, 2026. (Photo by Zhang Xuhui/Xinhua) Fossils on display include specimens recovered during more than two decades of rescue excavations by researchers from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). Also on display are the world's first 3D preserved fossilized pterosaur eggs and embryos, along with large pterosaur specimens making their public debut. This is the first time all of these specimens have been displayed together. The exhibits present a panoramic recreation of pterosaur life and evolution during the Cretaceous period roughly 130 million years ago, the museum said. Xu Xing, head of the CAS institute, said the museum not only highlights China's leading role in global pterosaur research but also offers the public a window to experience scientific discovery up close and appreciate the wonders of ancient life. ■ You may like Two teachers devote their lives to a remote mountain village Chinese dance drama "A Dream of Red Mansions" makes U.S. debut in New York A glimpse of Yinxu Museum in Anyang, China's Henan EcoChina | A scenic drive into Hainan's rainforest InPics | Shougang Park reinvents itself as vibrant urban destination Pinglu Canal to become operational on Sept. 16 More from GLOBALink BRICS cooperation: Shared prosperity for half of world's population What BRICS family saw at CIFIT: markets, investment and new partnerships How AI is reshaping everyday services at CIFTIS

body: Across China: In Yan'an, visitors see how CPC turns history into progress-Xinhua Across China: In Yan'an, visitors see how CPC turns history into progress Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-14 14:03:00 YAN'AN, Shaanxi, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- When Ivan Racan was still a boy, not yet 10 years old, his father returned to Croatia from China in 1981, carrying with him a sanxian -- a traditional three-stringed Chinese instrument. The instrument hung on the wall of his childhood room, bringing a piece of distant China into his everyday life. More than 40 years later, Racan came across a similar instrument at a museum in Shanghai. He was struck by the realization that while the sanxian had remained much the same, China itself had transformed dramatically. For Racan, a member of the Croatian Parliament and son of former Croatian Prime Minister Ivica Racan, the instrument connects two periods of China's modern history. His father had visited China as an official of the former Yugoslavia. When he returned, he brought back stories that captured the early days of a transformation, one that would go on to reshape the country over the decades to come, Racan said. Decades later, Racan visited China himself and made a point to travel to Yan'an, which was once a center of the Chinese revolution. During his journey through the city in northwest China's Shaanxi Province, he encountered a modern country that would have been difficult to imagine in 1981. On Sept. 10, more than 200 representatives from over 50 countries attended a thematic briefing in Yan'an. Through stories of rural development, ecological conservation, industrial upgrading and cultural heritage protection, the event demonstrated how the Communist Party of China (CPC) has translated long-term goals into changes that reach communities and ordinary families. "This is something that has to be commended, appreciated, studied," Racan told Xinhua. For Petre Danci, a parliamentary advisor at the Office of the Secretary of the Romanian Senate and secretary of the Romania-China Friendship Group within the Alliance for the Union of Romanians, China's transformation is not an inherited memory. It is part of his own life. Danci, who speaks fluent Mandarin, arrived in Beijing in 2011. He studied Chinese at the Capital University of Economics and Business before completing bachelor's and master's degrees. During seven years of study and life in Beijing, he experienced China through lectures, friendships and the everyday norms of student life. "Every single time I come to China, I see a lot of development," he said. "Even if I go to a very familiar city, like Beijing, or Shanghai, or some other big cities, I still see the improvement." His latest journey to Yan'an brought him face to face with an earlier chapter of China's history. Danci learned about the period when Yan'an served as a center of the Chinese revolution and said he could still feel the Yan'an spirit in China today. That connection became clearer when he heard about the development of Liangjiahe Village, the technological upgrading of traditional industries and the restoration of environmentally fragile land through years of afforestation. "It takes function, leadership and organization," Danci told Xinhua. He believed China's experience in agriculture, ecological restoration and industrial modernization could offer useful references for Romania. Such experience should not be copied mechanically, he said, but adapted to local conditions through exchanges among people, businesses and governments. Having studied the Chinese language and experienced the country as a student, Danci said he hoped to help strengthen communication between Romania and China. The connection between Yan'an's revolutionary history and China's present-day development was expressed most directly by Leevameng Leebouapao, deputy director general of the Land Department at the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment of Laos. During a visit to Nangou Village in Yan'an, he saw how poverty alleviation, public infrastructure and improvements to the rural environment had changed people's lives. "Socialism creates conditions for equality," he said. "People have equal access to education, healthcare, transport and other public services. China has demonstrated this in practice." What impressed him was that development had not been limited to major cities such as Beijing and Shanghai. Roads, communications networks and public services had also reached rural communities. In Nangou Village, he said, the practical work of the CPC and the government had made life more convenient for villagers and significantly improved their living environment. He added that China's experience in poverty alleviation and improving people's livelihoods deserved to be studied by other developing countries, including Laos. Beneath Pagoda Hill in Yan'an, visitors did not simply listen to stories about the CPC's past, but also to how the spirit formed in Yan'an continues to shape China's development today. ■ Across China: In Yan'an, visitors see how CPC turns history into progress

title: Across China: In Yan'an, visitors see how CPC turns history into progress

body: Feature: U.S. scholar finds harmony with nature in China through Lao Tzu-Xinhua Feature: U.S. scholar finds harmony with nature in China through Lao Tzu Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-14 13:55:00 Misha Tadd, an American scholar of Laozegetics, holds a book launch at the School of Philosophy, Nankai University in north China's Tianjin Municipality, on Nov. 11, 2025. (Xinhua) by Xinhua writers Song Rui and Li Kun TIANJIN, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- For 46-year-old American associate professor of philosophy Misha Tadd, the mountains and rivers in China unfold like living pages from the classic work Tao Te Ching, waiting to be read by those who know how to understand them, rather than just scenery. This summer, Tadd became a special tour guide for his sister, who was visiting China for the first time. Their journey took them from the historical landmarks of Tianjin and Beijing to the rural landscapes of Shanxi Province in north China. Tadd's account of this trip was about much more than sightseeing. It played out like a traveling lecture on Chinese philosopher Lao Tzu's ancient classics, with each landscape revealing a new lesson along the journey. Tadd, who directs the Global Laozegetics Research Center at Nankai University in north China's Tianjin Municipality, has devoted years to studying the Tao Te Ching. In his view, tracing the classics back to their origins and engaging with the very landscape that inspired those philosophical ideas is itself a way of finding harmony with nature, a living encounter with the world that shaped Lao Tzu's way of thinking. TAO ON TOUR As they wandered through the Mazu Temple and the historic Five Great Avenues in Tianjin and stood before the Forbidden City and the Great Wall in Beijing, Tadd showed his sister how China breathes new life into its ancient sites. "Letting old buildings tell their stories on the modern stage, this practice itself embodies the wisdom of 'The Way follows nature' (dao fa zi ran in Chinese)," he said. At the Foguang Temple and Nanchan Temple near Mount Wutai in Shanxi, the unassuming, centuries-old structures inspire another Taoist insight -- "The Sage wears coarse cloth externally, but embraces jade internally." "These temples have survived for a millennium precisely because they are hidden in remote mountains and never sought to glorify themselves," Tadd observed. "Many once-splendid, lavishly decorated palaces have long been lost to history." He reflected that qualities like softness and obscurity, often seen as passive, can nurture the greatest longevity. Traveling to Datong, Shanxi, the landscape opened up to reveal hillsides covered with solar panels, gleaming blue under the sun. Tadd pointed to them as a practical example of "wuwei," often translated as "non-action" or "effortless action." "Using solar energy aligns well with the principle of 'wuwei,'" he explained to his sister. The panels convert sunlight into electricity with minimal disruption to the environment, he noted, a beneficial result of non-interference, especially when compared to the environmental impact of burning wood or coal. But for Tadd, the relevance of "wuwei" extends far beyond solar panels. He sees it as a philosophical corrective to the human-centered thinking that has dominated the West since the Renaissance. While that mindset has driven scientific and social progress, it has also diminished humanity's sense of humility before the cosmos, a humility that Tadd believes is urgently needed today. "As science and technology advance, we seem to be escaping the constraints of nature," he said. "But solving small problems, like protecting ourselves from the cold or heat, has created bigger ones, like climate change." The Tao Te Ching, he argues, offers a timely reminder: respect nature's rhythms, and learn to live with the universe rather than against it. "On one hand, we need to reduce our energy consumption," he said. "On the other, we need to produce energy in a way that follows nature's course -- in a 'wuwei' way." ROOTS OF REVELATION These insights often bring Tadd back to his first encounter with the Tao Te Ching. At 14, growing up in a remote village in western Massachusetts, he found an English translation of the classics in his local library. "It was a special edition -- each page of English translation was accompanied by a black-and-white photo of China's natural scenery, with the original Chinese text written in brushstroke over the images." The beauty mesmerized the boy, who had always been enchanted by the forests and mountains. "The book describes the relationship between humans and the universe in a subtle way. It resonated with me deeply," Tadd said. Tadd began learning Chinese, determined to draw closer to the ancient philosophy. As a junior in college, he chose to study in Xi'an, the ancient capital of northwest China's Shaanxi Province -- a decision that set him on a path to a lifetime of studying Chinese culture. Tadd finds that many of Lao Tzu's ideas stem from observations of China's unique geography that still resonate today. "Xi'an is in the Yellow River basin. In such an environment, you cannot ignore the power of water, because the river was once so difficult to control," he said. Lao Tzu's idealization of water's softness, adaptability, and compliance is likely linked to these regional characteristics. By immersing themselves in such landscapes, ancient philosophers could more easily elevate local observations into universal principles about the cycles of yielding and unity in the cosmos, Tadd added. HARMONY IN ACTION Though the Tao Te Ching contains only about 5,000 characters, its concise verses carry profound meaning. It has found a global audience and become a source of cross-civilizational philosophy. This very phenomenon inspired Tadd to pioneer the field of "Global Laozegetics." In 2022, he published "The Complete Bibliography of Laozi Translations: A Global Laozegetics Reference," which cataloged 2,052 translations in 97 languages. Today, the special collection at Nankai University's Global Laozegetics Research Center houses over 340 translations, a testament to the long and colorful history of cultural exchanges between China and the world. Tadd champions experiential learning over purely academic research, convinced that the Tao Te Ching's legacy has a profound connection with living people and their stories and that within those natural landscapes, one can best appreciate the unfettered spirit of the Tao. As more foreign students come to study in China, Tadd offers this advice: "Beyond experiencing the rapid technological development in big cities, they should also go to the countryside, to the mountains, even to the desert, to feel China's millennia-old beauty and the friendliness of its ordinary people." He hopes international visitors will recognize China's environmental strides over the past two decades. "Environmental degradation knows no borders," he said. "Seeing China's progress, I think, can inspire people elsewhere to embrace sustainability." The wisdom of the Tao Te Ching has become inseparable from Tadd's own character. "In China, I try to be like water, taking the shape of my surroundings, but not as a disguise or a loss of self. It's about adapting while staying true to who I am," he said. ■ Misha Tadd, an American scholar of Laozegetics at Nankai University, attends an event related to Laozegetics in Luyi, central China's Henan Province, on April 3, 2026. (Xinhua) Feature: U.S. scholar finds harmony with nature in China through Lao Tzu

title: Feature: U.S. scholar finds harmony with nature in China through Lao Tzu

body: Across China: Echoing across battlefields and generations, bugle evokes Long March memories 90 years on-Xinhua Across China: Echoing across battlefields and generations, bugle evokes Long March memories 90 years on Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-14 13:29:45 This photo taken on Sept. 8, 2026 shows the historic bugle score donated by Luo Guangmao (L) and a bugle mouthpiece he once used, both displayed at the Ninghua Revolutionary Memorial Museum in Ninghua County in southeast China's Fujian Province. (Xinhua/Zheng Huansong) FUZHOU, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- For many visitors to Ninghua County in southeast China's Fujian Province, the journey begins with a historic bugle score. Once used by the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army, the score now sits silently in a display case at the Ninghua Revolutionary Memorial Museum, its yellowed pages evoking the stirring calls that echoed across battlefields more than nine decades ago. In an era of limited technology, bugles played an essential role in military communications. Described as a "codebook" for troops, the exhibited booklet contains more than 340 pieces of bugle music, covering the Red Army's daily routines, training, and combat commands. "It is the most complete surviving Red Army bugle score formally published in China," said Yang Liting, a museum docent, highlighting its value in research on the Red Army's revolutionary history. Behind this precious artifact lies the story of a Red Army soldier's commitment to the revolutionary cause. Luo Guangmao joined the Red Army in the early 1930s. Selected as a bugler for his powerful voice, he was sent to a military school for systematic training. Upon graduation, he received a copy of the bugle score from the school and promised to protect it as he would his own life. In 1934, Luo was wounded in battle and later lost contact with the main force. Fearing the score might fall into enemy hands, he secretly made his way home, entrusted it to his mother, and then left to evade enemy capture. After the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949, when Luo sought to retrieve the score, his aging mother could no longer remember where she had hidden it. Not knowing the score's whereabouts had long weighed on the veteran soldier. It was not until 1974 that Luo discovered a package while dismantling the family's granary. "He burst into tears the moment he saw the score wrapped in layers of cloth and oil paper," Yang said. Finally, Luo fulfilled the promise he had made as a young bugler. He donated the score to the museum, helping preserve the memory of the Red Army and the contributions of Ninghua soldiers in the Long March. During the Long March, an epic 1934-1936 military trek that broke through the siege of the Kuomintang (Nationalist Party) forces, the Red Army soldiers braved raging rivers, frigid mountains, and arid grasslands, with some marching as far as 12,500 kilometers. More than 6,000 people from Ninghua joined the Long March, many dying amid fierce battles against enemy forces. Only 58 reached the destination in northwest China, data from local authorities showed. The sacrifices are not forgotten. Efforts are underway in Ninghua to keep the history alive, and the bugle remains one of the most vivid links to that past. Since the early 1990s, Xia Chufa, a resident of Quanshang Town in Ninghua, has devoted himself to collecting revolutionary artifacts, especially bugles. To date, the 70-year-old has traveled to more than 20 provinces nationwide and handled over 20,000 items. In 2018, Xia built a dedicated museum for his collections with financial support from the local government and over 10 million yuan (about 1.5 million U.S. dollars) of self-raised funds. The museum now houses more than 1,500 bugles of different types. "It's something that I must do, even if it means going without food or drink," he said. Asked why he keeps collecting bugles, Xia offers a simple answer. "I just want those who have never seen these things to have a place to see them. I don't want future generations to forget our difficult past." Fortunately, young people are taking up the bugle, as the bugler system continues in the military today, to carry forward the revolutionary spirit and boost morale. Zhang Jiahao, 24, is a bugler with the Ninghua unit of the Chinese People's Armed Police Force. After struggling three years ago with high notes he could barely produce, he is now passing on his skills to newcomers. Meanwhile, Zhang also serves as a guide at the Ninghua Revolutionary Memorial Museum. He feels a sense of responsibility to share stories of Red Army soldiers who once charged forward at the sound of bugle calls with a growing number of visitors, as this year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. "Standing beside the bugle score that a veteran bugler vowed to protect with his life, how could we not sound the bugle today?" Zhang said. ■ Across China: Echoing across battlefields and generations, bugle evokes Long March memories 90 years on

title: Across China: Echoing across battlefields and generations, bugle evokes Long March memories 90 years on

body: Erdogan to visit Syria soon: Turkish FM-Xinhua Erdogan to visit Syria soon: Turkish FM Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-14 05:46:30 Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan (L) and Syrian foreign affairs chief Asaad Hassan al-Shibani attend a joint press conference in Damascus, Syria, Sept. 13, 2026. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan will visit Syria soon as Damascus and Ankara move to deepen political and economic cooperation, Fidan said Sunday. (Photo by Ammar Safarjalani/Xinhua) DAMASCUS, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan will visit Syria soon as Damascus and Ankara move to deepen political and economic cooperation, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Sunday. Preparations were underway to create suitable conditions for the visit, Fidan said at a joint press conference in Damascus with Syrian foreign affairs chief Asaad Hassan al-Shibani after their meeting, according to Syria's state-run SANA news agency. During their meeting, the two officials discussed strengthening bilateral ties and activating a high-level joint committee spanning political, diplomatic, economic and security cooperation, as well as energy, education, culture and refugee returns. Shaibani said the committee would operate under joint leadership, hold regular meetings, and include a permanent secretariat and specialized sectoral committees to follow up on decisions. For his part, Fidan said the two countries were setting up mechanisms to facilitate business and investment, covering financing, visas, work permits, and certification, noting strong Turkish investor interest in energy and textiles. Relations between Damascus and Ankara have expanded rapidly since the fall of the former Syrian government in December 2024. ■ Erdogan to visit Syria soon: Turkish FM

title: Erdogan to visit Syria soon: Turkish FM

body: Trump's Irish unification remarks draw opposition from Britain-Xinhua Trump's Irish unification remarks draw opposition from Britain Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-14 05:14:15 People walk out of a branch of Bank of Ireland in Dublin, Ireland, on March 1, 2021. (Xinhua) LONDON, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- The remarks of U.S. President Donald Trump on the unification of Ireland and Britain's Northern Ireland have sparked strong opposition from Britain. During a two-day visit to Ireland, Trump said on Saturday he would "love to see" the unification of Ireland and Britain's Northern Ireland. "President Trump is shooting from the hip as usual, just like he did with Greenland and Canada becoming the 51st state," said Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch on X on Saturday. She added that "Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom." "I disagree with President Trump," said Reform UK leader Nigel Farage on X the same day, "Northern Ireland is a proud and integral part of the United Kingdom." ■ You may like Two teachers devote their lives to a remote mountain village Chinese dance drama "A Dream of Red Mansions" makes U.S. debut in New York A glimpse of Yinxu Museum in Anyang, China's Henan EcoChina | A scenic drive into Hainan's rainforest InPics | Shougang Park reinvents itself as vibrant urban destination Pinglu Canal to become operational on Sept. 16 More from GLOBALink BRICS cooperation: Shared prosperity for half of world's population What BRICS family saw at CIFIT: markets, investment and new partnerships How AI is reshaping everyday services at CIFTIS

body: Meeting between Iran, Gulf states scheduled for Monday in Oman postponed-Xinhua Meeting between Iran, Gulf states scheduled for Monday in Oman postponed Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-14 05:16:15 This photo taken on June 20, 2026 shows the Strait of Hormuz near Khasab, a small town in northern Oman. (Xinhua/Wen Xinnian) MUSCAT/TEHRAN, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- A meeting between Iran and Gulf states scheduled to take place in the Omani city of Salalah on Monday has been postponed, according to a social media post by Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi on Sunday. "In the interests of consensus the regional meeting set for tomorrow in Salalah has been postponed," Al Busaidi said on X. "We remain committed to fostering dialogue that supports stability and lasting cooperation in our region," he added. Confirming the meeting's deferral in an interview with Iran's official news agency IRNA, Mohammad Ali Bak, director general of the Persian Gulf at the Iranian Foreign Ministry, said it was postponed to another date at some regional countries' requests and based on a joint decision by Iran and Oman. The official stressed that Iran is in close consultations with Oman to ensure the necessary arrangements and coordination regarding the appropriate time for holding the meeting. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei announced on Friday that Gulf littoral states' foreign ministers were scheduled to meet in Oman on Monday to exchange views on regional issues, including the Iran-Oman talks on designating safe routes in the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking to Al Jazeera on Saturday, Baghaei said the gathering would "hopefully" be attended by foreign ministers from Gulf states as well as Iran and Iraq. ■ You may like Two teachers devote their lives to a remote mountain village Chinese dance drama "A Dream of Red Mansions" makes U.S. debut in New York A glimpse of Yinxu Museum in Anyang, China's Henan EcoChina | A scenic drive into Hainan's rainforest InPics | Shougang Park reinvents itself as vibrant urban destination Pinglu Canal to become operational on Sept. 16 More from GLOBALink BRICS cooperation: Shared prosperity for half of world's population What BRICS family saw at CIFIT: markets, investment and new partnerships How AI is reshaping everyday services at CIFTIS

body: 3rd cluster munitions review conference opens in Laos-Xinhua 3rd cluster munitions review conference opens in Laos Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-14 13:25:00 VIENTIANE, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- The third Review Conference of the Convention on Cluster Munitions officially opened on Monday in Lao capital Vientiane, bringing together delegations and senior officials globally, as well as representatives of international organizations and relevant sectors. The conference, chaired by Lao Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Thongsavanh Phomvihane, is being held from Monday to Friday, Lao News Agency reported on Monday. The conference is particularly significant for Laos, one of the countries most heavily affected by cluster munitions. Its hosting underscores the government's commitment to international peace and security under the Convention on Cluster Munitions, while highlighting its continued efforts to address the country's legacy of unexploded ordnance. Laos has played an active role in the convention process from the early drafting stages through the adoption of the convention. The government has incorporated the convention's objectives into its national strategic framework, Safe Path Forward III (2021-2030), to support the effective implementation of international commitments at the national level. ■ 3rd cluster munitions review conference opens in Laos

body: As Mid-Autumn Festival nears, mooncakes make their annual return - Chinadaily.com.cn WS6aa3c084e4b06d4aa055d9ca China Edition | Global Edition | ASIA | 中文 China Latest Society Innovation Education Cross-Strait HK/Macao Health Environment Military Video World Asia-Pacific Americas Europe Middle East Africa Business Policies Companies Industries Technology China Up-close China Data Motoring Video Culture Art Music and Theater Film and TV Books Heritage Events and Festivals People Cultural Exchange Video Photo Gallery Fashion Health Travel News City Tours Guides and Tips My Footprints Around the World Features Photo Video Food Sports Soccer Basketball Volleyball Tennis Golf Track and field Swimming Motor China Stars Opinion Cartoons Editorials Global Lens We Comment Columnists Global Views Chinese Perspectives Opinion Line Regional Newspaper China Daily PDF China Daily E-Paper China Daily Global PDF China Daily Global E-Paper Mobile CULTURE News Heritage Art Film Theater Fashion Cultural Exchange Books Photo Video HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE 中文 CULTURE News Heritage Art Film Theater Fashion Cultural Exchange Books Photo Video Home / Culture / China Vibes As Mid-Autumn Festival nears, mooncakes make their annual return Classic, time-honored fillings still draw loyal customers despite a growing array of modern alternatives By Chen Nan | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 06:50 Share - WeChat Ding Shumin, a Beijing native in her 60s, stood at the counter of a pastry shop in Beijing, carefully selecting mooncakes. One for herself, another for a relative, a few for friends — and some for her grandson. By the time she left the shop, Ding had packed about 20. She could have chosen chocolate, durian and some other contemporary flavors. Instead, she stuck to the taste she has loved since childhood: wuren, a traditional filling made with nuts and seeds. "When I was little, eating mooncakes was one of the things I looked forward to most at Mid-Autumn Festival," Ding said. "Wuren was always my favorite. Even now, I still have to buy some." The packaging of the mooncakes invoked as much nostalgia as the taste. Five mooncakes were first bundled in brown kraft paper, then wrapped in bright red paper bearing the shop's name and the flavor in black calligraphy, before being tied with coarse twine. There was no elaborate gift box — just a humble wrapping that has survived from another era. With Mid-Autumn Festival around the corner on Sept 25, old-fashioned mooncakes are a familiar sight in Beijing, and bakeries are competing for attention with their increasingly inventive flavors. For Li Baozhi, who is in his 50s, has been in the trade for decades and now works with the pastry shop of Ya'er Liji, a time-honored halal food brand known for traditional Beijing flavors, the appeal of the traditional varieties lies in their simplicity. Staff members at the pastry shop of Ya'er Liji display traditional-mooncakes in Beijing on Thursday. WANG ZHUANGFEI/CHINA DAILY Li began learning to make mooncakes when he was about 20 years old. He remembers the earliest versions as plain, firm and crumbly. "The oldest style may have been made simply with sugar, oil and flour," Li said. "You put the mooncake into a square mold, pressed it flat, knocked it out of the mold and then baked it." Today, Li makes traditional fillings including wuren, black sesame, red bean and jujube paste, which he said are most popular among buyers. The pastry is also distinctly different from the soft, syrupy crust of Cantonese-style mooncakes. "Cantonese-style mooncakes feature a lot of filling and thin skin, while Beijing-style ones have thicker, crispy skin and less filling," Li said. Wuren, he added, is particularly popular among older customers. But preserving tradition does not mean freezing it in time. "Although it is traditional, it still has to be improved. Otherwise, it won't work," he said. For Li, mooncakes are part of the rhythm of everyday Chinese life — much like dumplings at Spring Festival and zongzi, or sticky rice dumplings, during Dragon Boat Festival. A mooncake that costs just a few yuan can carry more meaning than an expensive gift box, he noted. That down-to-earth quality may be precisely what gives traditional mooncakes staying power. In the past, mooncakes were a precious seasonal treat because food was less abundant. Today, they have to compete with a seemingly endless menu of alternatives — including flavors that earlier generations could hardly have imagined. "The sales were even stronger in the past, because there was less choice," Li said. "But now people have more options — you can eat mooncakes, or hairy crabs instead." Yet the ritual has proved difficult to replace. At the bakery where customer Ding shopped, several thousand mooncakes are sold daily, according to Ding Shilong, the restaurant's culinary director. At the busiest point before the festival, sales can climb to 10,000 or even 20,000 pieces a day. In nearby Qianmen, a historic district in central Beijing, 53-year-old Zhai Guangjun runs another traditional bakery tucked inside a hutong. He started selling mooncakes about a month before the festival, with most customers coming from the neighborhood. For many, Zhai said, buying old-fashioned mooncakes is less about novelty than memory — a small edible link to childhood and to the annual promise of family reunions. Mooncake fillings vary widely across China, from Beijing's traditional wuren and jujube pastes to Shanghai's savory fresh meat fillings and the rich lotus seed paste in Guangdong province. The same tension between tradition and novelty plays out elsewhere in China too. On Sept 8, Russian influencer Marina Maloy, who lives in Shanghai, posted a video of herself sampling mooncakes on Nanjing East Road. Alongside the city's classic fresh meat mooncakes, she tried newer versions flavored with fermented red bean curd sauce, shrimp and crab roe (the rich, golden substance found inside a crab). After sampling her way through the mooncakes, Maloy said the experience gave her a glimpse of people's "respect for tradition and their love of life". [Photo provided to CHINA DAILY] Four years after the BRICS Technical and Vocational Education and Training Cooperation Alliance was set up, it has grown into a platform that mirrors the technical and vocational education and training priorities of each member country. As such, it offers a space for policy dialogue, knowledge exchange and joint capacity-building. The alliance, which has 97 institutions as its members and is managed by the China Education Association for International Exchange in Beijing, translates high-level BRICS consensus into grassroots people-to-people collaboration, said Yang Jun, vice-president and secretary-general of the association. Its work has been acknowledged in summit documents from the 14th to the 17th BRICS summits. Most recently, the declaration of the 13th BRICS Ministers of Education Meeting in Bhubaneswar, India, adopted on Aug 7, highlighted its work in joint projects, information sharing and collective upgrading of technical and vocational education and training. The alliance adopts a multistakeholder governance model involving governments, industry associations, training institutions and companies, Yang said. This has enabled a series of practical initiatives — policy dialogues, best-practice sharing, faculty exchanges, student engagement and industry-academia matchmaking — and it has steadily expanded its activities, membership and influence, he said. Since 2022, annual hybrid forums have been hosted by each rotating BRICS chair, with sessions held in Beijing, Johannesburg, Moscow, Brasilia and New Delhi. Discussions have focused on skills related to the green economy, sustainable workforce development and inclusive digital transformation for technical and vocational education and training, creating a recurring high-level dialogue channel for practitioners across the member states, Yang said. Youth mobility and skills development form another core pillar. Three sessions of the Rising Star TVET Student Camp have brought together more than 100 young participants from BRICS countries. The program includes keynote speeches, cross-cultural youth panels, corporate site visits and cultural immersion, helping young professionals expand international peer networks and sharpen job-ready competencies, he said. One participant, Fatimah Rashed N. Almahasheer from Saudi Arabia, said the camp "unites youth from diverse backgrounds to share perspectives and brainstorm innovative solutions to shared global challenges". Another participant, Yeaymrokal Kebede Mola from Ethiopia, said the alliance creates opportunities for young people to engage in meaningful dialogue, discuss ideas and collaborate on projects related to important global issues. Goitsemang Itlotleng Maledu of South Africa said BRICS members stand to gain collectively through better infrastructure, trade finance and strengthened science, engineering and technical capacities. To improve teaching quality across the network, the alliance has run 12 online workshops and seminars for faculty members and institutional administrators, Yang said. With the help of 50 international specialists, these sessions have covered digital-resource building, industry-education integration, curriculum design and teaching evaluation, reaching more than 1,000 teaching and managerial staff, he said. Joint research has also become a cornerstone. Last year, the alliance published a report that examined technical and vocational education and training in various countries and the implications for economic development. Work on a second-phase research project began this year, with participation extended to the new BRICS-plus members Ethiopia, Egypt, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates, Yang said. zoushuo@chinadaily.com.cn Photos Africa eyes initiative in disease control US marks 25 years since 9/11 Chinese robots step into UK spotlight Houthis seize strategic port in Red Sea Immigrant story Dear You touches hearts ECB hikes rates again but remains cautious on future path World in Focus Cultural ambassador Asia Focus + Toxic haze chokes lungs Indonesia's man-made arboreal bridges offer orangutans a lifeline Special Coverage + 2025 A Date with China GMD SCO Summit Cities Tianjin Friends Afar + Livestreamer brings life in Shanxi to Latin America Ties That Bind + Vital pass to boost China-Pakistan trade Top BACK TO THE TOP English 中文 HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper

body: China scales up embodied AI's reach - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS LIFESTYLE CULTURE TRAVEL WATCHTHIS SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL FORUM NEWSPAPER MOBILE Home Business Industries Home / Business / Industries China scales up embodied AI's reach Vast industrial base, dense supply chains boosting robot performance By CHENG YU | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 07:42 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE A young visitor watches a humanoid robot during the 2026 World Robot Conference in Beijing on Aug 19. ZOU HONG/CHINA DAILY Microduck, a robot duck that waddles, carries objects with its beak and skates on tiny wheels, has become an unlikely global AI hit. Priced at disarmingly $399, the gadget drew orders of as many as 10,000 units within days of its launch, with sales topping $2.6 million in the first 24 hours. Interestingly, it was developed by French robotics developer Pollen Robotics, part of New York-based AI platform Hugging Face, but it runs on a chip from China's Rockchip, and is manufactured in China by Shenzhen, Guangdong province-based firm Seeed Studio, according to media reports. Behind the toy-like duck is a much bigger technological shift. The global AI race is moving from models that generate words and images into embodied AI — robots that can perceive, reason and act in the physical world — and China is betting that its vast manufacturing base, dense supply chains and rapidly expanding robot fleet can give it an edge. This transition was on vivid display across Beijing in August. At the 2026 World Robot Conference, 373 companies packed exhibition halls with more than 3,000 products, including 311 debuts. Days later, more than 2,000 robots descended on the World Humanoid Robot Games, where they sprinted, fought, danced and tackled tasks drawn from factories, homes and service industries. Taken together, the events captured a Chinese robotics industry trying to make a crucial transition: from machines that look impressive on stage to machines that can earn their keep on factory floors. For much of the generative-AI boom, the competitive scoreboard was relatively straightforward: advanced semiconductors, computing clusters, foundation models, data and developers. Robots complicate that equation. A humanoid may need a sophisticated AI model, but it also needs motors, reducers, bearings, cameras, tactile sensors, batteries, power electronics, precision-machined joints and hands capable of manipulating objects. All of those components must work together reliably, repeatedly and cheaply. China already operates the world's largest industrial robot market and has spent decades building electronics, electric-vehicle and automation supply chains that can increasingly be redirected toward embodied AI. Components refined for smartphones and cars — cameras, batteries, sensors, motors and power electronics — are now turning up inside robots. Xi Ning, chair professor of robotics and automation at the University of Hong Kong, said at the World Robot Conference that China's gap with the United States in basic robotics theories and methods had shifted from one of "quality" toward one more of "quantity", while parts of China's supply chain had already moved ahead. 1 2 3 Next >>| 1/3 Next Photo Beijing right in your palm As Mid-Autumn Festival nears, mooncakes return Xi calls on BRICS to unite Global South, deepen cooperation Xi attends second day of BRICS summit in New Delhi Xi: China, India can achieve shared growth Xi meets Modi in New Delhi Top BACK TO THE TOP English 中文 HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper

body: Fallacy of 'China Shock 2.0' - Opinion - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Opinion Cartoons Editorials Global Lens We Comment Columnists Global Views Chinese Perspectives Opinion Line Home Opinion / Global Lens Home / Opinion / Global Lens Fallacy of 'China Shock 2.0' By John Gong | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:18 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE MA XUEJING/CHINA DAILY The European Union's threat of a trade war against China — harsher trade measures unless upcoming trade negotiations yield concrete results — builds on the fabricated foundation of a "China Shock 2.0", supported by the EU's roughly €1 billion-a-day ($1.16 billion a day) goods trade deficit with China. "Shock 2.0" is so named because China's integration into global trade after its accession to the WTO in 2001 was portrayed as one that triggered the first "China Shock", when China became a major exporter riding on the back of low-value-added products and low labor costs. "Shock 2.0", however, manifests in exports of high-value-added and high-tech products such as electric vehicles, batteries and solar panels, which appear to upend the manufacturing base in Europe. This theory blames China's industrial policy, surmising that State aid makes Chinese products unfairly cheap for the European market, leading to what they refer to as "dumping" or excess capacity that is squeezing the global market. This theory goes so far as to postulate that China is going to dominate global markets in practically all fields, and that China is a mercantilist state which is not interested in imports, only exports. Let's first get the facts straight. China is definitely interested in imports. In fact, the Chinese government is probably the only government in the entire world that actively promotes imports by going out of its way to help foreign countries and companies to export to China. Every year, China holds the China International Import Expo, or CIIE, in Shanghai, the world's first national-level expo dedicated to imports. As a matter of fact, contrary to the conventional wisdom in Europe, China's imports have increased faster than exports in recent months. For example, in August, imports by China increased by 28.2 percent year-on-year, while its exports increased by 25 percent. State aid by the Chinese government, if it really exists, resulting in dumping is another factual fallacy. First, the subsidy's legality under the WTO framework needs to be carefully examined. The relevant framework outlaws direct government subsidies associated with production and exports; but doesn't outright outlaw subsidies associated with initial R&D and industry infrastructural development in a nascent and emerging industry. In 2011, the European Union itself was found by the WTO to have provided subsidies to Airbus, with the United States pegging the amount at more than $18 billion. Second, alleged subsidy leading to dumping in the European markets borders on total absurdity as prices of Chinese-made cars sold in Europe are much higher than in China. Take Chery Automobile as an example, a highly internationalized company whose exports accounted for nearly 70 percent of its sales in the first half of 2026. For some of Chery's Jaecoo and Omoda cars and SUVs, prices in European markets are substantially higher than those of comparable models in China. If subsidies ever exist, it is actually the other way around, with European consumers subsidizing Chinese consumers. Third, even if the Chinese government has played an instrumental role in initially cultivating the domestic EV market, the impact is still minimal in today's production cost structure. According to a study by Rhodium Group published in February, direct government grants to BYD contributed about $292 per vehicle to its cost advantage, roughly 1 percent of the sticker price of BYD's Seal model in Europe. Geely's corresponding cost advantage is even less, only $64 per vehicle. My citing these numbers by no means implies endorsement of Rhodium, but goes to show that the European Union is barking up the wrong tree. The real reasons behind China's exports are better products, rapid innovation and strategic direction in the face of a profound technological revolution as far as the automobile industry is concerned. The automobile industry is undergoing wholesale electrification. Not only is the market moving toward EVs, consumers are also embracing advanced infotainment features and autonomous driving capabilities, features in which European automakers are lagging far behind. Excess capacity in China is often cited as a major driving force behind the trade imbalance between the EU and China. Nevertheless, the excess capacity issue should be understood in a global context. When the industry is undergoing an electrification revolution, of course some capacities will be in excess and some in great demand. Actually, the real excess capacity is outdated and inefficient — capacity geared toward producing cars that consumers no longer want, such as internal combustion engine vehicles. If politicians in Brussels are still disciples of the free market and free trade, what capacity is in excess and what is not should be determined by the market, should be voted on by consumers with their pocketbooks. The author is a professor at the School of International Trade and Economics, University of International Business and Economics. The views don't necessarily reflect those of China Daily.
