By Erik Nilsson | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 07:11 Share - WeChat A foreign visitor poses with two women in traditional costumes at the Temple of Heaven on June 20. The number of foreign tourists visiting China, and Beijing in particular, hit a record high in 2025. WANG XIN/FOR CHINA DAILY A robot rock band jammed as onlookers snapped photos, and an AI photo booth dressed visitors in traditional Chinese costumes, while AR glasses translated conversations in real time. And a new platform promises to put all of Beijing — visas, subways, shops, temples, and hidden hutong alleyways — in the palm of your hand. This was the scene at Beijing's Shougang Park last week, as the World Conference on Tourism Cooperation and Development 2026 drew representatives from over 50 countries and regions, dozens of cities, international organizations, and cross-border travel companies for a three-day event themed "Smart Tourism, Shared Prosperity". The event's sixth edition, hosted by the World Tourism Cities Federation and co-organized by the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism, concluded on Friday. The event was part of the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services. The writer tries the "smart photo booth" interactive devices at the World Conference on Tourism Cooperation and Development 2026 in Beijing. ERIK NILSSON/CHINA DAILY Expanding outreach A highlight was the launch of China Bound·Beijing, an English-language cultural tourism platform rolled out by China Daily in cooperation with the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism. It includes a website (chinabound.cn/beijing) and dedicated pages on China Bound's Alipay and WeChat mini-programs, offering everything from itinerary planning to inspiring destination profiles and AI-powered field assistance. Zheng Fang, deputy director of the Beijing culture and tourism bureau, describes it as a one-stop gateway for overseas visitors. "Through this platform, we hope to provide our overseas audiences with authoritative, firsthand information and updates about Beijing tourism," Zheng says. "The platform also provides a wide range of information about visas, transportation, shopping, scenic attractions, events, and other aspects of Beijing travel. We hope this will help international visitors plan their trips before coming to Beijing and provide them with comprehensive support throughout the process," she explains. "It's an important step in Beijing's efforts to expand its communications and outreach to international markets actively. We hope our friends overseas will find this platform useful, and that we earn the love and support of visitors from around the world." Joseph Daniel Lema, a professor at the College of Hospitality, the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, hails the platform's potential. "This makes travel easier and more accessible. It saves people time and inconvenience. I think it's going to be a real boon for the future," he says. "It's going to help tell the narrative of Beijing. This is a very ancient, historic city, so there's lots to talk about here; there's lots to learn. This app is going to help do that." Lema notes that the China Bound. Beijing release builds on a broader application introduced earlier this year. What excites him most, he says, is how the platform connects the dots of a traveler's journey — from the moment of inspiration to the final transaction. "Connecting a lot of the services has been a challenge for tourism for a long time. How do we connect everything from transportation to entry to exit, from food and beverage to events and entertainment? This app will be very valuable for a seamless experience," Lema says. He believes its timing is significant. "This is what the new generations coming up want. They're on their phones, and they want a seamless experience ... people want to learn, and this is another channel to bring that all together." It'll help Beijing show its true self to the world, Lema says. "It's going to be a good asset for Beijing, and it also introduces the latest technologies," he says. "Many people don't realize how advanced the technology is here. China Bound is bringing everything together, from initial curiosity and travel searches to deciding where to go, and managing the experience while you're here, then following up and satisfaction, and so on. These apps can have the capabilities to do all of that." 1 2 Next >>| 1/2 Next

body: Xi unveils five initiatives for stronger BRICS - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Latest Home China Latest Xi unveils five initiatives for stronger BRICS Deeper cooperation essential for greater progress, president says By ZHAO JIA in Beijing and MO JINGXI in New Delhi | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 06:55 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE President Xi Jinping delivers a speech while attending the second day of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, on Sunday. YAN YAN/XINHUA President Xi Jinping unveiled five initiatives — covering the areas of artificial intelligence, trade and investment facilitation, digital industry, smart manufacturing, and talent development — to deepen practical cooperation among BRICS countries and bolster the collective strength of the Global South. Addressing the second session of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi as he wrapped up his two-day participation in the gathering on Sunday, Xi stressed that a stronger foundation for cooperation was essential for the expanded grouping to achieve greater progress. He urged BRICS countries to leverage their close ties with emerging markets and Global South countries, pursuing open cooperation for mutual benefit while safeguarding stable and smooth industrial and supply chains. They should foster a larger integrated market, build incubators for innovation, upgrade traditional industries, develop emerging industries and deploy future industries, Xi added. China will be a pioneer in establishing a BRICS AI open source community, and it will support cooperation in developing and applying large language models, hold specialized AI seminars and training courses, and build an open AI ecosystem, Xi said. He proposed a BRICS special economic zone partnership under which countries could set up an intelligent portal, coordinate policies and build a new frontier for open development. China will also host the BRICS Forum on Trade in Services next year to cultivate new drivers of economic and trade cooperation. Furthermore, China will push for the establishment of a BRICS digital ecosystem cloud platform and conduct digital skills training, technological exchanges and industrial alignment to jointly advance the digital economy, Xi said. He expressed the country's readiness to assist fellow BRICS countries in building smart factories and developing standards and norms, jointly promoting manufacturing transformation and upgrading. Xi also proposed a BRICS engineer cultivation alliance for the joint development of engineers and mutual recognition of competency standards. China will launch a BRICS youth exchange program for scientific and technological innovation to cultivate more high-caliber talent. Noting that this year marks the launch of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30), Xi said China will continue to pursue high-quality development, expand high-standard opening-up, implement the Global Development Initiative and advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation to share opportunities and prosper together with other countries. Liu Ying, a researcher at the Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies at Renmin University of China, said that as BRICS marks its 20th anniversary and moves toward its next "golden decade", China's five initiatives respond to the shared development needs of BRICS and the wider Global South. China has offered not just directions for cooperation, but also concrete platforms and mechanisms to implement it, she said, helping BRICS countries expand their international voice while strengthening their own development foundations. Openness and inclusiveness in AI especially matter, Liu said, as open-source cooperation, large-model development and talent training can help Global South countries access and apply AI as a foundational resource for national development — an effort that China's strengths in technology, industry and application can help make possible. China is practicing "developmental multilateralism" — combining capacity building with real development outcomes to help the Global South participate more fully in the new wave of technological and industrial change, and ultimately pushing the global system toward a fairer, more inclusive and balanced order, Liu added. As the Global South, with its collective rise, has become a key driver of world multipolarity, Xi said that to bring stability to the world and make it a better place, BRICS countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, be an active, stabilizing and positive force in international affairs, and advance the well-being of all humanity. He stressed that Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, safeguarding sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs and the peaceful settlement of disputes, to ensure that international law and international rules are applied to all, free from double standards. Xi emphasized the need to uphold multilateralism and the authority and role of the United Nations, and to support multilateral institutions in advancing reform and increasing efficiency. World Trade Organization reform should proceed in the right direction, while the international financial architecture must be reformed and improved to increase developing countries' representation and voice, he added. Global South countries should remain committed to a people-centered development philosophy and strive to deliver on the UN's 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, he said. Addressing shared challenges, Xi said that Global South countries should work together to strengthen security governance, tackle traditional and nontraditional threats, and improve global climate governance. BRICS draws its growing influence from an inclusive approach that respects different development paths and promotes shared economic gains, said Lan Qingxin, director of the BRICS Research Center at the University of International Business and Economics in Beijing. body: President's remarks praised as visionary for BRICS - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Latest Home China Latest President's remarks praised as visionary for BRICS By LIU JIANQIAO in Beijing and XU WEIWEI in Hong Kong | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 07:16 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE President Xi Jinping is warmly welcomed upon his arrival on Saturday at an airport in New Delhi, India, to attend the 18th BRICS Summit at the invitation of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. XIE HUANCHI/XINHUA President Xi Jinping's speeches during the 18th BRICS Summit reflect the wider global community's aspirations for fairness, stability and shared progress, and present a timely and forward-looking vision for strengthening cooperation among BRICS countries and the wider Global South, international experts said. Xi, when attending the second day of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, on Sunday, called for the Global South to jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, safeguard the basic norms of international relations including sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of disputes, and ensure that international law and international rules are applied to all. He also urged support for multilateralism and the upholding of the authority and role of the United Nations. Maarij Farooq, deputy editor-in-chief at Daily Ittehad Media Group and the Pakistan Economic Network, said that Xi's remarks at the 18th BRICS Summit "present a timely and forward-looking vision for strengthening cooperation among BRICS countries and the wider Global South". Farooq said that Xi's emphasis on sovereign equality, multilateralism, international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes reflects the growing demand for a more balanced and representative international system. "At a time of increasing geopolitical uncertainty, President Xi's message is significant because it places dialogue, cooperation and shared development at the center of international relations," Farooq added. Xi, when attending the first day of the BRICS Summit on Saturday, noted that as it marks the 20th anniversary of its establishment, the BRICS countries have actively explored development paths suited to their own national conditions, setting an example of self-strengthening through unity. Xi said that the BRICS countries should deepen mutual understanding through communication and dialogue, properly handle differences, and ensure that BRICS cooperation continues to move forward steadily. "President Xi's remarks reflect that BRICS' solidarity, cooperation and contribution to global peace and progress have deepened during the last 20 years," said Karori Singh, former director of the South Asia Study Centre at the University of Rajasthan in India. Balew Demissie, a senior consultant at the Policy Studies Institute of Ethiopia, said, "President Xi's call for BRICS to be a pioneer of our times speaks to the wider global community's aspirations for fairness, stability and shared progress." Khalid Taimur Akram, executive director of Pakistan Research Center for a Community with Shared Future in Islamabad, said that in his speech, Xi presented a clear vision for the future of BRICS, emphasizing the importance of unity, cooperation and shared development among the Global South countries. "President Xi highlighted peace, development, technological innovation, cultural understanding and better global governance. These are areas that are very important for the future of developing countries," said Akram. Experts also hailed China's dedication to building a fairer and more equitable technology system, which will bring more benefits to the BRICS countries and the broader Global South community. Xi's speech offers a compelling and coherent vision of BRICS as a pioneering force that stands firmly on the right side of history, advancing innovation, peace, mutual civilizational learning, and a fairer global governance system, said Dicky Budiman, a senior researcher at both YARSI University in Indonesia and Griffith University in Australia. If BRICS members build on this platform with active technology-sharing, it has real potential to narrow the digital divide, he added. Victor Raballa in Nairobi, Yang Gao in Toronto contributed to this story. body: Intl sci-tech collaboration urged - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Society Home China Society Intl sci-tech collaboration urged Forum hails innovation partnerships key to advancing global development By WANG XIN in Shanghai | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 07:33 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Global scientists and officials have praised China's advances in science and technology, calling for stronger international collaboration to promote innovation and address common challenges at the 2026 Pujiang Innovation Forum, which concluded on Monday in Shanghai. Co-hosted by the Ministry of Science and Technology and the Shanghai municipal government, the fourday forum focused on basic research and future industries, with discussions covering interdisciplinary research, artificial intelligence for science, biomanufacturing, quantum computing, brain-inspired intelligence, commercial aerospace, nuclear fusion energy and advanced materials. The forum also showcased a wide range of the latest sci-tech achievements made in China, unveiling new innovations in fields such as brain-computer interfaces, next-generation computing, fusion energy, chip manufacturing, life sciences and healthcare. Shanghai Oriental TianSuan Technology Co presented a project aimed at extending intelligent computing capabilities from the ground and into space. The project seeks to gradually build a space-based intelligent service network that could provide computing support for the future development of the digital economy and AI. Startorus Fusion introduced its Compact-Tokamak-based repetitive Reconnection-heated Fusion Reactor-1 (CTRFR-1), a device designed to explore a smaller and potentially more cost-effective approach to producing fusion energy. The company said the reactor uses a domestically developed technology approach that is globally unique and is undergoing technical validation. CARsgen Therapeutics Holdings officially unveiled Satricabtagene Autoleucel Injection (Satri-cel), which it described as the world's first chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy approved to treat a solid tumor. CAR T-cell therapy modifies a patient's immune cells so they can better recognize and attack cancer cells. The forum welcomed South Africa and Hunan province as its guests of honor. Hunan Vice-Governor Liu Yang highlighted the province's achievements in the intelligent audiovisual sector. "We have gathered over 5,000 upstream and downstream enterprises and more than 68,000 industry professionals, focusing on breakthroughs in key core technologies in the intelligent audiovisual field. In 2025, the province's audiovisual industry revenue reached 290 billion yuan ($43.2 billion)," Liu said. Thomas Mtontsi of the National Research Foundation's South African Environmental Observation Network (NRF-SAEON) shared the organization's experience in environmental observation and research at the forum. Making his first visit to China, Mtontsi said he was "incredibly impressed and blown away" by the country's science and technology advances and expressed hope for greater collaboration with Chinese partners. "China is already far ahead of many nations and the sci-tech innovation here is amazing. That's why it's important for us to work with China. Collaborations will help us jointly understand the changes in the environment and how to respond to them. Combining our expertise, we can co-create things to do much more and go further," Mtontsi said. His comments echoed the views of many experts and scholars from around the world, who stressed the growing importance of international sci-tech cooperation in tackling global challenges. At the forum's opening ceremony, UNESCO and Shanghai jointly proposed the establishment of the Global Innovative Cities Alliance, which aims to promote innovation cooperation among cities worldwide and help create an open, inclusive and sustainable future for sci-tech innovation. Janos Kendernay, senior adviser on city diplomacy at Budapest City Hall, said Shanghai and Budapest have developed solid cooperation and partnerships over the past decades in areas including urban planning and mobility. He said he was impressed by Shanghai's progress in science and technology and urban management, and expected the two cities to further strengthen cooperation in innovation and technology. "We appreciate very much the initiative because it also shares our priority, which is how to use technology to make human life better and to build more livable cities for the future," he said. Benoit Dubuis, president of the Swiss Academy of Engineering Sciences, has been visiting China for about 30 years. He said he was always impressed by the rapid pace of sci-tech development in China, as well as the country's large pool of engineers and their ambition, energy, enthusiasm and willingness to pursue innovation. "Almost all the major issues are global, so there is no country, university or city which can address them alone. I'm always insisting on 'trust' between the people with the willingness to work together," Dubuis said. For Hanns-Christoph Naegerl, a professor of experimental physics at the University of Innsbruck in Austria, the most impressive aspect of the forum was the "vibrant research activities" in Shanghai and China, where scientists and researchers are actively advancing science and technology, producing impressive results. Naegerl, whose research focuses on quantum science, said he had witnessed major changes and "very strong" advances in China's quantum science sector over the past decade. He said Chinese scientists and young researchers were open-minded and innovative, with "excellent stamina and endurance on top of being highly qualified". He also valued the "friendly and good" competition with Chinese peers in basic research in quantum science. The forum also strengthened regional cooperation which will support the development of basic research and future industries in Shanghai and across the country. The Major Project of the Yangtze River Delta Joint Fund for Basic Research of the National Natural Science Foundation of China, as well as the joint construction of the Yangtze River Delta Science Data Sharing and Service Platform, were launched at the forum's opening ceremony on Saturday. body: Charting pathways to amplify Global South solidarity - Opinion - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Opinion Cartoons Editorials Global Lens We Comment Columnists Global Views Chinese Perspectives Opinion Line Home Opinion / Global Lens Home / Opinion / Global Lens Charting pathways to amplify Global South solidarity By Endalkachew Sime | China Daily Global | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:07 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE SONG CHEN/CHINA DAILY Rooted in sovereign equality, demand-driven development and mutual benefit, the China-Africa partnership stands as an ever-evolving and exemplary blueprint for advancing the empowerment of the Global South. This framework delivers tangible socioeconomic results while redefining how emerging economies organize collective agency within a landscape marked by fracturing global supply chains, inequitable multilateral financial rules and widening development divides. China has been Africa's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, and the bilateral trade volume exceeded $348 billion in 2025, marking an annual increase of 17.7 percent. The cooperation framework increasingly prioritizes African industrialization, moving beyond simple commodity trade to support local manufacturing, value chain development and job creation. Established in 2000, the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation has delivered successive action plans that have launched thousands of livelihood-focused "small yet beautiful" projects spanning agriculture, healthcare, digital connectivity and vocational training. By 2024, more than 220,000 African professionals had received technical training through Chinese programs, while agricultural technology demonstration centers have boosted food security for millions of rural households across sub-Saharan Africa. Cooperation with China comes without the political conditions that are often associated with Western financial mechanisms. Africa faces growing debt vulnerabilities and an alternative development finance architecture is urgently required. That's why the New Development Bank under the BRICS framework presents a viable alternative financing channel. Since its founding, the NDB has approved over $40 billion in project financing across member and partner states, including multiple sustainable infrastructure initiatives in Egypt, Bangladesh and South Africa. Deepening coordination between FOCAC mechanisms and BRICS financial institutions creates new avenues to scale affordable, long-term capital for African economies and extend comparable opportunities to other Global South regions. At the 18th BRICS Summit held in New Delhi on Sept 12-13, leaders adopted a joint declaration reaffirming their commitment to inclusive global governance and multilateralism, while pledging enhanced cultural and people-to-people exchanges. The summit underscored an agenda centered on improving global governance and fostering sustainable, inclusive global economic growth, while calling for international and regional peace and security. It has amplified the collective voice of the Global South and carries far-reaching implications for Africa. BRICS has expanded significantly in recent years, with Egypt and Ethiopia among the African countries that have joined the group, embedding African perspectives firmly within the group's decision-making processes. The summit's priorities — improving global governance, revitalizing global trade, deepening economic cooperation and strengthening regional security — align closely with core African demands for fairer global trading rules, predictable investment flows and African-led conflict resolution frameworks. The New Delhi summit also provided a timely diplomatic window to draw broader lessons from China-Africa engagement and explore how they could inform broader BRICS+strategy for the collective advancement of the Global South, offering a platform to translate the shared aspirations of developing nations into coordinated, actionable outcomes. And as China is set to take over the BRICS presidency in 2027, the China-Africa partnership will serve as an institutional anchor for the next phase of Greater BRICS cooperation. Looking beyond the summit, a key priority should be advancing coordinated South-South value chain integration. For decades, most Global South economies have remained trapped at the lower end of global production networks, exporting raw materials while importing finished manufactured goods. China-Africa industrial parks and special economic zone partnerships offer a template to break this cycle, supporting local processing capacity to boost export competitiveness. BRICS nations can jointly promote such industrial cooperation models across Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia, facilitating technology transfer and shared manufacturing capacity among developing economies. Parallel progress on local currency settlement mechanisms, being explored and implemented in various forms among BRICS members and their partners, can reduce systemic exposure to currency volatility and unilateral financial sanctions. On regional security, the China-Africa framework prioritizes African solutions to African problems, rejecting external military interventionism and prioritizing political mediation of conflicts. This principle aligns with core BRICS consensus on advancing inclusive security governance. At the New Delhi summit, BRICS leaders reaffirmed the importance of advocating greater African representation within the United Nations Security Council and other multilateral bodies, a longstanding demand shared widely across the Global South. Unified advocacy for reform of global governance institutions remains essential to dismantle outdated power structures that systematically marginalize developing countries. As the influence of BRICS expands, narratives questioning the intentions of South-South partnerships continue to circulate. Yet the lived experience across African nations demonstrates that the China-Africa model operates on fundamentally different terms from traditional donor-recipient hierarchies. Cooperation projects are negotiated bilaterally, aligned with national development strategies set by African governments, and designed to support long-term self-reliance rather than permanent dependency. This partnership advocates a multipolar international order where every nation, large or small, enjoys equal decision-making rights. Moving forward, amplifying Global South voices demands sustained, institutionalized dialogue rather than ad-hoc diplomatic coordination. BRICS can draw on FOCAC's regular ministerial conferences, thematic working groups and people-to-people exchange frameworks to build permanent consultation channels with Global South communities. Expanded collaboration in climate finance, digital transformation and food security — all critical areas for Africa and developing regions — can demonstrate how collective South-South action delivers tangible progress toward the UN Sustainable Development Goals. The China-Africa partnership, developed over two decades of effective collaboration, serves as a practical model for Global South nations to unite and advance shared interests. Its foundation of equality, mutual respect and win-win development presents a viable alternative to hierarchical international relations. Applying the lessons from this partnership to the commitments made at the September summit — and carrying them forward under China's 2027 BRICS presidency — could not only strengthen Africa-BRICS ties but also initiate a new era of unified Global South action, reshaping international trade, finance and security for the future. The author is former state minister of planning and development of Ethiopia. The views do not necessarily reflect tho

body: Yangtze's 'living fossil' - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Going Green Home China Going Green Yangtze's 'living fossil' Some 1 million artificially bred Chinese sturgeon are being released into the wild each year, Hou Liqiang and Liu Kun report. By Hou Liqiang and Liu Kun | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:05 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE MUKESH MOHANAN/CHINA DAILY Editor's note: As protection of the planet's flora, fauna and resources becomes increasingly important, China Daily is publishing a series of stories to illustrate the country's commitment to safeguarding the natural world. In a high-stakes effort to save one of the world's most ancient fish species, Chinese scientists have built a self-sustaining captive population of the Chinese sturgeon — a critical breakthrough as the wild population teeters on the brink of total collapse. Researchers have successfully raised third-generation sturgeon in captivity, meaning the artificial population can now reproduce on a large scale without taking a single fish from the river, according to Wu Jinping, an associate researcher at the Yangtze River Fisheries Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Chinese sturgeon have existed for over 140 million years, and coexisted with the dinosaurs during the Early Cretaceous period. They are often referred to as "living fossils" because their body shape and physical features have remained largely unchanged for tens of millions of years. The breakthrough is of great significance for the conservation of the ancient species, Wu said, adding that stock enhancement has become one of the most effective measures to replenish resources in the wild. With support from the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, since 2024 China has released millions of artificially bred Chinese sturgeon back into the wild each year. Some 1.05 million Chinese sturgeon were released in 2025, and over 500,000 were released in the first half of 2026. "Sustained, large-scale releases of high-quality sturgeon of different sizes can help meet the need to replenish the natural population," Wu said. The Chinese sturgeon, an iconic species of the Yangtze River ecosystem, has been under severe pressure in the wild for decades. When the Gezhouba Dam was completed in 1981, it isolated the sturgeon from a 600-kilometer stretch of the lower Jinsha River and upper Yangtze River, which served as their major spawning grounds. In 1982, a new spawning ground was discovered in a roughly 4-km river section between the Gezhouba Dam and Miaozui — which became the species' sole known breeding site. However, this last refuge proved unable to sustain consistent reproduction, according to Wu, who said the first documented interruption of natural spawning occurred there in 2013. Although the breeding was rediscovered in 2014 and 2016, no natural spawning activity has been recorded since. Recent monitoring results show that the number of adult Chinese sturgeon migrating to the spawning ground below Gezhouba has fallen to just over 10 in each of the past three years. Hydroacoustic surveys detected 11 spawning adults in 2023, 10 in 2024 and 11 in 2025, he said. Wu said the wild population is declining sharply and is on the brink of extinction. The halt in natural reproduction means the population cannot replenish itself effectively without intervention. Restoring the wild population still faces major challenges, he said. While artificial breeding and releases can provide important support, scientists must further identify the key factors restricting natural reproduction. He called for efforts to restore the ecological functions of key habitats, including engineering measures to improve the terrain and substrate of spawning grounds. Hydrological regulation should also be explored to create suitable conditions for spawning, including appropriate water temperature, water level, sediment concentration and flow velocity. Monitoring of the species' marine life history should also be launched, Wu said, noting that stronger protection of key habitats across the sturgeon's life cycle will be essential for the long-term recovery of the species. body: Health minister: China will continue to implement fertility-friendly policies - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Society Home China Society Health minister: China will continue to implement fertility-friendly policies By Wang Xiaoyu | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-09-14 13:59 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE China will continue to have a relatively abundant workforce, and sustained efforts will be made to foster a fertility-friendly society, Health Minister Lei Haichao said on Monday. Although China's total population has declined for four consecutive years, the country is still home to 1.405 billion people and will remain a major population power for years to come, Lei said during a news conference held by the State Council Information Office. With more than 10 million students enrolling in colleges and universities each year — a sign of expanding access to higher education, Lei said the nation is building a growing workforce of highly skilled workers. Meanwhile, the annual number of newborns has held at about 8 million, despite an overall downward trend. "Compared with other developed and developing countries, the number of nations with this level of births is still very small, so China will still have a relatively ample labor force in the future," he said. Lei stressed that China will continue to roll out fertility-friendly measures to ease the burden of giving birth to, raising, and educating children. So far, more than 30 million families have benefited from the fertility subsidy policy launched last year. Over the next five years, he said more efforts will be made to integrate nursery and kindergarten care services and to support communities and employers in setting up nursery care facilities, so that residents can access such services more conveniently and at an affordable price. It is also important to promote a positive view on marriage and fertility, he added. body: Beijing tightens citywide drone restrictions - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Society Home China Society Beijing tightens citywide drone restrictions By Wang Xiaoyu | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-09-13 21:53 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Beijing has tightened restrictions on drones, prohibiting the possession and storage of drones and their core components across the city starting Nov 15 under a revised regulation adopted by the city's lawmakers. The revised regulation, passed by the Standing Committee of the Beijing Municipal People's Congress, tightens controls on drones compared with the previous version, which took effect on May 1, as authorities move to strengthen airspace security in the capital. In line with the new rules, the entire administrative area of Beijing will be designated as controlled airspace for unmanned aircraft. Flights by unmanned aircraft will be prohibited across the city unless otherwise permitted under relevant regulations. The possession and storage of drones and their core components will also be prohibited. Individuals and organizations will also be barred from transporting or carrying drones and their core components into Beijing. Exceptions will apply to special-purpose flights. Organizations involved in counterterrorism, public order, emergency rescue and disaster relief, major events, teaching, scientific research and manufacturing may conduct flights in accordance with relevant national regulations. Such organizations must establish safety management systems, clearly assign management responsibilities and take measures to prevent safety incidents, according to the revised regulation. Beijing began implementing its drone management regulation on May 1, together with rules requiring authorities to verify information on drones. The verification work, which included registration of existing devices, was completed on July 31, according to the authorities. The current information-verification rules will cease to apply when the revised regulation takes effect. To help residents dispose of drones already in Beijing before the Nov 15 deadline, authorities have opened several channels in addition to allowing owners to take their devices out of the city themselves. Drone owners can sell their aircraft to buyback companies certified by district-level governments or hand them over to government-designated recycling facilities. In either case, they can receive subsidies ranging from 100 yuan ($14.9) to 3,000 yuan per drone, in addition to the money received from selling the device. Another option is to send drones by China Post's EMS service to an address outside Beijing between Sept 12 and Nov 14, and the delivery fee will be waived after the equipment is verified. Residents who choose to take their drones out of Beijing themselves must do so by Nov 15, using transportation such as civil aviation, rail or road services. The revised regulation also establishes a citywide ban on drone storage. Unless otherwise provided by law or regulation, no organization or individual may establish a warehouse, temporary storage site or other storage facility for unmanned aircraft within Beijing. Public security authorities will conduct inspections and take legal action against those who fail to move their drones out of Beijing by the deadline or illegally store them, according to the authorities. Beijing said it will continue routine controls over the city's airspace and provide policy guidance and services to help residents comply with the new requirements. body: Veteran CCTV presenter Jing Yidan dies aged 71 - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Society Home China Society Veteran CCTV presenter Jing Yidan dies aged 71 By ZHAO YIMENG | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:04 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Jing Yidan Chinese journalists, broadcasters and viewers are mourning the death of Jing Yidan, a veteran television journalist and presenter remembered for her calm, thoughtful style and decades-long commitment to the integrity of the profession. Jing, a familiar face to generations of Chinese television viewers, passed away on Sunday at 71 after suffering an acute cerebral hemorrhage in her hometown of Harbin, Heilongjiang province, in June, according to a death notice released by her daughter. She was later transferred to a hospital in Beijing, where she received treatment until death. Tributes have poured in from former colleagues and fellow broadcasters. Many remembered Jing not only as a prominent TV host but as a journalist whose restrained reporting, careful questioning and sense of responsibility earned the trust of viewers. Jing joined China Central Television in 1988 and worked as a reporter, editor and presenter before becoming a broadcast director. Over the span of her career, she hosted influential programs such as Focus Report , Oriental Horizon and News Probe . She also anchored live coverage of major events, including the handovers of Hong Kong and Macao special administrative regions to China. Jing received the China Golden Mic Awards, one of the highest honors for broadcasters in the country, three times. Her most enduring professional legacy was her two decades with Focus Report , a program known for investigative reporting and public-interest journalism. "I was with Focus Report for 20 years," said Jing in a speech at the 2026 graduation ceremony of Peking University's HSBC Business School in May. Reflecting on her career after retirement, she said the most valuable thing she had done was "to amplify the voices of the vulnerable, spread the voices of the wise and advance the progress of civilization". Bai Yansong, a longtime colleague and partner on Focus Report , praised Jing's professionalism and he reflected on their 30-year career partnership. "Jing walked her journey with composure and determination, always smiling and curious as she experienced the seasons," said Bai in a tribute posted online. Broadcaster Cao Kefan, who received the China Golden Mic Awards in the same year as Jing in 1997, remembered her as warm and considerate in private and exceptionally dedicated to her work. "She devoted herself wholeheartedly to every task," said Cao in a written tribute, adding that the restraint and conscience she demonstrated on screen had long been an example for other presenters. Former CCTV sports commentator Han Qiaosheng also remembered Jing as calm and rational, highlighting how she used "calm and sincere reporting to record the times". For many viewers, Jing's programs were a part of everyday life for generations who watched TV around the dinner table. " Oriental Horizon and Focus Report — the programs we loved watching while having dinner when we were children," one commenter wrote on social media. Another described Jing as a journalist who "used integrity to embody the spirit of journalism", adding that her voice and image would remain in viewers' memories. Jing's daughter said that over the nearly three months from the summer solstice to white dew, her mother received an outpouring of well wishes from people hoping for her speedy recovery. On June 17, her social media account posted a video of her visiting Cai Lei, a former senior executive who has been living with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Jing brought him a bundle of wheat and a copy of his book Believe. Cai wrote on Sunday that they had planned for Jing to host an offline reading event for an expanded edition of the book. "I never imagined that those warm words would become a farewell," Cai wrote. "I will carry her words with me, continue to 'believe' and continue moving forward." Shi Shusi, a famous commentator in China, said the tributes to Jing have become a remembrance not only of an individual broadcaster but of a generation of TV journalism in which professionalism, restraint and public trust were central to the craft. zhaoyimeng@chinadaily.com.cn Photo 19th Chinese Bridge foreign participants tour Beijing Heilongjiang begins autumn rice harvest across black soil fields Colorful activities mark Teachers' Day across China Snow leopard repeatedly spotted in Gansu's Qilian Mountains Evacuated residents returning home after Gyirong mudslide Neighbors give Lao hospitals healthy dose of support Latest Veteran CCTV presenter Jing Yidan dies aged 71 Intl sci-tech collaboration urged President's remarks praised as visionary for BRICS Xi: China, India should be partners Beijing tightens citywide drone restrictions Xi calls on BRICS to unite Global South, deepen cooperation State Council News A look at China's economy in H1 of 2026 Xi returns to Beijing after BRICS summit Policies concerning expats, foreign enterprises in August 2026 Exclusive Hands off! body: Robotics companies eye homes as potential market - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Business Macro Companies Industries Technology Motoring China Data Finance Top 10 Home / Business / Technology Home Business Technology Robotics companies eye homes as potential market New frontier is tougher, less predictable operating environment than factories By CHENG YU | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:19 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE A cosplayer takes photos with a deformable robot T1 from Qiyuan Robotics during the ChinaJoy 2026 expo in Shanghai on July 31. CHEN YUYU/FOR CHINA DAILY China's next "family member" may be 88 centimeters tall, weigh 15 kilograms and small enough to fit inside a backpack. It is not a child or a pet, but Qiyuan Q1, a compact robot from Qiyuan Robotics, the consumer-robotics business of Shanghai-listed Swancor Advanced Materials. Together with another deformable robot T1, the two robots are expected to be delivered soon. The launch marks a new test for China's fast-growing embodied artificial intelligence industry. After two years spent proving that humanoid robots can walk, run, dance and work in factories, companies are increasingly confronting a harder question: can they build a robot ordinary consumers actually want in their homes? Tian Hua, CEO of Swancor Advanced Materials, has framed the bet in broader terms. "Personal robots are not simply industrial robots moved into homes, nor are they AI toys with large models stuffed into hardware shells. They are a still-emerging new species of human-machine interaction." For Tian, the long-term prize is not just selling another gadget. He said that personal robots could become the next major interface after keyboards, screens, smartphones and smart speakers — a physical carrier connecting AI, digital services and real-world life. The ambition comes with a tougher operating environment than factories. Factories are relatively structured environments, with fixed routes, predictable lighting and repetitive tasks. Homes are chaotic: chairs move, toys appear on the floor, pets wander through rooms and the same cup can be in the kitchen one day and the bedroom the next. That is why Qiyuan is not starting with a full-sized humanoid promising to do everything. The Q1 is deliberately small. Its 88-centimeter frame is designed for companionship, entertainment and embodied-AI development, while its size and 15-kilogram weight may help reduce power consumption and safety risks around children and elderly users. Tian said making Q1 small was partly about giving a home robot greater approachability and safety, supported by torque sensing and force-control capabilities. The T1 takes a different approach. Standing about one meter tall, it can switch between a wheeled humanoid form for indoor use and a quadruped configuration for grass, gravel, slopes and other outdoor terrain. The two designs reflect a broader rethink across the robotics industry: the most useful consumer robot may not be the one that looks most human, but the one that best fits human life. Such a design is also being explored abroad. US-Norwegian robotics company 1X has opened reservations for its NEO home robot, while South Korea's LG Electronics has developed a wheeled dual-arm robot designed to work with smart-home appliances. For Swancor, the bigger test may be less about body shape and more about whether it can move from prototypes to mass production. The company said its consumer embodied-AI robot business had received 210 million yuan ($31.29 million) in advance payments in the first half of 2026. It also invested 164 million yuan in related research and development and built a robotics R&D team of about 180 people. The company has partnered with Lens Intelligent Robotics, a unit of Lens Technology, on a first-phase production line planned at the 10,000-unit level, covering precision parts processing, joint-module production and final assembly. In Guangzhou, Guangdong province, the company has worked with Shangpin Home Collection on so-called robot-ready homes, integrating furniture, smart controls and robotic systems so machines can more easily locate and manipulate household objects. Tian said: "Swancor's materials background is not incidental to the robotics push. Many technical problems ultimately become materials problems; the company's experience in lightweight, environmentally friendly and high-strength materials can be applied to robot bodies, with some key materials expected to be supplied internally after product launch." Wang Feili, China industrial analyst at UBS Securities, said in a separate interview that humanoid robots have not yet reached a true commercialization turning point. "Industrial use cases are likely to scale first over the next three to five years, while the home remains the most promising but more distant market," Wang said. chengyu@chinadaily.com.cn Photo Pop Land City Carnival Tour arrives in Shanghai Gansu's traditional medicine industry embraces tech and global markets China International Big Data Industry Expo showcases data achievements in Guiyang World Humanoid Robot Games open in Beijing Tourists shop for Taiwan goods in Fujian The 'Vibrant China' media tour in Hunan: Changsha blends history with creativity Most Viewed in 24 Hours State Council News A look at China's economy in H1 of 2026 Policies concerning expats, foreign enterprises in August 2026 Top 10 Top 10 countries attracting Chinese tourists Business focus Manufacturing edge a win-win multiplier abroad 'New new three' power China's trade China Data China's CPI up 0.8% in August SOEs SOEs return more profits to State China's central SOEs invest 1.1t yuan in Xinjiang during 14th Five-Year Plan period Special 2026 CIFTIS China International Supply Chain Expo Top BACK TO THE TOP English 中文 HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Copyright 1994 - . body: Brazil hydro upgrades power green partnership - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Business Macro Companies Industries Technology Motoring China Data Finance Top 10 Home / Business / Industries Home Business Industries Brazil hydro upgrades power green partnership By ZHENG XIN | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:04 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE As the global transition toward sustainable development accelerates, clean energy cooperation between China and Latin America is proving to hold boundless potential, as Chinese technological innovation revitalizes critical legacy assets amid the region's ambitious push for grid modernization. "China has advanced technology and rich experience, while Brazil boasts abundant natural resources and immense market demand," said Ye Xiaoning, a senior engineer at the State Grid Energy Research Institute. "This complementarity is the very key to our successful cooperation," he added. Ye noted that the mutually beneficial partnership perfectly demonstrates how developing nations can join hands to comprehensively develop and utilize clean energy on a massive scale. This year marks a historic milestone: the 10th anniversary of the Ilha Solteira and Jupia hydroelectric power plants under Chinese stewardship. On July 1, 2016, CTG Brasil, a unit of China Three Gorges Corporation, the world's biggest dam builder and operator, officially took over operations of the two massive stations. Over the past decade, these two hydroelectric heavyweights spanning southeastern Brazil have undergone a profound metamorphosis. Once aging plants plagued by equipment deterioration and frequent unplanned outages, they have been completely transformed into a shining benchmark of Sino-Brazilian hydropower integration and now serve as the vital energy backbone for Brazil's prosperous southeastern economic corridor, said the company. Boasting an installed capacity of 1.55 million kilowatts, the Jupia Hydropower Station generated an estimated 6.77 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity in 2025 alone. The Ilha Solteira Hydropower Station, on the other hand, is currently Brazil's sixth-largest hydroelectric facility and features 20 generation units and a total capacity of 3.44 million kW. Combined, these facilities offer nearly 5 million kW of capacity. Every year, the two stations transmit a massive amount of clean hydropower to the Brazilian grid, meeting the electricity needs of over 6 million people. CTG acquired the 30-year concession rights for the projects between 2015 and 2016 in a landmark $3.7 billion transaction, which remains the company's largest overseas acquisition to date and firmly established CTG as Brazil's third-largest non-state power generator. Rather than merely operating the existing infrastructure, CTG initiated a monumental "heart transplant" for the aging facilities. Since the major hydropower technical renovation was officially launched in 2017, CTG Brasil has completed the technological upgrading of 12 generating units in two batches across both stations. This mammoth overhaul has brought a fundamental change to the operational conditions of both plants. Coupled with a continuously consolidated safety culture, the operational reliability of the units has been significantly increased. In 2024, the comprehensive availability rate of CTG Brasil's power stations reached an impressive 95.6 percent. Furthermore, a new centralized control center in Ilha Solteira, which became fully operational in 2022, has fundamentally eliminated historical safety hazards within the backbone power grid, ensuring the continuous, highly efficient delivery of clean power, it said. Li Yinsheng, chairman of CTG International, noted that while Brazil offers a highly professional workforce and a competitive market, foreign investors must carefully navigate stringent labor regulations, infrastructure shortfalls and complex tax frameworks. In response, CTG has pioneered a deeply localized management model that fully empowers local Brazilian professionals. According to Ye, China and Brazil, as two of the world's leading hydropower nations, share a profound mutual understanding of large-scale energy infrastructure. zhengxin@chinadaily.com.cn Photo Pop Land City Carnival Tour arrives in Shanghai Gansu's traditional medicine industry embraces tech and global markets China International Big Data Industry Expo showcases data achievements in Guiyang World Humanoid Robot Games open in Beijing Tourists shop for Taiwan goods in Fujian The 'Vibrant China' media tour in Hunan: Changsha blends history with creativity Most Viewed in 24 Hours State Council News A look at China's economy in H1 of 2026 Policies concerning expats, foreign enterprises in August 2026 Top 10 Top 10 countries attracting Chinese tourists Business focus Manufacturing edge a win-win multiplier abroad 'New new three' power China's trade China Data China's CPI up 0.8% in August SOEs SOEs return more profits to State China's central SOEs invest 1.1t yuan in Xinjiang during 14th Five-Year Plan period Special 2026 CIFTIS China International Supply Chain Expo Top BACK TO THE TOP English 中文 HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Copyright 1994 - . body: Delight in watching development of robotics - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Business Macro Companies Industries Technology Motoring China Data Finance Top 10 Home / Business / Technology Home Business Technology Delight in watching development of robotics By Cheng Yu | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 08:52 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Robots compete in a 100-meter sprint on Wednesday during the just-concluded second World Humanoid Robot Games, which ran from Aug 22 to Wednesday at Beijing's National Speed Skating Oval. [Photo by Zou Hong/China Daily] At the recent World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, I happened to find myself a few seats away from Wang Xingxing, founder of Unitree Robotics. When the opening ceremony ended, most of the corporate executives in the row got up and left. Wang stayed. He kept watching. And then he laughed. Not the polite, camera-ready smile executives wear at public events. He actually laughed out loud — several times — as robots sprinted, stumbled, crashed, scrambled back to their feet and tried again. That caught my attention because I had seen Wang at another milestone only days earlier: Unitree's stock market debut. For most entrepreneurs, ringing the listing bell is the kind of moment that is celebrated with champagne, hugs and photographs destined for office walls. Wang looked almost unnervingly calm. He barely smiled. The contrast was striking. The man who showed little emotion while ringing the bell was visibly delighted watching a robot fall over. At the listing ceremony, Wang was surrounded by capital: valuations, price-to-earnings ratios, market capitalization and stock charts. At the robot games, he was watching machines run, jump, fail, recover and improve. Since Unitree listed on Shanghai's STAR Market, investors have experienced both extremes. On its first trading day, excitement surrounding humanoid robots pushed Unitree's market value above 440 billion yuan ($65.56 billion) at one point. But the rally quickly reversed. Within about two weeks of listing, more than 230 billion yuan had been erased from its peak valuation. That kind of swing makes for irresistible headlines. It also makes it easy to confuse a stock chart with an industry. The pullback does not necessarily mean Unitree's fundamentals suddenly deteriorated. New shares often have limited freely tradeable supply, and enthusiasm for humanoid robots had already pushed expectations extraordinarily high before the company even reached the market. Unitree's IPO was priced at a price-to-earnings ratio of 92.92 times, embedding a substantial growth premium. When investors eventually stopped asking how high the stock could go and started asking how much of the future had already been priced in, some correction was almost inevitable. The more important question is what lies underneath the share price. Humanoid robots remain an early-stage industry. The path to mass commercialization is still unclear. Costs remain high, useful applications are limited and a robot that looks brilliant in a demonstration may still struggle to perform the same mundane task reliably for eight hours on a factory floor. That is the uncomfortable reality behind the excitement. But it is also why Unitree matters. The company is one of the relatively small number of humanoid-robot makers globally that has reached meaningful shipment scale while also generating a profit. Its revenue approached 1.7 billion yuan in 2025, and its humanoid robot shipments ranked among the world's highest. In an industry where many companies are still burning cash to prove that their machines can walk, Unitree has already demonstrated strengths in vertically integrated research and development, rapid product iteration and supply-chain management. There is still a caveat. Much of Unitree's revenue today comes from universities, research institutes and other professional customers. The truly enormous markets — industrial production and household use — remain largely in pilot stages. Robots that companies or families will buy repeatedly, at scale and for clear economic reasons, are still being developed. That is why Unitree's listing may ultimately matter more as a benchmark than as a spectacle. The next phase of the humanoid-robot race will increasingly be judged not by how impressive a demonstration looks, but by orders, deployment, reliability, repeat purchases and economies of scale. On the track, robots kept making mistakes. Some ran beautifully. Others looked awkward. A few fell hard enough to trigger laughter from the audience. Wang laughed too. And suddenly his expression at the IPO ceremony made a little more sense to me. A stock can rise 400 percent and then lose hundreds of billions of yuan in market value. Those numbers can change in days. A robot learning how to run, fall and stand back up again is slower. But for a technology obsessive, that may be the part that actually matters. body: A trade bonanza for all, 20 years in the making - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Business Macro Companies Industries Technology Motoring China Data Finance Top 10 Home / Business / Policies Home Business Policies A trade bonanza for all, 20 years in the making By ZHONG NAN | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:13 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Deeper trade and investment ties among BRICS countries — Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, as well as other member states — will help bolster economic resilience across the Global South and inject fresh momentum into an increasingly strained multilateral trading system, market watchers and business leaders said. The group was established as BRIC in 2006, with South Africa joining five years later, and it has evolved into a major platform for Global South countries to deepen economic ties and advance collaboration in areas ranging from trade and investment to finance and agriculture. As protectionism and geopolitical tensions add to uncertainty in the global economy, analysts said more BRICS collaboration could provide members with greater room to diversify markets and supply chains, as well as reduce their exposure to external shocks. Wang Lei, director of the BRICS cooperation center at Beijing Normal University, said BRICS has gained greater economic significance as developing countries seek broader markets, more diversified sources of investment and deeper integration into regional and global supply chains. There is ample room to deepen collaboration in production capacity, trade in goods and services and cross-border investment, Wang said. Echoing that view, Cai Tongjuan, deputy dean of Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies at Renmin University of China in Beijing, said the size and diversity of BRICS economies give members considerable scope to tap into each other's markets. The potential for deeper economic collaboration is reflected in China's growing trade with several of its BRICS partners. Exchanges with Russia, India, Brazil and South Africa all recorded double-digit growth in the first seven months of this year. The value of China's trade with Russia rose 21.5 percent to 1.1 trillion yuan ($163.7 billion) between January and July compared with the corresponding period in 2025, while the value of its trade with India rose 18.4 percent to 748.39 billion yuan, the General Administration of Customs said. The value of the country's trade with Brazil rose 21.4 percent to 881.53 billion yuan from January to July compared with the corresponding period last year, and the value of trade with South Africa rose 21.7 percent to 261.19 billion yuan. Andre Thomashausen, professor emeritus of international law at the University of South Africa, said BRICS countries should deepen cooperation in digital technologies and smart manufacturing to accelerate the upgrading of traditional industries, while expanding trade and investment in renewable energy. Deeper economic ties are also translating into business opportunities for Chinese manufacturers in fast-growing BRICS markets. The value of exports of steam garment care products to India by Ningbo Kaibo Group Co Ltd, a home appliance manufacturer in Ningbo, Zhejiang province, rose 34.2 percent to 31.26 million yuan from January to July compared with the corresponding period last year, driven by rising demand in India's growing home appliance market. Lu Dongfei, the company's foreign trade director, said faster urbanization, an expanding middle-income group and rising demand for higher-quality garment care are creating new opportunities in India, according to information released by Ningbo Customs. zhongnan@chinadaily.com.cn Photo Pop Land City Carnival Tour arrives in Shanghai Gansu's traditional medicine industry embraces tech and global markets China International Big Data Industry Expo showcases data achievements in Guiyang World Humanoid Robot Games open in Beijing Tourists shop for Taiwan goods in Fujian The 'Vibrant China' media tour in Hunan: Changsha blends history with creativity Most Viewed in 24 Hours State Council News A look at China's economy in H1 of 2026 Policies concerning expats, foreign enterprises in August 2026 Top 10 Top 10 countries attracting Chinese tourists Business focus Manufacturing edge a win-win multiplier abroad 'New new three' power China's trade China Data China's CPI up 0.8% in August SOEs SOEs return more profits to State China's central SOEs invest 1.1t yuan in Xinjiang during 14th Five-Year Plan period Special 2026 CIFTIS China International Supply Chain Expo Top BACK TO THE TOP English 中文 HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Copyright 1994 - . By Li Yingxue | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 07:05 Share - WeChat Chinese science fiction writer Qiyue (left) attends an event at a Respublika bookstore in Russia. CHINA DAILY Decades before Chinese science fiction writer Zhao Lei — better known by his pen name Qiyue (July) — arrived in Moscow with his novel The Stars, he was a middle school student saving an entire semester's pocket money to buy the works of Soviet science fiction pioneer Alexander Belyaev. In September, that early literary connection took on new meaning as Qiyue introduced his own vision of the future to Russian readers at the 39th Moscow International Book Fair. "For me, Belyaev and Jules Verne were the two writers who introduced me to science fiction," he said. Held from Sept 2 to 6 in the Russian capital, the book fair brought together writers and publishers from China and Russia. Qiyue attended as part of a Chinese delegation organized by China Educational Publications Import & Export Corporation Ltd. On Sept 3, Qiyue joined popular Russian science fiction writer Vadim Panov for a discussion on Chinese and Russian science fiction. The venue was packed, with visitors passing through the exhibition area also stopping to hear the two writers discuss the development of science fiction in China and Russia, its international influence and the future of human civilization. In Qiyue's opinion, the recent rise of Chinese science fiction is closely connected with the country's rapid technological and social development. "Literature is always a reflection of reality," he said. "As China has begun moving toward technological innovation and creating the future, Chinese people have also become more interested in the future than they were before. They can increasingly imagine themselves living in a future shaped by technology. This has created fertile ground for the rise of Chinese science fiction." He said, however, that Chinese science fiction is still developing and has yet to establish a mature, stable, creative ecosystem with a widely recognizable identity. At the same time, he sees an emerging Chinese character in some works, which he describes as "a form of collective heroism rooted in ordinary people". Qiyue participates in a China-Russia science fiction discussion with renowned Russian cyberpunk writer Vadim Panov. CHINA DAILY "It is neither an individual protagonist awakening and performing a selfless heroic act, nor the vague collective efforts of ordinary people," he said. "It is more like starting from the perspective of each individual, igniting each person's small flame, and eventually bringing all those lights together." A signing session for the Russian edition of The Stars followed the discussion. According to the organizers, copies of the book quickly sold out, and a long line formed at the signing table. Some readers bought copies for friends and relatives who could not attend, and one fan purchased four books. First published in Chinese in 2019, The Stars was released in Russian by AST Publishers in 2024. Set in the near future, the novel explores the consequences of mysterious signals detected by China's FAST telescope, the world's largest single-dish radio telescope. Genetic information encoded in one of the signals enables scientists to create an alien "construct" that begins to alter the known laws of physics. Yet beneath its cosmic scale, the novel remains grounded in ordinary human lives. "When I wrote this novel, I simply wanted to be sincere — to write about the reality I had actually seen and the people I knew and understood," Qiyue said. The scientists he knows must deal not only with major scientific questions but also with the pressures of buying a home, getting married, and building a career. Qiyue and Panov discuss science fiction at the Moscow International Book Fair. CHINA DAILY "People's struggles are never only 'big struggles'. They are a mixture of problems, both large and small," he said. "An everyday concern involving a 100-square-meter apartment can become intertwined with a science fiction canvas spanning thousands of light-years. That contrast arises naturally." That attention to ordinary life, he believes, is also what allows The Stars to connect with readers overseas. "I don't know whether Russians have the same anxiety about buying a home, but I believe they also face all kinds of real-life difficulties," he said. "The specific circumstances may be different, but the experiences people share are universal." On Sept 2, Qiyue visited Respublika, a major bookstore chain in Russia, for a reader meet-and-greet and book signing. He spoke with local science fiction enthusiasts about his writing journey, the conception of The Stars and how he places ordinary lives within stories that unfold on a cosmic scale. Qiyue began publishing science fiction in 2001 and became a full-time writer in 2019. He has been honored at the Galaxy Awards and the Chinese Nebula Awards. From a teenager saving his pocket money for Russian science fiction to signing his own novel for Russian readers, Qiyue's journey to Moscow has come full circle. Through The Stars, the conversation continues — across languages, borders and imaginations — about the future of humanity and the lives of ordinary people within it.
title: Moscow lit up by 'The Stars'

[Photo provided to chinadaily.com.cn] L'Oréal China hosted a forum in Dunhuang last weekend, presenting a new interpretation of L'Oréal Group's global "Essentiality of Beauty" concept in China. The initiative explores the profound impact of "beauty" on individuals and society through four dimensions -- historical culture, quality of life, socio-economic development, and international exchange -- while inviting more people to participate in creating beauty. In her opening speech, Lan Zhenzhen, president of public affairs for L'Oréal North Asia and China, explored the rich meaning of beauty. "Beauty is not just a visual experience, but also a form of cultural heritage and social responsibility. Through this project, we hope to inspire more people to pursue and create beauty," she said. Guo Hao, author of the book series Chinese Traditional Colors. [Photo provided to chinadaily.com.cn] At the forum, Guo Hao, author of the book series Chinese Traditional Colors , gave a mini lecture on the aesthetics of color in the Dunhuang murals. Artist Hu Junjun, creator of the land art project "Desert Inquiry", shared insights into her creative inspiration and understanding of beauty. Jiang Changjian, Fudan University scholar. [Photo provided to chinadaily.com.cn] Fudan University scholar Jiang Changjian served as the forum's special guest host. Shi Zhan, scholar and professor at the Shanghai International Studies University's Institute for Global Civilization History, and knowledge blogger Zhao Jian also joined the event to discuss the influence of beauty and its future possibilities. Through the forum, L'Oréal China hopes to further advance its aesthetic education projects, support the protection and inheritance of cultural heritage, and promote the idea of "Beauty in Diversity, Harmony in Beauty". L'Oréal China hosted a forum in Dunhuang last weekend, presenting a new interpretation of L'Oréal Group's global "Essentiality of Beauty" concept in China. [Photo provided to chinadaily.com.cn] The colors of Dunhuang, an integral part of its artistic heritage, face the threat of fading after millennia of exposure to wind and sand. In response, L'Oréal's brand SkinCeuticals, under its "Protecting the Caves, Protecting Beauty", initiative, has donated to the China Dunhuang Grottoes Conservation Research Foundation for six consecutive years to support the conservation of the grottoes. This year, SkinCeuticals also launched the Grass Grid Sand Control Public Welfare Project, using sand-stabilizing measures to provide long-term ecological protection for the grottoes.
