body: Art gallery brings ancient compendium to life - Chinadaily.com.cn WS6aa72b14e4b06d4aa055dcd4 China Edition | Global Edition | ASIA | 中文 China Latest Society Innovation Education Cross-Strait HK/Macao Health Environment Military Video World Asia-Pacific Americas Europe Middle East Africa Business Policies Companies Industries Technology China Up-close China Data Motoring Video Culture Art Music and Theater Film and TV Books Heritage Events and Festivals People Cultural Exchange Video Photo Gallery Fashion Health Travel News City Tours Guides and Tips My Footprints Around the World Features Photo Video Food Sports Soccer Basketball Volleyball Tennis Golf Track and field Swimming Motor China Stars Opinion Cartoons Editorials Global Lens We Comment Columnists Global Views Chinese Perspectives Opinion Line Regional Newspaper China Daily PDF China Daily E-Paper China Daily Global PDF China Daily Global E-Paper Mobile CULTURE News Heritage Art Film Theater Fashion Cultural Exchange Books Photo Video HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE 中文 CULTURE News Heritage Art Film Theater Fashion Cultural Exchange Books Photo Video Home / Culture / Art Art gallery brings ancient compendium to life Xinhua | Updated: 2026-09-14 07:00 Share - WeChat An image depicting an ancient waterwheel and an ancient mill is on display at the exhibition, featuring the digital version of the Siku Quanshu, or The Complete Library of the Four Treasuries, in Lanzhou, Northwest China's Gansu province, on Aug 25. LANG BINGBING/XINHUA An art gallery in Lanzhou, the capital of Northwest China's Gansu province, has turned a colossal ancient literary collection into something anyone can enjoy. Instead of displaying dense classical Chinese that only scholars can master, it exhibits 122 images from this seldom-shown 18th-century compendium, including a sketch of an ancient Indian unicorn, a star map nearly a millennium old, and the private scribbles of a stern, diligent emperor. These images form part of a years-long project to digitize a copy of the Siku Quanshu, which translates as the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries, one of the most comprehensive collections of Chinese classical works in history. Compiled during the Qing Dynasty (1644-1911), the compendium runs to nearly 800 million characters across thousands of volumes, covering everything from Confucian philosophy to farming techniques. Seven copies were originally produced, but only three and a half survive today, preserved in Beijing, Taipei, Lanzhou and Hangzhou. For decades, this massive treasured collection was locked away. To better preserve its copy, Lanzhou built a dedicated library in an underground repository with constant temperature and humidity. In 2021, a project was launched to digitize it. By the end of May 2022, the scanning of the text was finished, and the project moved into data processing. A team of young editors then spent more than two years checking the data page by page, and along the way, they discovered something unexpected: the playful side of the massive and complex text. "Most people think such a work would be too difficult to read," says Zhang Yang, deputy director of the digital publishing center at Duzhe Publishing and Media, the project's lead. "But as we went page by page, we found plenty of vivid images that could spark modern readers' curiosity." What started as a routine check soon turned into a curatorial mission. The team selected 122 of the most striking images and organized them into 12 sections, covering tea culture, astronomy, architecture, medicine, costume, and even weapon-making. The editors gave the sections titles, such as "Ancient Gardening Know-How" and "Ancient Stargazing Guide", bridging the gap between centuries-old social life and the modern day. One section is called "World Mystery Box", featuring images from geographical works by Western missionaries during the Qing Dynasty. These images depict the Colosseum in Rome, the Colossus of Rhodes, and exotic and mythical creatures, such as lions and mermaids. "We had long heard of the Siku Quanshu by name, but this is our first time seeing it up close," says Liang Tao, a visitor from Xi'an. "It's both fun and awe-inspiring." That reaction reflects the exhibition's goal. Song Xuejuan, who heads the digitization project, says the exhibition "transforms 'static preservation' into 'dynamic sharing', and turns an academic treasure into a public experience". For a long time, there was a disconnect between traditional culture and younger generations. In recent years, however, new technologies, fresh perspectives and innovative storytelling have helped connect ancient heritage with contemporary trends. The Mogao Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Gansu, dating back to the 4th century, are an example. In the 1980s, local researchers began exploring digital documentation. Today, they have completed high-precision digital capture of 323 caves. The images rendered on screen are now even clearer than what the naked eye can see on site, revealing details that once required climbing ladders to inspect. A girl views an image featuring the digital version of the Siku Quanshu at the exhibition. LANG BINGBING/XINHUA Another example is the immersive interactive digital exhibition of oracle bone inscriptions, held in Tianjin in April. Using artificial intelligence and mixed reality technologies, it allowed visitors to experience the ancient ritual of oracle bone divination. The Lanzhou gallery says it had previously received only a few hundred visitors per day on average. But since this new image exhibition launched, it has seen attendance surge to over 3,000 on peak days. Among the crowds are many children accompanied by parents. For Song's team, they were no longer editors merely checking for data errors, but rather communicators sharing the treasures with the public. "I used to think the Siku Quanshu was unreachable," says Song Jia'ni, a 34-year-old editor on the team. "But once you get into it, you will realize you don't have to begin with a long history. One picture, or one detail, is enough to hook you."
title: Art gallery brings ancient compendium to life

body: Fresh violence sparks tension in Middle East - World - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE World Asia-Pacific Americas Europe Middle East Africa China-US China-Europe China-Japan China-Africa Home World / Middle East Home / World / Middle East Fresh violence sparks tension in Middle East Commercial vessel attacked off Iran as Houthis target Saudi military base By JAN YUMUL in Hong Kong and CUI HAIPEI in Dubai, UAE | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 10:08 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Tensions escalated in the Middle East over the weekend after one person was killed as an Iranian vessel came under attack in Qeshm Island while Yemen's Houthi rebels and the Yemeni government exchanged strikes over the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. An Iranian commercial ship was struck near Hengam Island and the Shib Deraz coast of Qeshm around 5 am on Sunday, killing one person and wounding three others, Iranian media reported, citing Hossein Amir Teymouri, the governor of Qeshm. He blamed the "American-Zionist enemy" for the attack. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations, or UKMTO, issued a report on Sunday saying it had received a report of an incident within the Strait of Hormuz. "A vessel has been struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Status of crew, damage assessment and environmental impact are unknown at present," said the UKMTO report. "Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO whilst authorities are investigating," the UKMTO said. The latest escalation comes as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian announced the foreign ministers of the Arab states would be meeting in Oman on Monday to reach an agreement on a framework for navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. Pezeshkian made the announcement in an interview with Indian media on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit, which took place in New Delhi on Saturday and Sunday. Pezeshkian reiterated Iran had no problems with its neighbors but objected to US military bases in the region allegedly being used to attack Tehran. But the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Bahrain clarified in a statement on Saturday that Manama would not participate in the meeting and that it "will not be a party to any group meeting that includes Iran before the return of diplomatic relations between the two countries". It said Bahrain's position had been communicated to Oman through official channels and that "it does not diminish the Kingdom's appreciation for their sincere efforts, nor its commitment to dialogue as a means to resolve differences". Further, the ministry said that dialogue "cannot ignore the facts", adding that Bahrain had been subjected to attacks targeting its infrastructure and civilian facilities, one of which, targeting an ammonia tank, nearly led to a catastrophe. "The ministry affirms that the security and stability of the region cannot be built on overlooking aggression, nor can it be bought by remaining silent about its consequences, nor can it be preserved through a policy of appeasement," it said. Yemen's Houthi group said on Sunday it had launched a large-scale ballistic missile and drone attack on a military base in southern Saudi Arabia. Drone strike In a statement posted on X, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea said the group had launched a large-scale ballistic missile and drone attack on a military base in Sharurah, Saudi Arabia, targeting weapons, depots and command-and-control facilities. He gave no information on casualties or damage. He said the operation was in retaliation for continued Saudi military action in Yemen, warning further escalation would be met with "larger operations" deeper inside Saudi territory. Over the past two days, Saudi fighter jets have been hitting various areas under the control of the Ansar Allah Houthis, including central provinces and the north of the country, trying to prevent more Houthi advances, Al Jazeera reported on Sunday. US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he believes Iran was behind the attacks that forced the closure of Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline. He also claimed that the Houthis asked Washington not to intervene in the recent tensions. Meanwhile, a senior Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy official also warned US naval vessels against approaching the Strait of Hormuz, vowing an "Iranian response" and challenging US claims of control over the critical waterway. body: AfD's victory signals far-right surge set to reshape Europe, experts say - World - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE World Asia-Pacific Americas Europe Middle East Africa China-US China-Europe China-Japan China-Africa Home World / Europe Home / World / Europe AfD's victory signals far-right surge set to reshape Europe, experts say By YANG RAN | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:55 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE A voter arrives at a polling station in Magdeburg, Germany, Sept 6, 2026. [Photo/Agencies] The far-right party's resounding victory in a recent German state election reflects a broader rightward drift across Germany and Europe, experts said. With crucial elections looming in major European nations next year, the continued rise of such parties is poised to profoundly reshape the continent's geopolitical landscape and the very fabric of the European Union, they said. The record victory of the far-right Alternative for Germany, or AfD, in the Saxony-Anhalt state election on Sept 6 has sent shock waves across Germany. The AfD captured an unprecedented 43.8 percent of the vote in the region, making it possible for the party to run a German state for the first time. Former German chancellor Angela Merkel described the outcome as "a turning point, a real turning point in German history". Wu Huiping, deputy director of the German Studies Center at Tongji University, said that while the Saxony-Anhalt vote is subnational, its implications for Germany's political landscape are profound. She noted the far-right AfD's nearly 44 percent state-level win was almost unthinkable for postwar Germany, which has remained vigilant against far-right forces. "This marks the emergence of a far-right party as the largest party after a state election and a possible coalition with the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance, or BSW, which would effectively breach the 'firewall' against the far-right." She said the AfD's steady rise has already pushed Germany's political ecosystem in a more conservative direction. "Even left-origin parties like the BSW now adopt tougher stances on immigration and emphasize national identity, signaling a conservative drift within the left camp. Meanwhile, mainstream parties have moved right on issues like immigration, further tilting the country's political center of gravity to the right." This unprecedented far-right triumph in Germany immediately sent ripples of concern across Europe. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez described the Saxony-Anhalt election as a warning of the "far-right threat" gaining traction throughout the continent. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot emphasized the urgent need to address the public anger and despair that fuel the popularity of radical movements. Cui Hongjian, a professor at Beijing Foreign Studies University's Academy of Regional and Global Governance, said the swift reactions from European mainstream parties and governments indicate the rise of the far right is no longer just an issue for a German local election, nor solely a German problem, but a pan-European one. He cautioned that influential European countries like France and Spain would soon face fierce competition from far-right parties as they head to the polls next year. "Current trends suggest that far-right parties are already gaining influence and consolidating their support in these countries. For mainstream parties and governments, this contest means not only that their long-standing dominance may gradually erode, potentially reducing them to marginal players, but also that the core principles they uphold could come under severe strain." Elections due Jian Junbo, a professor and director of the Center for China-Europe Relations at Fudan University, echoed this, suggesting that the AfD's decisive victory in Germany will instill considerable confidence in far-right parties in other countries to win their respective elections and create a powerful "demonstration effect" across Europe, signaling the rapid rise of far-right parties across the continent. Next year, several EU countries, collectively representing over half of the bloc's population, are due to hold national elections, including France, Greece, Poland and Spain. For mainstream parties in these countries, the outlook appears far from rosy. A research study led by Matthijs Rooduijn, a political scientist at the University of Amsterdam, for the PopuList survey, shows that European votes for far-right parties have grown nearly fivefold since the mid-1990s. Experts agree the sustained rise of far-right forces in Europe stems from a complex interplay of severe internal and external challenges facing the continent. "Economic problems, livelihood issues, and geopolitical dilemmas are deeply intertwined, yet mainstream parties have largely failed to offer effective solutions. As long as Europe's overall environment, including its economic and geopolitical situation, does not ease or change, the soil for far-right politics to grow will remain," Cui said. Citing Europe's unresolved issues, Wu said, "It's imaginable that right-wing populist or far-right parties could still rise to power in more countries, further pushing Europe toward conservatism." She outlined several profound shifts, anticipating possible drifting to more "national-interest-first" policies and immigration restrictions. Wu also suggested that euro-skeptic far-right parties changed their strategy about the EU and are trying to reform the EU from within, promoting a "national conservatism" centered on national interest and sovereignty. Furthermore, she said, "The far right's pro-Russia leanings could have impacts on the continent's security architecture." Cui highlighted the broader geopolitical ramifications, saying that the rightward-shifting political atmosphere in Europe would align its political trajectory more closely with that of the United States. "If far-right parties in various countries adopt national-interest-first policies after taking office, it would first weaken the momentum of European integration and sow greater trans-Atlantic discord, as prioritizing domestic interests over collective solutions would lead to increased trans-Atlantic conflicts." "In the interests of consensus the regional meeting set for tomorrow in Salalah has been postponed," Al Busaidi said on X. "We remain committed to fostering dialogue that supports stability and lasting cooperation in our region," he added. Confirming the meeting's deferral in an interview with Iran's official news agency IRNA, Mohammad Ali Bak, director general of the Persian Gulf at the Iranian Foreign Ministry, said it was postponed to another date at some regional countries' requests and based on a joint decision by Iran and Oman. The official stressed that Iran is in close consultations with Oman to ensure the necessary arrangements and coordination regarding the appropriate time for holding the meeting. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei announced on Friday that Gulf littoral states' foreign ministers were scheduled to meet in Oman on Monday to exchange views on regional issues, including the Iran-Oman talks on designating safe routes in the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking to Al Jazeera on Saturday, Baghaei said the gathering would "hopefully" be attended by foreign ministers from Gulf states as well as Iran and Iraq. body: Beijing, Colombo seek closer media ties - World - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE World Asia-Pacific Americas Europe Middle East Africa China-US China-Europe China-Japan China-Africa Home World / Asia-Pacific Home / World / Asia-Pacific Beijing, Colombo seek closer media ties By SHAO XINYING in Colombo, Sri Lanka | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:24 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Closer media cooperation is needed to build mutual trust, deepen understanding and strengthen ties between China and Sri Lanka, scholars and experts said at a media seminar in Colombo on Friday. "Media is no longer simply a means of transmitting information. It has become a powerful instrument for building understanding between societies and strengthening relations," said Kaushalya Ariyarathne, deputy minister of Mass Media of Sri Lanka, at the 2026 China-Sri Lanka Media Cooperation and Exchange Seminar. She highlighted recent progress in a program-sharing arrangement allowing 10 Chinese productions, including the science fiction series The Three-Body Problem , to be translated and broadcast in Sri Lanka. Wei Huaxiang, Chinese ambassador to Sri Lanka, said "the voices of developing countries remain relatively weak" in the global landscape. He called on media organizations from both countries to "strengthen coordination in international communication" and speak with a common voice on issues, including climate change, poverty reduction, development and global governance, while countering misinformation and misleading narratives. Shanika Sriyananda, a senior journalist of Daily Financial Times and former media director of the Ministry of Defense in Sri Lanka, recalled a moving moment from her trip to China's Yunnan province in June. Reflecting on the story of the ancient Chinese monk Faxian, who wept upon seeing a Chinese silk fan in ancient Sri Lanka, she said: "Something similar happened to me." After receiving a silk scarf with a heartwarming note from her Chinese friend, she said "tears came to my eyes", as she felt the bond of friendship between the two countries. Chen Wenling, a senior research fellow at the Academy of Contemporary China and World Studies, called for joint responses to shared global challenges, and the fostering of new values, worldviews and perspectives. New opportunities Underscoring China's advances in AI, Chen said large language models and other AI technologies are being rapidly applied across diverse industries. "This technological strength will present new opportunities for deeper China-Sri Lanka cooperation," she said. Wang Lei, a professor at the School of Government and director of the Center for BRICS Cooperation Studies at Beijing Normal University, said tea serves as a vivid illustration of deep cultural ties and a natural bridge for people-to-people connections between China and Sri Lanka. The two countries should deepen ties across media, think tanks, and academia to "bolster South-South cooperation and explore viable modernization paths for the Global South", he added. Tissa Ravinda Perera, a professor at the Faculty of Management and Finance of the University of Colombo, emphasized that media communication must not be one-way. "It should enable the Sri Lankan audience to understand China while allowing the Chinese audience to learn about Sri Lanka," he said. During the event, delegates witnessed the launch of the Colombo Initiative on China-Sri Lanka Media Cooperation and an accompanying action plan. The seminar brought together more than 80 guests from government agencies, media outlets, think tanks and universities in China and Sri Lanka. It was held ahead of the 70 years of diplomatic ties between China and Sri Lanka and the 75th anniversary of the signing of the Rubber-Rice Pact next year. Meanwhile, a China-Sri Lanka friendship organizations symposium was held in Colombo on Saturday, focusing on people-to-people connections. A "Southern Messengers" mobile bookcase was handed over to promote educational and cultural exchanges between the two countries. [Photo/Xinhua] LONDON -- The remarks of US President Donald Trump on the unification of Ireland and Britain's Northern Ireland have sparked strong opposition from Britain. During a two-day visit to Ireland, Trump said on Saturday he would "love to see" the unification of Ireland and Britain's Northern Ireland. "President Trump is shooting from the hip as usual, just like he did with Greenland and Canada becoming the 51st state," said Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch on X on Saturday. She added that "Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom." "I disagree with President Trump," said Reform UK leader Nigel Farage on X the same day, "Northern Ireland is a proud and integral part of the United Kingdom." body: Hongjiang ancient town: Where China’s commercial heritage lives on - China Bound — For a Wow China Experience! Destinations − Suzhou Dunhuang Yunnan Shanxi Scenic Spots World Heritage Sites Museums Plan Your Visit + Entering China How to Pay Helpful Tools Calls & Internet To Pack Getting Around Where to Stay Health & Safety Attractions Ticketing Etiquette & Culture Frequently Asked Questions Shopping Best Bites www.chinaservicesinfo.com www.chinadaily.com.cn Home > A Wow China Experience > Recommended Hongjiang ancient town: Where China’s commercial heritage lives on Updated: 2026-09-09 | China Bound [Photo provided to China Bound] Nestled at the confluence of the Yuanjiang and Wushui rivers in Huaihua, Hunan province, Hongjiang Ancient Commercial Town was once a major trading hub connecting Hunan, Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi and Sichuan. Known as the “Metropolis of Southwest China” and the “First Ancient Commercial Town in China”, it preserves more than 380 historical buildings dating from the Ming and Qing dynasties (1368-1911) to the Republic of China period (1912-49). Its distinctive layout of “seven lanes, eight alleys and nine streets” shapes the maze-like ancient town with stone-paved slopes lined with fortress-like yinzilou residences. High brick walls, few exterior windows and central courtyards reflect ingenious designs for ventilation, lighting, fire prevention and security, while intricate carvings, stone sculptures, firefighting water vats and historical plaques add to the town’s timeless charm. [Photo provided to China Bound] Yet Hongjiang is far from a museum frozen in time. More than 200 shops and stalls continue to bring the old commercial quarter to life, with restaurants, guesthouses, cultural stores and intangible cultural heritage experiences welcoming visitors. After dark, the streets take on a new atmosphere, illuminated for nighttime exploration as red lanterns glow against traditional buildings. Explore former banks, escort agencies (providing armed security services for merchants) and tax offices, watch immersive performances such as The Rise of the Commercial Town and A Matchmaking Proposal at the Qin Residence, and sample local specialties. It is a chance to step into the world of Hongjiang’s historical merchants while experiencing a vibrant town where the past remains part of everyday life. [Photo provided to China Bound] Who it’s for A rewarding destination for history buffs, travelers interested in Chinese commercial heritage, culture seekers and anyone curious about the evolution of trade and business in China. Best time to visit Summer brings lively festivals and outdoor performances, while the Spring Festival season features special cultural and tourism programs, including the Hongfu Hongjiang New Year celebrations. Don’t miss 1. Explore the world of Hongjiang’s merchants: Step inside historical buildings such as Shengfeng Bank, Zhongyi Escort Agency that provided armed security for merchants, the Lijin Bureau (a Qing Dynasty tax office), Tianjun Theater and Shaoxing Troupe, and catch a live performance. At Xufulong Merchant House, you can still see tools and equipment once used in the town’s tung-oil trade. 2. Marvel at the fortress-like yinzilou : These distinctive residences feature high walls, windowless exteriors and central courtyards, reflecting the Hongjiang merchants’ traditional wisdom of protecting and preserving their wealth. 3. Watch immersive live performances: Don’t miss nighttime productions such as The Rise of the Commercial Town and A Matchmaking Proposal at the Qin Residence , which bring the town’s colorful commercial history to life. 4. Taste local flavors: Try Hongjiang blood glutinous rice duck, a local specialty made by braising duck with glutinous-rice blood cakes. The town’s many snack stalls and restaurants offer plenty of other regional dishes to discover. Before you go 1. The town can get busy during peak seasons and public holidays. Visit early in the morning for a quieter and more relaxed experience. 2. Wear comfortable walking shoes, as the historical stone-paved streets can be uneven. 3. In summer, bring sun protection and stay hydrated. Spring and autumn are generally more comfortable for walking, though a light jacket is recommended. Practical essentials Address: Xinmin Lu, Yuanjiang Lu subdistrict, Hongjiang district, Huaihua, Hunan province Opening hours: 8 am-5:30 pm Getting there: By public transport: Take a high-speed train to Huaihua South Railway Station. From the Huaihua Comprehensive Transport Hub on the west side of the station, take the dedicated tourist shuttle bus to Hongjiang Ancient Commercial Town Visitor Center. The journey takes approximately 70-90 minutes, with tickets costing around 30 yuan ($4.45)/person. By car: Search for “Hongjiang Ancient Commercial Town (洪江古商城)” in your navigation app. Roads inside the historical town are narrow, so visitors arriving by car should park at designated parking areas outside the old town.
title: Hongjiang ancient town: Where China's commercial heritage lives on

Its name is associated with Laozi (Lao Tzu), the ancient Chinese philosopher and founder of Taoism who is said to have lived here in seclusion. Traditional Taoist temples stand among the summit peaks, often shrouded in clouds. From the mountaintop, visitors can enjoy sweeping views of the majestic mountains stretching across the vast Central Plains.

body: Team China ready to shine at U17 World Cup - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Sports Soccer Basketball Volleyball Tennis Golf Track & field Swimming Home / Sports Home / Sports Team China ready to shine at U17 World Cup Coach Ma hopes her players can show their true abilities as well as creativity to advance into the knockout stage Agencies | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:43 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE China's under-17 women's football team impressed with three group wins over U17 teams from Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Manchester City at last month's 2026 Shanghai Future Star Cup. [Photo/Xinhua] China's under-17 women's football team has concluded a monthlong training camp as coach Ma Xiaoxu prepares her young players for the FIFA U17 Women's World Cup in Morocco. "We certainly want to win because results are what count in competitive sports," Ma, 38, told Xinhua. "But I also hope the players can show their abilities on the World Cup stage without fear or restraint." China is in Group E with the United States, Samoa and Kenya. The top two teams from each group and the four best third-placed teams will advance to the knockout stage. "At this age, I hope they can show their true abilities from training, show creativity, make their own decisions on the field and enjoy the games," Ma said. "The experience of competing is the most important thing for their development. Meanwhile, we will certainly give everything to fight for the best possible results." Ma knows firsthand how important a youth World Cup can be. As an 18-year-old player in 2006, she helped China finish runner-up at the FIFA U20 Women's World Cup and won both the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player and the Golden Boot as its top scorer. That same year, she was named AFC Asian Player of the Year. Twenty years later, Ma is preparing for a global youth tournament on the other side of the touchline. "When I first took over this team, I felt like I suddenly went back to their age," Ma said. "Seeing their young energy and vitality was exciting for me and gave me motivation." However, Ma said she would not simply reproduce the methods that worked for her as a player. "Every player has a different path of development, and football is constantly evolving," she said. "I am also continuing to learn. I hope to teach them more advanced ideas and, after filtering out some of the problems I experienced before, give them better things. "I hope every player can have her own personality. As a coach, I need to think carefully and treat every player individually. The most important thing is to let them maintain their love for football. I think it is very important that they do not lose that love as they get older." China earned its World Cup berth by reaching the semifinals of the AFC U17 Women's Asian Cup in May. The team came back from two goals down to level the semifinal against defending champion the Democratic People's Republic of Korea at 2-2 before eventually losing 4-2. Ma said securing a World Cup place was the team's most basic objective. "Participating in a world-class tournament has a big impact on a player's development," she said. "Their future development will also help drive the overall development of Chinese women's football." The semifinal highlighted both the progress the team has made and the weaknesses Ma wants her players to address. Against the DPRK's high press, China tried to build through passing combinations from the back rather than repeatedly resorting to long balls. But mistakes under pressure gave their opponents opportunities to shoot. "I think we have to make some changes and not blindly play long balls," Ma said. "But that does not mean pursuing buildup from the back for its own sake. The most important thing is to get the ball behind the opponent's defense and into the penalty area to create dangerous attacks." Ma praised her players' execution but said they needed to improve their ability to adjust during matches. "The players have strong execution, but they still need to improve their ability to adapt during a game," she said. "Under high pressure, they may not even be able to hear some of the instructions we give from the sideline. "I hope they can bravely face the challenges of a high press. Results are certainly important, and we will try to win every game. But for 17-year-old players, I think it is more important in this process to develop the habit and awareness of thinking independently." Ma noted that 18 to 20 years old is an especially important period for young players to develop, and that playing overseas can expose them to higher-level competition. "I think those few years from 18 to 20 are when players improve the fastest," she said. "If they can experience higher-level leagues and have teammates with stronger technical and tactical abilities, they will gradually adapt to the pace and intensity of matches, learn how to make decisions more quickly under pressure and make better use of their bodies in physical confrontations." Ma has also used the past several months to develop as a coach. After completing the Asian Cup campaign, she briefly joined the women's national team coaching staff as an assistant to head coach Ante Milicic during the team's training camp and matches in central China's Wuhan. "For me, as a coach who has just started out, being able to work with a high-level foreign coach and see their working methods, their thinking and how they organize training camps has been very helpful," Ma said. "The national team coaching staff are very open. Whenever I have questions, they are willing to help." body: Rybakina on top of world - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Sports Soccer Basketball Volleyball Tennis Golf Track & field Swimming Home / Sports Home / Sports Rybakina on top of world Ruthless Kazakh dethrones Sabalenka to capture first US Open crown Agencies | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:45 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina celebrates with the winner's trophy after her final win against Belarus' Aryna Sabalenka. Rybakina delivered a devastating display to dethrone two-time defending champion Sabalenka with a 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 win in the US Open final on Saturday, earning a third Grand Slam crown to accompany her ascent to world No 1. [Photo/Agencies] NEW YORK — Elena Rybakina came to New York and took everything that had belonged to Aryna Sabalenka. First, it was the No 1 ranking in women's tennis, then the US Open trophy. The tournament that for so long was a struggle for Rybakina turned into the site of her coronation. Rybakina won her first US Open title and punctuated her climb to the top of her sport by beating Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 on Saturday. Rybakina had already been guaranteed to replace Sabalenka at No 1 in the rankings this week and for good measure took the title that Sabalenka had won the previous two years. "It's still so difficult to process what happened," Rybakina said. "Too many achievements these few weeks." It was the third Grand Slam title for Rybakina and the second this year — both against Sabalenka on hard courts. She opened the season by beating Sabalenka for the Australian Open title. This time, Rybakina stopped Sabalenka's 19-match winning streak at the US Open, where she hadn't lost since falling to Coco Gauff in the 2023 final. Rybakina earned $5.5 million, the largest prize in Grand Slam history, and tied Sabalenka and French Open winner Mirra Andreeva with a tour-high three titles this season. Elena Rybakina serves against Aryna Sabalenka during the women's singles final of the US Open. [Photo/Agencies] Sabalenka falls short Sabalenka took home $2.8 million but it was clear how little that meant to her, as she smashed her racket after a brief hug with Rybakina at the net. Sabalenka was trying to become the first person since Serena Williams from 2012-14 to win three in a row at Flushing Meadows. "I was just out there competing, trying to do my best with what I had there today," Sabalenka said. "Not good enough." Rybakina dethroned the champ without even bringing her best service game. The WTA Tour leader in aces got less than half of her first serves in but instead put Sabalenka under constant pressure with a strong return game, racking up 12 break chances and converting three, which was all she needed. The third meeting of No 1 vs No 2 in a US Open women's final since 2000 was the first to go the way of the challenger. Williams was the top seed for the other two, beating her sister Venus in 2002 and Victoria Azarenka in 2013. The numbers didn't signify much this time, because they were going to flip Monday. Sabalenka had held the top spot for 99 consecutive weeks, but Rybakina gained enough points to unseat her simply by reaching the semifinals. The 27-year-old who was born in Russia but represents Kazakhstan won her first major title at Wimbledon in 2022 and now needs just the French Open to complete the career Grand Slam. And it's clear her power — and her ability to absorb her opponent's — was something that unnerved Sabalenka. "Her serve is amazing, the way she's able to step in and overpower you on court, and especially if it's a US Open court where it's super fast, it's definitely a huge advantage for her," Sabalenka said. "A lot of things make her dangerous." A native of Belarus, Sabalenka sometimes swings from her heels, like a golfer trying to unleash a 300-yard drive, grunting "Aaaaahhhh!" as she takes her mighty cuts. Rybakina's power comes more easily. There is little sound coming from her side of the net besides the squeaking of her sneakers, and she rarely shows any hint of stress. "I think Elena is probably — not nonchalant, I don't want to say that, because she's not nonchalant — but just no reaction ever," Gauff said after losing to Rybakina in the semifinals. Rybakina did show some frustration after pulling a backhand wide with a break point in the opening game of the third set, but soon she had taken charge of the match for good. Sabalenka had won the two other meetings this season, on the hard courts at Indian Wells and Miami, and leads their rivalry 10-8. But her season has taken a dip after those victories. Sabalenka fell to Naomi Osaka in the fourth round at Wimbledon, then returned to action with consecutive fourth-round exits in Toronto and Cincinnati. Learn to love New York Rybakina had to take a brief break after she was forced to stop playing in her quarterfinal match against Iga Swiatek in Cincinnati because of a foot injury, but she recovered in time for a tournament where she had never done particularly well previously, failing to advance past the fourth round until this year. "I have come here for the last 10 years, and it was never successful — nothing close to that," Rybakina said. "It's just incredible. I'm falling in love with New York more and more." The Arthur Ashe Stadium, meanwhile, had been Sabalenka's house, with four straight trips to the final and six to at least the semis. Whatever troubled her during the summer seemed forgotten once she was back in New York — until Saturday. Sabalenka repeatedly looked toward her coaches' box with her palms up, wondering why everything was going so poorly, and showed much more frustration than that when she double-faulted to hand Rybakina a 3-2 lead in the first set. Rybakina hit the serve back and the ball bounced directly to Sabalenka, who whacked it into the crowd, earning a warning from the chair umpire. Sabalenka eventually began putting consistent pressure on Rybakina in the second set. She picked up two break points with a chance to end the set with a 5-4 lead, and though Rybakina won four straight points to get out of that jam, Sabalenka got another chance in the next service game and this time capitalized, stepping into a return to set up a miss by Rybakina. Belarus' Aryna Sabalenka smashes her racquet after losing her women's singles final match. [Photo/Agencies]
title: Rybakina on top of world

body: What China has taught me about cooperation - Opinion - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Opinion Cartoons Editorials Global Lens We Comment Columnists Global Views Chinese Perspectives Opinion Line Home Opinion / Global Lens Home / Opinion / Global Lens What China has taught me about cooperation By Hodan Osman Abdi | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:35 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE LI MIN/CHINA DAILY My relationship with China spans more than 20 years, and during this time I have absorbed many habits and perspectives that have profoundly influenced my outlook on life, development and international cooperation. Much of that influence lies not in grand theories, but in the daily details of life. My family often laughs at me because drinking a cup of hot water is my remedy to every ailment. It is a simple habit I picked up in China, perhaps unwittingly. But beyond these small habits lies a deeper understanding of how people and countries can work together, a perspective shaped significantly by China's culture and philosophy. As Somalia's ambassador to China, I have been particularly influenced by the concept of "harmony in diversity". This principle, which I have come to appreciate deeply, does not mean enforcing uniformity or compelling others to obey a single set of rules. It is about accepting differences while finding common ground, so that people can move in the same direction in harmony and embark on broader cooperation. When I first came to China, I was driven by personal goals: earning a bachelor's degree by a certain age, followed by a master's degree, and eventually a doctorate. My first stop was Beijing, and from there I took a train to Yangzhou in Jiangsu province. It was a long journey, with the old-fashioned train stopping every half an hour. I was in a sleeper car and got off at every stop to ask the conductor, "Are we in Yangzhou yet?" The answer was always: no, no, no. Today, the same journey from Beijing to Yangzhou takes around five hours by bullet train, a testament to the phenomenal progress made by China in just a few decades. Many people say China's development is a miracle. But I do not think "miracle" fully describes what we are seeing. Many people have worked very hard, and worked together, to make this happen. China has shown me how a country can handle problems, keep moving forward and turn long-term effort into tangible change in people's everyday lives. This has also shaped my understanding of the concept of "harmony in diversity". There is a similar idea in traditional Somali culture. If everyone can gather under a tree, put all their issues on the table and talk, they can resolve their differences. This is especially important today, as Somalia and China have elevated their bilateral ties to a strategic partnership amid Somalia's major reconstruction efforts. There are many areas of cooperation that need to be pushed forward, and that responsibility weighs heavily on me. In China, I have observed an approach that begins by listening to a partner's needs and then tailoring solutions accordingly. The goal is not simply to solve a problem for someone, but to empower others to solve future problems. As the saying goes, "Give a man a fish and he will eat for a day; teach him how to fish and he will eat for a lifetime." This philosophy resonates with Somalia's development journey. The bustling hub of Lido Beach in Mogadishu symbolizes Somalia's reconstruction. No one could have imagined such a scene in the past. Chinese infrastructure projects have played an important role in Somalia, including a major highway built in the 1970s and still in use today. It's an approach that looks to the future and empowers people to pull themselves out of their plight. Against this background, I recommended in late 2016 or early 2017 that Somalia join the Belt and Road Initiative. In 2018, I had the honor of accompanying the then president of Somalia to China to sign the memorandum of understanding for our participation in the initiative. My bond with China, therefore, is not only about the changes I have witnessed over the past two decades. It is also about what those experiences have taught me about cooperation. Governance at its core is not about systems or acronyms. It is about people, and ensuring that nations on the margins feel included at the table. Global governance should be an invitation for everyone to understand and learn from one another, not a fixed formula that everyone must follow. An open approach means accepting differences, finding common ground and promoting cooperation in ways that allow human civilization as a whole to move forward. The author is the ambassador of the Federal Republic of Somalia to China. This article is based on an interview by Jiao Jie for China Daily's "Hello, Diplomat" series. body: Shared Himalayan pain, shared call for climate justice - Opinion - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Opinion Cartoons Editorials Global Lens We Comment Columnists Global Views Chinese Perspectives Opinion Line Home Opinion / Global Lens Home / Opinion / Global Lens Shared Himalayan pain, shared call for climate justice By Saroj Gautam | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:28 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE SONG CHEN/CHINA DAILY On the morning of Aug 26, a section of a glacier in the Himalayas plunged into the Lhende River, a tributary of Nepal's Bhote Koshi River, blocking it with a wall of ice, rock and mud. When that improvised dam gave way, it sent a flood surging down the Trishuli corridor, before slamming into Gyirong Port on the Chinese side. The death toll is still rising. It was, by any measure, a disaster the region's riparian communities had never witnessed. Thousands of families on both sides of the border are still waiting for loved ones who may never return. Whole villages were swept away; parents lost children, and children lost parents. The pain of waiting to know whether people are going to come back is unspeakable. As Global South countries, China and Nepal share a similar trajectory of development, while bearing far less historical responsibility for carbon emissions, the major source of current climate change and effects. Whatever else divides Nepal and China along their 1,400-km border, the response to the calamity showed what functioning neighborly cooperation looks like during an emergency. China activated a Level-II national disaster relief emergency response covering all affected people regardless of nationality. Its Ministry of Emergency Management dispatched tunnel-rescue specialists to Nepal, while PLA Air Force Y-20 aircraft carried tents, blankets, sleeping bags, rations and first-aid kits from Chengdu, China's Sichuan province, to Kathmandu. China's Ministry of Natural Resources shared satellite and hydrological data with its Nepali counterpart and began releasing 3D reconstructions of the collapse. Premier Li Qiang visited the areas affected by the disaster to supervise rescue operations, reflecting a coherent political and operational response. The foreign ministries of China and Nepal have maintained continuous communication. China has expressed its readiness to offer additional support tailored to the needs of Nepal. Scientists call this system — the Hindu Kush Himalayan range and the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau — the Third Pole or Asian Water Tower: the largest freshwater reserve outside the two poles, and the source of the Indus, Ganges, Brahmaputra, Yangtze and Mekong rivers, on which nearly two billion people depend. That system has warmed roughly 0.42°C per decade since 1980, nearly double the global average, destabilizing glaciers and multiplying unstable lakes at altitudes hardest to survey or instrument. A joint ICIMOD-UNDP assessment identified 3,624 glacial lakes across the region, 47 potentially dangerous, including 21 in Nepal. Aug 26 was not an anomaly: this was the third major glacier — or lake-triggered flood to strike the corridor in just over a year, following a July 2025 flood in Xizang autonomous region that swept away the Miteri Bridge linking the two countries. The pattern is no longer anomalous, it is structural. Despite scientific evidence of climate change affecting the Himalayas during challenging times, there is a tendency among certain individuals to lay the blame on China for various issues, including natural disasters. In the wake of a recent flood, some people began to criticize China before any scientific evidence was assessed. It is essential to recognize that China is also a developing nation undergoing significant modernization, and no political system can entirely prevent natural disasters. Historically, China has faced numerous devastating natural events such as earthquakes, floods, typhoons, and landslides, many of which are exacerbated by climate change. Despite these challenges, China is positioning itself to take a leading role in green development and resilience against future natural disasters. Its installed renewable capacity passed 2,337 gigawatts in 2025, with wind and solar overtaking thermal power in its installed capacity for the first time, and its renewable output, roughly 4 trillion kilowatt-hours, now exceeds the European Union's entire consumption. That build-out is going global: Chinese solar and wind exports reached roughly $29 billion, with Global South sales growing fastest, and Beijing's overseas cooperation has shifted toward smaller, community-scale projects suited to remote terrain. Its $3.1 billion China South-South Climate Cooperation Fund was built as a developing-country adaptation vehicle outside the traditional donor-recipient model. The Asian Water Tower belongs to neither country alone, and the injustice it is delivering was manufactured by neither. What Aug 26 offers, alongside its grief, is unusually clear evidence for an argument long made quietly: that a region contributing almost nothing to the emissions warming its own glaciers has a legitimate claim on the finance and technology of the states most responsible for that warming. Whether this becomes a footnote or a turning point depends on whether Kathmandu, Beijing and the wider Global South press that case together, before the next glacier moves. The author is a researcher at the Center for Nepal Studies, East China University of Technology. The views don't necessarily reflect those of China Daily. body: AI opening new pathways for SMEs to 'go digital' - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Business Macro Companies Industries Technology Motoring China Data Finance Top 10 Home / Business / Technology Home Business Technology AI opening new pathways for SMEs to 'go digital' China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:25 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Visitors experience virtual reality glasses from a Chinese technology firm during the 32nd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Small and Medium Enterprises Ministerial Meeting in Guangzhou, Guangdong province, on Sept 1. CHEN CHUHONG/CHINA NEWS SERVICE GUANGZHOU — On a production line at Seng Fong Holdings Berhad in Malaysia, a robotic arm grips a 35-kilogram block of rubber, with 3D cameras, laser scanners and artificial intelligence algorithms serving as its "eyes" and "brain". The setup is designed to tackle a longstanding challenge in the traditionally labor-intensive rubber processing industry. Rubber blocks coming out of drying ovens vary in shape, making them difficult for conventional robotic systems to handle. Developed by an AI company in China's southern Guangdong province, the solution has enabled the Malaysian rubber processor to automate more of the handling process, cutting labor costs by 20 to 30 percent while improving management efficiency, according to the company's chairman. The case points to a broader shift taking place across the Asia-Pacific region. AI is creating new opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises to innovate, while deeper regional connectivity is helping them turn technological advances into new sources of growth. That trend was reflected at the 32nd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Small and Medium Enterprises Ministerial Meeting, held recently in Guangzhou, capital of Guangdong, as officials from APEC economies gathered to explore how technological innovation can empower SMEs and drive their further development. SMEs are a major pillar of the regional economy. As technological and industrial transformation accelerates and global supply chains undergo profound changes, AI and other emerging technologies are creating both new opportunities and new challenges for SMEs across the Asia-Pacific region. AI-powered robotics are opening up new pathways for the digital transformation of SMEs, while open-source technologies are further lowering the barriers to technology access and application, enabling more businesses to participate in technological innovation, said Yang Qian, co-founder and chief operating officer of the Shenzhen-based embodied AI startup X Square Robot, at a parallel forum held alongside the ministerial meeting. "What once required six months, costly computing power and a professional team can now be done in three days with a workstation and an idea," she said. "This gives SMEs, for the first time, a more level playing field with industry giants in innovation." Yet SMEs across the region still face challenges, such as high digital transformation costs and talent shortages, highlighting the need for greater regional cooperation. Kwon Jong-hyun, vice-chairman of the Beijing Chapter of the World-OKTA, cited embodied intelligence as an example, saying China's strengths lie in scale and speed, while those of the Republic of Korea lie in precision and reliability. Such cooperation, he said, is not simply about adding strengths together, but about multiplying their impact by combining complementary capabilities. China's experience in supporting SMEs' digital transformation offers one example. The latest move came on Sept 4, when the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology released an action plan to support AI entrepreneurship among SMEs for 2026-28. The plan aims to foster more than 10,000 technology-based and innovative SMEs, more than 2,000 "little giant" firms, as well as a number of gazelle companies and unicorns. It is also advancing the establishment of AI application cooperation centers with member countries of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations with overseas branches in Laos, Malaysia and Vietnam already operational. These centers promote cross-border cooperation in large models, the data industry, and smart agriculture, bringing Chinese solutions together with local partners. China stands ready to work with all parties to help more SMEs thrive and grow, Vice-Premier Zhang Guoqing said in a speech delivered at the opening ceremony of the meeting. body: RMB internationalization 2.0: Where business flows, ecosystem grows - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Business Macro Companies Industries Technology Motoring China Data Finance Top 10 Home / Business / Policies Home Business Policies RMB internationalization 2.0: Where business flows, ecosystem grows By Jean Lu | China Daily | Updated: 2026-09-14 09:50 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Renminbi internationalization is entering what I would call its 2.0 window. The question is no longer simply whether the RMB appears in more cross-border transactions, but whether companies and investors are using it as a full-fledged international currency — to hold, hedge, invest and finance in ways that align naturally with their business needs. The shift is already visible in the data. According to the People's Bank of China — the country's central bank — overseas RMB loans rose 31.7 percent year-on-year in the first half. More broadly, the RMB is now the leading currency for China's cross-border receipts and payments, and the world's second most-used currency in trade finance. Two forces are driving this. The global monetary system is becoming more multipolar, creating greater demand for alternatives to overreliance on a single currency. At the same time, as global supply chains shift, Chinese companies are operating overseas in new ways — building factories, hiring locally and integrating more deeply into regional markets. Consider a Chinese manufacturer building capacity in Southeast Asia, the Middle East or Europe. Its parent company keeps its books in RMB. Some equipment and components still come from China. Local wages and taxes are paid in local currency, while some global inputs may still be priced in US dollars. In that setting, using RMB for China-related payments becomes a natural business choice: it reduces currency mismatch, lowers funding costs and creates a natural hedge. This is where RMB internationalization 2.0 becomes tangible: in contracts, working capital, treasury and investment decisions. A currency becomes international when businesses keep choosing it because it works. For this ecosystem to grow sustainably, four pillars must reinforce one another. First, the offshore RMB pool must deepen alongside demand. A deeper pool supports efficient pricing, market confidence and resilience. Hong Kong already processes around 75 percent of global offshore RMB payments, yet liquidity has not always kept pace with expanding settlement, financing and investment needs. Encouragingly, the gap is narrowing. In July 2026, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority further increased the size of the Renminbi Business Facility from 200 billion yuan ($29.8 billion) to 500 billion yuan, reflecting strong take-up and reinforcing Hong Kong's role as a scalable offshore RMB liquidity hub supporting real-economy financing. As one of Hong Kong's three note-issuing banks, Standard Chartered sees rising settlement volumes firsthand. The priority now is to deepen the pool, broaden liquidity-management tools and help funding flow more readily to genuine commercial demand. Second, the RMB must also reach a broader circle of markets and businesses. China's local-currency swap agreements with more than 30 countries and regions provide an important foundation. Traditionally viewed as emergency backstops, their actual use has remained limited. As global trade and investment patterns evolve, they can increasingly support liquidity for day-to-day commercial activity. The opportunity is to turn this policy network into an ecosystem of commercial use — by enabling companies, financial institutions and investors to encounter and choose the RMB naturally in trade and investment. As swap lines become bridges for ordinary transactions, the RMB's international role can grow more sustainably. Third, beyond settlement, the RMB must also offer investors more reasons — and more ways — to hold it. Settlement may be the entry point; investment and financing create a lasting cycle of demand. Beyond highly liquid government bonds and the dim sum bond market, choices have historically been narrow. Deeper credit markets and a broader range of derivatives — including swaps — would give overseas investors more flexibility to allocate capital and manage risk. Encouragingly, the market is gaining both depth and breadth. In the first half, Panda bond issuances exceeded 160 billion yuan, up 69 percent year-on-year, while broadly defined dim sum bond issuances surpassed 900 billion yuan, an increase of around 50 percent. Product innovation is advancing in tandem. In May, Standard Chartered China supported a qualified foreign investor in completing a Chinese government bond futures transaction on the China Financial Futures Exchange — the first participation by an overseas institution in China's onshore government bond futures market. Just last month, Standard Chartered also participated in the inaugural transactions in five-year offshore Chinese government bond futures, giving international investors a more efficient and transparent tool to manage interest-rate risk. The next step is to build a fuller ecosystem of RMB-denominated assets, credit products, collateral and hedging tools — making the RMB a credible investment choice rather than a cost to manage. And fourth, none of this can happen at scale without infrastructure that continues to evolve. The Cross-border Interbank Payment System is central to this evolution, making cross-border RMB transactions more efficient and secure. CIPS is expanding steadily, with the value of transactions processed recording a compound annual growth rate of more than 21 percent between 2023 and 2025. But building the channel is only the beginning. Liquidity, products and business flows must move through it at scale. As the first foreign bank to become a direct CIPS participant both onshore and offshore, Standard Chartered has seen that link first-hand. Our role has been to bring more institutions into the network and channel more business flows through it. In 2025, Standard Chartered China and Standard Chartered Hong Kong served more indirect participants than any other foreign bank, while ranking among the leading direct participants by transaction value. Digital infrastructure provides a further boost. Together, mBridge and Cross-border e-CNY Transfer Services provide complementary rails that shorten settlement routes and reduce time and cost. They augment existing infrastructure by making cross-border RMB flows more automated and easier to embed in business activity, though both are still in early stages of adoption. These market developments are underpinned by clear and sustained policy support, including in China's 15th Five-Year Plan. We see Shanghai and Hong Kong each have a distinct but complementary role to play — as China's financial "twin engines". Shanghai's strength lies in the depth of the onshore market and its potential to develop more RMB-denominated assets and risk-management tools. Hong Kong brings offshore liquidity, global connectivity and its established role as a leading offshore RMB hub. The tide is already rising. Making the RMB easier to use, hedge, invest and finance will give companies more tools to navigate a complex operating environment, while supporting China's high-quality opening-up and a more balanced global financial system. Ultimately, the global economy will benefit from the deepening internationalization of the RMB. The writer is CEO & executive vice-chair of Standard Chartered China. body: تنگه هرمز در حالی به یکی از اصلیترین کانونهای رویارویی ایران و آمریکا تبدیل شده که همزمان تلاشهای دیپلماتیک برای مدیریت بحران نیز با موانع جدی روبهرو شده است. در تازهترین تحولات، یک کشتی تجاری ایرانی در نزدیکی قشم هدف قرار گرفت و یک نفر کشته و چند نفر زخمی شدند؛ از سوی دیگر، نشست برنامهریزیشده ایران و کشورهای خلیج فارس برای بررسی وضعیت کشتیرانی در هرمز به تعویق افتاد. ادامه حملات و توقیف یا تهدید نفتکشها، کاهش شدید تردد دریایی و گسترش ناامنی به دیگر مسیرهای راهبردی منطقه، نگرانیها درباره اختلال طولانیمدت در جریان صادرات انرژی و افزایش فشار بر بازار جهانی نفت را تشدید کرده است. پ ، پـ تبلیغات تبلیغات جنگ ایران و آمریکا: روز صد و هشتاد و نهم : آنچه باید بدانید اصابت به یک کشتی تجاری ایرانی در نزدیکی قشم: یک کشتی تجاری ایرانی در نزدیکی جزیره قشم و در محدوده تنگه هرمز هدف قرار گرفت. رسانههای دولتی ایران از کشته شدن یک نفر و زخمی شدن چند نفر خبر دادهاند؛ عامل حمله هنوز بهطور رسمی مشخص نشده و آمریکا نیز مسئولیت آن را نپذیرفته است. نشست ایران و کشورهای خلیج فارس درباره هرمز به تعویق افتاد: نشست برنامهریزیشده برای امروز در عمان با هدف بررسی سازوکار عبور کشتیها از تنگه هرمز به تعویق افتاد. اختلاف میان کشورهای شورای همکاری خلیج فارس، بهویژه درباره توافق ایران و عمان، عامل اصلی این تعویق عنوان شده است. بحران هرمز به بابالمندب هم سرایت کرده است: همزمان با بحران هرمز، حوثیها، فشار بر مسیر کشتیرانی بابالمندب را افزایش دادهاند و طبق گزارشهای جدید یک جزیره راهبردی در این آبراه را در اختیار گرفتهاند. این تحول، نگرانیها درباره شکلگیری یک بحران همزمان در دو گلوگاه اصلی انرژی جهان را افزایش داده است. حملات به زیرساختهای نفتی عربستان، فشار را بر بازار نفت بیشتر کرده است: رویترز گزارش داده که حملات اخیر به زیرساختهای انتقال نفت عربستان، همراه با اختلال در هرمز و بابالمندب، ظرفیت صادرات نفت منطقه را بهشدت کاهش داده است. قیمت نفت نیز به بالای ۱۰۰ دلار در هر بشکه رسیده و بازار با نگرانی درباره طولانی شدن بحران مواجه است. ترامپ: جنگ ایران میتواند طولانیتر از انتظار ادامه پیدا کند: در تازهترین ارزیابیها، دولت ترامپ خود را برای ادامهدار شدن بحران آماده میکند. رویترز گزارش داده که رئیسجمهور آمریکا انتظار دارد جنگ و فشار بر ایران ممکن است تا انتخابات میاندورهای آمریکا در نوامبر ادامه پیدا کند؛ موضوعی که نشان میدهد واشنگتن فعلاً نشانهای از پایان سریع درگیری نمیبیند. تبلیغات ۰۹:۲۴:۳۶ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ ایستگاه پمپاژ نفت عربستان تقریباً بهطور کامل تخریب شد امروز شرکت Vantor Technologies تصاویر ماهوارهای با وضوح بالا از خسارات واردشده به ایستگاه پمپاژ خط لوله شرق ـ غرب عربستان سعودی در المصبعة (Al-Mesba'ah) با مختصات 23.9565، 40.0538 منتشر کرد. به نظر میرسد این ایستگاه تقریباً بهطور کامل تخریب شده است. مقامهای سعودی اعلام کردند که این حمله از خاک عراق انجام شده. ۰۹:۱۹:۱۷ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ ادعای بلومبرگ: دولت ترامپ از ورود رئیس سازمان انرژی اتمی ایران به کنفرانس آژانس بینالمللی انرژی اتمی در وین جلوگیری کرد ۰۸:۵۹:۱۴ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ وزیر انرژی عمان: تنگه هرمز باز خواهد شد به گزارش فرارو، وزیر انرژی عمان گفت: تنگه هرمز باز خواهد شد و احتمالاً اختلالات ایجادشده در آن کوتاهمدت خواهد بود. باید مسیرهای خروج نفت متنوع و گزینههای جایگزین صادرات، چه از طریق عمان و چه یمن، تعیین شود. خوشحالم که عمان همچنان قادر به ادامه تولید نفت و گاز است. افزایش شدید قیمت نفت و گاز طبیعی مایع برای همه پایدار نیست ۰۸:۴۷:۳۵ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ ترامپ: واشنگتن در نهایت ایران را ترک میکند ترامپ در جریان سفر به ایرلند و هنگام حضور در مسابقات گلف آزاد ایرلند، در پاسخ به پرسشی درباره اینکه آیا آمریکا پس از جنگ ایران را ترک خواهد کرد، گفت واشنگتن در نهایت ایران را ترک میکند، مگر اینکه تصمیم بگیرد در این کشور بماند و «مثل ونزوئلا نفت را نگه دارد». ۰۸:۴۲:۱۹ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ مهمترین تحولات نفت برنت به ۱۰۸ دلار در هر بشکه رسید و نفت آمریکا نیز ۱۰۳.۲۲ دلار معامله شد. عبور کشتیها از تنگه هرمز به کمتر از ۱۰ فروند در روز کاهش یافته است. آمریکا مسیر ۱۰۱ کشتی تجاری را در تنگه هرمز تغییر داده است. عربستان چند بار درباره خطر احتمالی در خمیس مشیط و ابها هشدار داد و سپس هشدارها را لغو کرد. وزیران خارجه عراق و امارات درباره روابط دوجانبه و امنیت منطقه گفتوگو کردند. کریس مورفی، سناتور آمریکایی : جنگ با ایران به نفع تندروها در تهران است. عمان نشست منطقهای برای امضای توافق درباره تنگه هرمز را به تعویق انداخت ۹ فرمانده تحت حمایت عربستان در عملیات بابالمندب کشته و زخمی شدند/فرارو ۰۸:۳۷:۱۵ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ روایت خلبان آمریکایی از لحظات پس از سرنگونی جنگندهاش بر فراز ایران براوو، خلبان آمریکایی که جنگندهاش بر فراز ایران سرنگون شده بود، میگوید: پس از اجکت، بر اثر برخورد با زمین، کمر، بازو و شانهام شکست و در درهای محاصره شده با صخرهها گیر افتادم ۰۸:۳۱:۳۵ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ ادعای فرمانده سنتکام: نگرانیای درباره کمبود مهمات برای مقابله با حملات ایران نداریم برد کوپر، فرمانده سنتکام ادعا کرد: نگرانیای درباره کمبود مهمات برای مقابله با حملات موشکی و پهپادی ایران نداریم. وی مدعی شد: نیروهای ما بهخوبی مسلح هستند و برای هر شرایط اضطراری آمادهاند. ۰۸:۲۲:۱۲ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ عربستان خواستار اصلاح توافق ایران و عمان درباره تنگه هرمز شد ادعای باراک راوید، خبرنگار اکسیوس: یک مقام خلیج فارس به من گفت که عربستان سعودی اصلاحاتی را در پیشنهاد عمان و ایران درباره تنگه هرمز ارائه کرده است؛ زیرا ریاض نگرانیهایی داشت مبنی بر اینکه متن پیشنهادی میتواند عملاً به ایجاد یک وضعیت موجود جدید در تنگه هرمز منجر شود که برای عربستان یا دیگر کشورهای شورای همکاری خلیج فارس قابل قبول نباشد. ۰۸:۱۶:۴۹ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ جهش ۳ درصدی نفت؛ برنت به ۱۰۸ دلار رسید قیمت نفت در آغاز معاملات هفته حدود ۳ درصد افزایش یافت و بهای نفت برنت با عبور از ۱۰۷ دلار، به ۱۰۸ دلار در هر بشکه رسید. نفت آمریکا نیز از ۱۰۲ دلار در هر بشکه فراتر رفت. ۰۸:۰۳:۴۷ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ اولین تصاویر از عملیات نجات خلبان و افسر تسلیحات جنگنده اف 15 سرنگون شده در ایران ۰۷:۵۷:۱۹ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ واکنش ترامپ به ادعای کمک چین به ایران در حمله به پایگاه آمریکا در حالیکه گزارشها از ارائه تصاویر ماهوارهای یک پایگاه آمریکایی در اردن به ایران پیش از حمله مرگبار موشکی حکایت دارد، دونالد ترامپ با کاستن از اهمیت این موضوع گفت چین همان کاری را انجام میدهد که آمریکا انجام میدهد. ۰۷:۲۰:۳۲ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ ادعای درخواست کمک بنسلمان از اسرائیل برای ممانعت از بستن تنگه باب المندب روزنامه اسرائیل هیوم مدعی شد محمد بنسلمان، ولیعهد عربستان برای جلوگیری از بستن تنگه استراتژیک بابالمندب توسط انصارالله یمن از اسرائیل درخواست کمک اطلاعاتی کرده است . ۰۶:۵۷:۲۵ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ تصاویر ماهوارهای از خسارت به یک ایستگاه پمپاژ خط لوله نفت شرق به غرب عربستان پس از حملات اخیر ۰۶:۴۶:۴۴ ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ اگر از اخبار جا ماندهاید... تفاهم تهران و مسقط بر سر هرمز؛ راهی برای کاهش تنش یا آغاز فصل تازه جنگ میان ایران و آمریکا؟ فشار آمریکا مانع حضور رئیس سازمان انرژی اتمی ایران در کنفرانس آژانس شد رایزنی فشرده قطر با عربستان، اردن و کویت پس از به تعویق افتادن نشست صلاله تلاش عربستان برای اصلاح متن پیشنهادی عمان و ایران درباره تنگه هرمز روایت خلبان آمریکایی از سقوط جنگندهاش در ایران/ کمر، بازو و شانهام شکست و در درهای محاصره شده با صخرهها گیر افتادم بیشتر بدانید: جنگ ایران و آمریکا تبلیغات ترامپ: جنگ ایران پس از انتخابات تمام میشود آیا جی دی ونس میتواند مسیر جنگ را تغییر دهد؟ هندسهی جدید قدرت؛ تقاطع هرمز و بابالمندب
title: نشست عمان به تعویق افتاد

body: نرخ هر گرم طلا ۱۸ عیار به نیمه اول کانال ۲۳ میلیون برگشت. یعنی تقریبا ۱۸۰ درصد بالاتر از ۲۳ شهریور پارسال پ ، پـ تبلیغات تبلیغات فرارو - قیمت هر گرم طلا 18 عیار امروز دوشنبه 23 شهریور پیش از شروع معاملات بازار 23 میلیون و 476 هزار تومان ثبت شد. به گزارش فرارو ؛ قیمت طلا 18 عیار روز گذشته از مرز 24 میلیون پایین آمد و حدود نیم میلیون تومان به ازای هر گرم تقلیل پیدا کرد. قیمت طلا 18 عیار البته در بازه یکماهه رشد 22 درصدی داشته و از یک 23 شهریور پارسال تا امروز شاهد جهش 180 درصدی قیمت طلا بودهایم. تبلیغات قیمت محصولات ایرانخودرو و سایپا امروز دوشنبه ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ قیمت روز خودرو | جدول جدید امروز قیمت طلا امروز دوشنبه ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ قیمت دلار امروز دوشنبه ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ بیشتر بدانید: قیمت طلا قیمت طلا 18 عیار طلا 18 عیار تبلیغات قیمت دلار امروز دوشنبه ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ قیمت دینار عراق امروز دوشنبه ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ قیمت درهم امارات امروز دوشنبه ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵

body: قیمت دلار از مرز ۲۳۰ هزار تومان عقب رفت اما بازدهی ماهانه آن کماکان حدود ۲۰ درصد است پ ، پـ تبلیغات تبلیغات فرارو - قیمت دلار در بازار آزاد امروز دوشنبه 23 شهریور پیش از شروع خریدوفروشهای بازار در محدوده 228 هزار و 600 تومان ایستاد. به گزارش فرارو ؛ نرخ دلار آزاد روز گذشته از مرز 230 هزار تومان عقب رفت اما همچنان در بازه یکماهه شاهد رشد تقریبا 20 درصدی قیمت دلار هستیم. قیمت دلار 23 شهریور سال قبل در محدوده 101 هزار تومان حضور داشت و در این مدت حدود 130 درصد ارتقا پیدا کرده است. تبلیغات قیمت محصولات ایرانخودرو و سایپا امروز دوشنبه ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ قیمت روز خودرو | جدول جدید امروز قیمت طلا امروز دوشنبه ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ قیمت دلار امروز دوشنبه ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ بیشتر بدانید: قیمت دلار دلار آزاد قیمت دلار آزاد تبلیغات قیمت دینار عراق امروز دوشنبه ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ قیمت درهم امارات امروز شنبه ۲۱ شهریور ۱۴۰۵ قیمت طلا امروز دوشنبه ۲۳ شهریور ۱۴۰۵
