Как сообщают корреспонденты «Хроники Туркменистана», после увеличения штрафов для лиц, торгующих в не предназначенных для этого местах, личный интерес полицейских к борьбе с этим видом правонарушений резко возрос. Не имеющие работы люди зарабатывают на жизнь, покупая оптом и продавая в розницу молочные продукты, виноград, сухофрукты, варёную кукурузу и другие товары возле рынков, магазинов, больниц, банков и отделений связи. Из-за мизерных доходов от такой торговли они не могут позволить себе ежедневно платить за торговые места на рынках Ашхабада. Ранее полицейские прогоняли торговцев с мест, где те нарушали порядок или загрязняли окружающую территорию. Бывали случаи, когда у них отбирали товары. Теперь, пользуясь нововведениями в Кодексе, сотрудники полиции на закреплённых за ними участках фактически установили неофициальную плату. Мелкие торговцы должны платить сотруднику полиции 50 манатов в неделю. Те, кто ездит по городу на грузовиках и продаёт дыни, арбузы, помидоры и виноград, должны платить по 50 манатов ежедневно. При этом занимающиеся такой торговлей утверждают, что в подобных условиях могут продолжать свою деятельность более спокойно. Согласно внесённым в Кодекс изменениям, размеры штрафов увеличились с 30–50 манатов до 50–100 манатов. Предусмотрены также предупреждение или безвозмездное изъятие товара. Ситуация с незаконной торговлей в городе практически не изменилась. Насколько эти изменения помогли пополнить государственный или региональные бюджеты, неизвестно. body: ХТ Расходы учителей средних школ Редакция 02 октября 2026 3678 Важное Лента Редакция - 08 октября 2026 Матвиенко отметила вклад О.Атабаевой в подготовку и проведение международных женских форумов ХТ Редакция - 07 октября 2026 Финал Международного конкурса красоты «Татар кызы — 2026» проходит в Туркменистане Лента Редакция - 07 октября 2026 Пезешкян встретится с Путиным в Туркменистане ХТ Редакция - 07 октября 2026 В стране прошел День поминовения После публикации материалов о проблемах в средних школах с точки зрения родителей учащихся предлагаем ознакомиться с мнением учителя одной из школ Ашхабада. По словам педагога, выпускники вузов, чтобы устроиться на работу в школу, вынуждены платить директору взятку в размере 2000 манатов. Еще около 2000 манатов, по словам собеседника, приходится платить за то, чтобы получить достаточное количество учебных часов и, соответственно, нормальную зарплату. Отдельно платят за то, чтобы назначенные учителю уроки шли без больших «окон», то есть подряд. В противном случае занятия могут быть распределены в течение всего рабочего дня. Например, учитель родного языка проводит урок в одном классе первым уроком, в другом — четвертым, а в следующем — шестым. В результате из-за двух-трех уроков учителю приходится проводить в школе практически весь день. «Домой приходишь уставший. А дома ждут другие дела, в том числе подготовка к урокам на следующий день. Если же сумеешь расположить к себе директора, то уроки тебе поставят в расписание подряд. Благодаря этому появляется больше свободного времени, чтобы отдохнуть и заняться домашними делами», — рассказывает педагог. Кроме того, по словам учителя, с сотрудников школ время от времени собирают по 50 или 100 манатов. В качестве причины могут называть предстоящую проверку со стороны городского отдела образования: якобы на эти деньги необходимо накрыть стол для проверяющих или приобрести подарки. В других случаях сборы объясняют нуждами школы. body: Azerbaijan’s block train traffic from China rises 40% in 2026 8 October 2026 19:15 (UTC+04:00) Qabil Ashirov Read more Azerbaijan Railways CJSC (ADY) received 416 block trains from China in January-September 2026, marking a 40% increase compared with the same period last year. Calculations show that approximately 297 block trains were received from China during the first nine months of 2025, according to local media sources. This means the number of block trains received from China increased by around 119 over the course of a year. The 40% increase in the number of block trains arriving in Azerbaijan from China is a positive indicator of the country's growing role in transit transportation between Asia and Europe. The trend is also significant for the development of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, widely known as the Middle Corridor. However, the increase in the number of block trains does not necessarily mean that the tonnage of cargo transported or ADY's freight transportation revenues have grown at the same pace. A more comprehensive assessment would require comparing additional indicators, including the number of containers transported, overall cargo volumes and freight transportation revenues. body: President Ilham Aliyev met with President of Turkmenistan in Turkmenbashi [PHOTOS/VIDEO] 8 October 2026 14:39 (UTC+04:00) AzerNEWS Staff Read more On October 8, President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev met with President of Turkmenistan Serdar Berdimuhamedov in Turkmenbashi. body: Azerbaijan's participation in C5 format opens new opportunities for cooperation, Turkmen president says 8 October 2026 11:15 (UTC+04:00) Akbar Novruz Read more Azerbaijan's participation in the Consultative Meeting of Central Asian Heads of State creates new opportunities for expanding economic cooperation with partners across Asia and Europe, Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedov said. Speaking at the opening of the eighth Consultative Meeting of the Heads of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan in Awaza on October 8, Berdimuhamedov described Azerbaijan's inclusion in the regional dialogue format as a significant development with considerable economic potential. The Turkmen leader highlighted the growing importance of cooperation between Azerbaijan and the five Central Asian countries, particularly in strengthening trade, transport and energy connectivity between the regions. He emphasized that closer engagement could help expand economic ties beyond the immediate region, creating additional opportunities for cooperation with European and Asian partners. "The role of Central Asia and Azerbaijan in regional and global processes—as key logistics and energy hubs for development—is currently steadily increasing," Berdimuhamedov stated. The remarks reflect the growing importance of transport and energy connections across the Caspian Sea, which links Azerbaijan with Central Asian economies and provides an alternative route for trade between Asia and Europe. Azerbaijan's participation in the consultative format brings together the five Central Asian states—Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan—with a country that plays a significant role in westward transport and energy infrastructure. The expansion of cooperation is particularly relevant to the development of the Middle Corridor, which connects China and Central Asia with Europe through the Caspian Sea, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Türkiye. Closer coordination could facilitate the movement of goods, improve transport infrastructure and support investment in logistics facilities along the route. Energy cooperation also represents an important area of potential engagement, given the region's hydrocarbon resources and growing interest in electricity transmission and renewable energy projects. body: Russia accuses Armenia of shifting responsibility over future of Gyumri military base 7 October 2026 16:40 (UTC+04:00) Akbar Novruz Read more Russia has accused Armenia's leadership of attempting to shift responsibility onto Moscow over the potential withdrawal of the 102nd Russian Military Base from Gyumri, as debate over the future of Russia's military presence in the country intensifies. Mikhail Kalugin, Director of the Fourth Department for CIS Countries at the Russian Foreign Ministry, made the remarks in an interview with RIA Novosti. According to Kalugin, Armenian officials are attempting to present the debate as though Moscow itself initiated discussions over the future of the Russian military presence. “Attempts to shift responsibility for the possible withdrawal of the base to Moscow are consistent with a curious feature of current Armenian political thinking. The ruling elite in Yerevan often expects the most important decisions to be made by external players,” Kalugin said. The Russian diplomat drew parallels with Armenia's increasingly complicated relationships with both the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) and the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO). Kalugin argued that Yerevan has similarly sought to place responsibility for major strategic choices elsewhere, pointing to Armenian statements that a referendum concerning the country's European integration should follow a positive signal from Brussels. He also cited discussions surrounding the CSTO, saying suggestions that Armenia could simply be excluded from the Russian-led security alliance would remove the need for Yerevan itself to decide whether to formally leave. Despite the increasingly sharp rhetoric, Kalugin said Moscow remained prepared to discuss all issues surrounding the Gyumri base. Any negotiations, he stressed, would have to proceed within the framework of the existing interstate agreements governing the deployment of Russian forces in Armenia. The future of the 102nd Military Base has emerged as another point of friction between Moscow and Yerevan amid a broader deterioration in bilateral relations. Russian President Vladimir Putin said in September that Moscow would not impose its military presence on Armenia and was prepared to withdraw its forces if Yerevan concluded that the base was no longer necessary. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan subsequently insisted that his government had never raised the question of removing the Russian base. “Since 2018, I have been in contact with the President of the Russian Federation and other senior officials, and I have never, not even once, raised the issue of withdrawing Russia’s 102nd Military Base from Armenia,” Pashinyan told parliament in September. He nevertheless said Armenia would not object if Moscow itself decided to withdraw the forces, arguing that developments in recent years had demonstrated that the Russian base was no longer of “vital importance” to Armenia's security. Pashinyan has maintained that if Russia wants to retain the base, Yerevan remains prepared to discuss the matter. The competing statements have therefore produced a dispute over who placed the future of the base on the political agenda, with Moscow accusing Yerevan of seeking to make Russia responsible for any eventual withdrawal and the Armenian government insisting that the issue was first publicly raised by the Russian side. The 102nd Russian Military Base has been stationed in Gyumri under an interstate agreement signed in 1995. An amendment agreed in 2010 extended the deployment until 2044. body: Home Azerbaijan Politics Baku Initiative Group issues statement over ongoing protests in France Politics News 8 October 2026 20:10 (UTC +04:00) Photo: AZERTAC Alish Abdulla Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 8. The Baku Initiative Group (BIG) is monitoring with serious concern the ongoing nationwide mobilization of high school students and youth in France, as well as reports regarding severe injuries sustained by protesters, numerous detentions, and the use of dangerous special crowd-control measures. This was reflected in a statement released by the BIG. According to the statement, the movement, which began in the city of Créteil and subsequently spread across France, initially emerged against a backdrop of grievances directly related to the right to quality education, specifically, shortages of teachers and other educational staff, the dilapidated state of school infrastructure, excessive academic workloads, and dissatisfaction with certain aspects of the higher education admissions system. "These grievances later evolved into a nationwide youth movement involving high school and university students, teachers, parents, and trade unions. The scale of these events demands particular attention. As of October 8, the French Minister of the Interior reported that more than 6,600 individuals had been detained, and 215 students and 89 educational staff members had sustained injuries. One particularly concerning aspect involves cases where minors sustain severe injuries. In the city of Lens, a 15-year-old student lost his hand as a result of the explosion of a sound grenade used during the protests. The BIG maintains that the right to education, the freedoms of expression and peaceful assembly, and the protection of children and youth from the use of unnecessary or disproportionate force are universal principles that must be upheld without selective application or double standards. Access to quality education is also a fundamental pillar of the genuine decolonization process. Education enables the elimination of structural inequalities, the preservation of identity, and the establishment of resilient, self-sufficient institutions. The BIG calls upon the French authorities to ensure that law enforcement measures during demonstrations strictly adhere to the principles of necessity, proportionality, and accountability; to guarantee the rights of minors and youth to peacefully express their views and assemble; to ensure effective investigations into incidents resulting in serious injuries; and to engage in substantive dialogue with students, teachers, and their representative organizations. France claims to uphold the protection of human rights, democratic freedoms, and human dignity as fundamental principles of its domestic and foreign policy. The consistent application of these principles must begin at home. Human rights cannot be defended selectively, and young people seeking to make their voices heard should be treated primarily as rights-holders rather than as a security issue. The Baku Initiative Group will continue to closely monitor developments and calls for dialogue, restraint, and full respect for fundamental rights," the statement said. body: Home Azerbaijan Azerbaijan's parliament calls European Parliament resolution biased Azerbaijan News 8 October 2026 17:52 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Trend News Agency Alish Abdulla Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 8. Azerbaijan’s parliament has rejected the allegations contained in the European Parliament’s October 8 resolution on human rights and freedoms in Azerbaijan, describing the document as a biased political action. The Azerbaijani parliament made the remarks in its response to the European Parliament’s resolution. The parliament said the European Parliament’s targeted political approach toward Azerbaijan had become more confrontational following the Second Karabakh War. It said resolutions adopted in recent years, along with calls for political pressure and sanctions against Azerbaijan, demonstrated that the organization had failed to accept what it described as the new geopolitical realities in the South Caucasus. The response also criticized the European Parliament for seeking to determine the scope of authority of Azerbaijan’s state bodies, issue instructions to law enforcement and judicial institutions, and set political conditions for bilateral relations. According to the parliament, this raises questions about whether the European Parliament seeks to build relations with Azerbaijan based on equality, mutual respect and non-interference in internal affairs. The parliament also referred to issues of corruption and illicit lobbying influence within the European Parliament, stressing the importance of the organization consistently applying its own standards. The response further said that the European Parliament applies double standards in its approach to human rights. It noted that while resolutions are adopted concerning Azerbaijan, European countries themselves continue to face problems related to police violence, restrictions on freedom of peaceful assembly and accountability for human rights violations. The parliament said the adoption of the resolution at a time when the Azerbaijan-Armenia peace agenda is advancing was also a matter of concern. It said unilateral initiatives and what it described as misguided assessments make it more difficult to build an environment of mutual trust and create additional obstacles to normalizing relations. The response also highlighted what the parliament described as a contradiction between the European Parliament’s call to restore cooperation with the Azerbaijani parliament and its adoption of documents that create interparliamentary tensions. The parliament said restoring trust requires abandoning confrontational rhetoric and recognizing the equal nature of interparliamentary relations. The Azerbaijani parliament said the country remains committed to protecting human rights and fundamental freedoms, ensuring the rule of law and implementing the principles of a state governed by law. The response also said that, while making allegations against Azerbaijan, the European Parliament remained silent about the rights of Azerbaijani refugees and internally displaced persons who, according to the parliament, were subjected to ethnic cleansing and other serious human rights violations during Armenia’s occupation of Azerbaijani territory. The Azerbaijani parliament called on the European Parliament to abandon what it described as confrontational rhetoric toward Azerbaijan and refrain from interfering in the country’s internal affairs. The parliament stated that no force can divert Azerbaijan from its path of democratic development. body: Home Azerbaijan Society Azerbaijan NGO opens landmine exhibition in Czech Republic (PHOTO) Society News 8 October 2026 16:58 (UTC +04:00) Alish Abdulla Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 8. Azerbaijan’s Gilavar Photo Club Public Union held an exhibition highlighting the country’s landmine problem in Brno, the Czech Republic’s second-largest city, on October 7, 2026, as part of its ongoing international campaign to promote the declaration of a “mine-free world” as the 18th UN Sustainable Development Goal. The exhibition on Armenia’s mine warfare against Azerbaijan was organized in partnership with the Land of Fire Azerbaijani diaspora organization in the Czech Republic, according to the State Support Agency for Non-Governmental Organizations of Azerbaijan. The exhibition featured documentary photographs depicting the life stories of Azerbaijanis affected by landmines and the severe consequences of mine explosions. Visitors were informed that extensive mine contamination of Azerbaijani territories during the occupation and the failure to provide accurate mine maps remain among the major obstacles to the safe return of Azerbaijanis to their native lands. It was also noted that Armenia should demonstrate humanitarian responsibility and provide accurate mine maps as a practical expression of its commitment to peace and a means of strengthening mutual trust. The Brno exhibition also highlighted the connection between the landmine problem and the issue of missing persons, noting that civilians are the primary victims in both cases. According to information presented at the exhibition, 32 mass graves have so far been discovered in the liberated territories. Examinations of human remains, it was reported, confirmed that the Azerbaijanis whose remains were found had been subjected to torture before being killed. The Gilavar Photo Club is a 2026 winner of the “Initiatives on the Problem of Mines and Unexploded Ordnance” grant competition, jointly announced by Azerbaijan’s NGO Agency and the Karabakh Revival Fund in partnership with the Azerbaijan National Agency for Mine Action (ANAMA). body: Home Central Asia Uzbekistan Uzbekistan Airports, Russia’s Krasnoyarsk airport discuss new routes Uzbekistan News 8 October 2026 15:13 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Uzbekistan Airports Niljan Bakhshaliyeva Uzbekistan Economics Correspondent Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 8. Uzbekistan Airports and Russia’s Krasnoyarsk International Airport discussed developing new air routes between Krasnoyarsk and Uzbek cities, as well as expanding transit connections through the two airports during a meeting in Tashkent. This was reflected in the statement by Uzbekistan Airports, following a meeting between Uzbekistan Airports and a delegation from Krasnoyarsk International Airport, led by its General Director Kirill Yermakov. The meeting continued discussions launched during the Russian-Uzbek forum in Fergana. The sides discussed attracting airlines, expanding the route network and developing convenient connecting flights. Particular attention was paid to potential direct routes between Krasnoyarsk and Fergana and Samarkand. The sides also discussed developing connecting services via Uzbek airports, including potential connections from Fergana to Istanbul and from Samarkand to Tel Aviv and Dubai. In the opposite direction, Krasnoyarsk could serve as a transit point for passengers from Uzbekistan traveling onward to destinations in Russia’s Far East and China, according to Uzbekistan Airports. "The parties agreed to jointly work on prospective routes and opportunities to attract airlines," Uzbekistan Airports said. In addition, the sides discussed joint marketing initiatives involving airlines and tourism companies. These initiatives could include promoting air routes, developing tourism products and increasing passenger demand. The talks form part of broader efforts to expand air connectivity between Uzbekistan and Russia and develop new passenger transit opportunities through regional airports. On October 8, President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev met with President of Turkmenistan Serdar Berdimuhamedov in Turkmenbashi, Trend 's special correspondent reports. During the conversation, the sides fondly recalled the visits of President Ilham Aliyev to Turkmenistan, as well as those of President of Turkmenistan Serdar Berdimuhamedov and Chairman of the Halk Maslahaty of Turkmenistan Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov to Azerbaijan, including Garabagh, highlighting the important role of these visits in developing bilateral relations. The sides discussed expanding cooperation in the political, economic, transport, transit, logistics, cultural, and humanitarian fields, as well as issues related to the Caspian Sea and cooperation within international organizations. President Ilham Aliyev praised the excellent organization of the event. Recalling Azerbaijan’s accession as a full-fledged participant in the Consultative Meeting of the Heads of State of Central Asia in November last year, the head of state once again expressed his gratitude for the unanimous support for this historic initiative put forward by Chairman of the Halk Maslahaty of Turkmenistan Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov. body: Home Azerbaijan Azerbaijan's trade turnover with Central Asian countries grew by more than 50 percent last year - President Ilham Aliyev (FULL SPEECH) Azerbaijan News 8 October 2026 11:24 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Press service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Laman Zeynalova Read more TURKMENBASHI, Turkmenistan, October 8. Last year, Azerbaijan's trade turnover with the countries of Central Asia grew by more than 50 percent, President Ilham Aliyev said as he addressed the 8th Consultative Meeting of the Heads of State of the Republic of Azerbaijan and Central Asia in Turkmenbashi, Trend 's special correspondent reports. Speech by President Ilham Aliyev - Esteemed Serdar Gurbangulyevich, Distinguished heads of state, Dear friends, First of all, I express my gratitude to the President of Turkmenistan for the invitation and traditional hospitality. I am glad to be back in brotherly Turkmenistan, in beautiful Awaza. In November last year, Azerbaijan became a full-fledged participant in the Consultative Meeting of the Heads of State of Central Asia. Once again, I express my gratitude to all my respected colleagues for their unanimous support for this historic decision. In this regard, I would like to note the role played by Turkmenistan and, personally, by the respected Gurbanguly Myalikgulyevich Berdimuhamedov. It was right here, in Awaza, in August last year, that he initiated Azerbaijan's full participation in this format. Azerbaijan-Turkmenistan relations have been developing dynamically in recent years. Since last year, five high-level visits have already taken place. This reflects the intensity of our political dialogue and the mutual desire to further strengthen bilateral ties. I would particularly like to highlight the construction of a mosque in the city of Fuzuli, initiated by the respected Gurbanguly Myalikgulyevich Berdimuhamedov. Last year, we jointly participated in laying its foundation. This gift from brotherly Turkmenistan to our country is yet another testament to the friendship and spiritual closeness of our peoples. Brotherly support in the restoration of the liberated territories of Azerbaijan holds special significance for us. In Fuzuli, a school named after Mirzo Ulugbek has already been built by Uzbekistan, and the Kurmangazy Children's Creativity Center has been built by Kazakhstan; in Aghdam, a school named after Manas has been built by Kyrgyzstan. We highly value this assistance. Azerbaijan's interaction with the countries of Central Asia has expanded significantly in recent years. Political ties are at a high level, and mutual high-level visits have become regular. Trade and economic cooperation are growing stronger, mutual investments are increasing, and joint projects are being implemented. Last year, Azerbaijan's trade turnover with Central Asian countries grew by more than 50 percent. Today, over 400 companies with capital originating from Central Asian countries actively operate in our country. In recent years, Azerbaijan has established joint investment funds with Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan. The capital of each of these funds amounts to hundreds of millions of dollars. I believe their potential should be utilized more actively, primarily for the implementation of joint projects, the creation of new manufacturing facilities, and the expansion of industrial cooperation. We must not only increase mutual trade; it is important to jointly invest, produce, and enter external markets. Transport is one of the primary areas of our cooperation. The Caspian Sea plays an increasingly vital role today in the transport connectivity of our countries. The transport infrastructure on both shores of the Caspian is of key importance for connecting Central Asia with Azerbaijan and further onward to international markets. In recent years, we have consistently increased our transport capabilities. We have made major investments in transport infrastructure, developing seaports, airports, railways, and highways. Today, we are observing significant growth in cargo transit volumes across the Caspian. Our common task is to make these routes more efficient and competitive. In parallel, the Digital Silk Way project is being implemented, and work is underway to lay fiber-optic lines along the bed of the Caspian Sea. The Middle Corridor is acquiring ever greater significance; last year, the volume of transit cargo along this route grew by more than 10 percent, and in the first eight months of the current year, by almost another 20 percent. The energy sector holds a special place in our cooperation. Azerbaijan plays an important role in the transit of energy resources from Central Asia to international markets. Oil from Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan is transported through the territory of our country, and the volume of these shipments is growing. Our cooperation in renewable energy is consistently expanding. We are working jointly with Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan to create a green energy corridor. Dear colleagues, The geopolitical importance of our cooperation format lies not only in joint projects in the energy and transport sectors. Peace, security, and political and economic stability in our countries form the foundation of all our successes and serve as a guarantee for the future successful development of the Central Asian states and Azerbaijan, as well as the strengthening of our interaction. Thank you for your attention. body: Home Azerbaijan Chronicles of Victory (October 7, 2020): President Ilham Aliyev interviewed by CNN-Turk TV (PHOTO/VIDEO) Azerbaijan News 7 October 2026 07:05 (UTC +04:00) BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 7. President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev has been interviewed by CNN-Türk television. Trend presents the interview. Mr. President Ilham Aliyev, welcome to CNN-Türk. Thank you for giving this interview on such historic days for Azerbaijan. Without further ado, let me immediately move on to the questions. First of all, what is the latest situation in the operations? Are they going as planned? What territory has been liberated from occupation? -Everything is going according to plan. The Azerbaijani army is restoring the territorial integrity of the country these days. The operation continues successfully. One city and many villages have already been liberated from the occupation. This once again proves that the Azerbaijani people will never put up with the occupation. We have repeatedly said this: Karabakh is our historical and ancestral land! Unfortunately, the negotiations held for a long time did not lead to any results. Therefore, of course, Azerbaijan had to restore its territorial integrity on its own and is doing exactly that. As you know, on 27 September the Armenian armed forces launched a new offensive against us. Many of our cities and villages are being shelled. Today the death toll among our civilians is about 30 people. The Armenian armed forces are shelling our cities and villages, about a thousand houses have been destroyed or seriously damaged. But everything is going according to plan, and I hope that the tasks before us will be fulfilled. -Mr. President, I would like to return to the processes in the zone of operations again. As we know, the Armenian army began shelling Azerbaijani cities outside the conflict zone with ballistic missiles. In particular, it is targeting settlements in the second largest city of Azerbaijan, Ganja, a power plant in Mingachevir with ballistic missiles. What do you think was the goal? -In my opinion, this is a sign of helplessness of the Armenian army and the crimes of the military-political leadership of Armenia because violence against civilians, the shelling of settlements and the destruction of peaceful cities with ballistic missiles is considered a war crime. This indicates that Armenia cannot resist us on the battlefield. Losing the battle and in an effort to stop us, and in order to harm the civilian population as much as possible, it resorts to such heinous acts. As you noted, Ganja and Mingachevir are cities that are far from the war zone. At the same time, our cities located near the front zone are bombarded every day. The nearest district is Tartar. From one to two thousand shells are dropped on the city of Tartar every day. The main purpose of this is violence against civilians. This once again demonstrates the fascist essence of Armenia, the fascist essence of its regime. But this does not frighten the Azerbaijani people and has no impact whatsoever. Our citizens living in these regions, in these cities and villages stand firmly. They say: long live the Motherland, may our lands be liberated from occupation as soon as possible. They will remain in these places to the end and will provide our army with moral support. -If Armenia continues shelling civilian settlements, will there be any change in your current position? -No, there should be no change in our position. We are not fighting against the Armenian people. I have already spoken about this many times. We are waging a fair fight. We want to restore our territorial integrity, we are doing this and we have achieved success in this matter and in this direction. Azerbaijan has never fought against the civilian population and against civilians. The other day I said that we have no problems with the Armenian people. Thousands of Armenians live in Azerbaijan, and they are our citizens. The Armenians living in Nagorno-Karabakh today are also our citizens. All our goals are military. We have every right to destroy military targets because they have caused great damage to our army and cities. Therefore, our duty is to destroy them and ensure the safety of our population. -Armenia's bombardment of civilian settlements with ballistic missiles is essentially a war crime, an act contrary to the Geneva Convention. In this context, do you plan to put forward any initiatives regarding war crimes before the UN? Do you collect evidence of these crimes on the ground? -We certainly do. All of their war crimes are already being recorded. Unfortunately, the international community did not react to the war crimes that were committed against Azerbaijan and our people earlier. The Khojaly massacre is an act of genocide that took place in front of the whole world. However, the then military-political leadership of Armenia was not held accountable for this. The destruction of our cities and villages, the appearance of more than a million internally displaced persons – the international community did not take any action in this regard. Therefore, this issue has not been resolved for many years because no distinction is made between the occupier and the victim of the occupation. And the shelling of our cities and villages by the Armenian armed forces with ballistic missiles today is a war crime. The leadership of Armenia, of course, must and will bear responsibility for this. -So far you have received several calls for a ceasefire. You have personally answered them. But looking at the 30-year history of the conflict, do you think that these calls will produce results? -I believe that these calls should not be just calls for a ceasefire. We have repeatedly said that sanctions should have been applied to the occupying state of Armenia. If sanctions had been applied in due time, then, perhaps, this issue would have been resolved long ago. Very serious pressure should have been put on Armenia – not in word but in deed. Unfortunately, this did not happen. Therefore, this process dragged on for 30 years. Negotiations that have been fruitless for 30 years are already losing their point. In addition, recently, the military-political leadership of Armenia, both with aggressive actions and aggressive statements, disrupted the process of negotiations. In other words, it dealt a crushing blow to the talks. To say that "Karabakh is Armenia" essentially means an end to the negotiations because the essence of the negotiations is that the occupied lands should be gradually and on a step-by-step basis returned to Azerbaijan. This is enshrined in the fundamental principles. To say that "Karabakh is Armenia" actually means an end to this process. There were other similar statements. After that, in July, Armenia attacked Azerbaijan in the direction of the state border, killing many soldiers and one civilian. Therefore, the restoration of the ceasefire must be ensured on certain conditions. First of all, we should be given a schedule for the withdrawal of the Armenian armed forces from the occupied lands. We have already communicated our position on this issue to the Minsk Group. I hope that our calls and proposals will not remain unanswered. -I think that speaking about the Minsk Group of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe, France should be mentioned separately. What can you say in connection with France's position on this issue? -I have already spoken about this several times. We have always perceived the Minsk Group as a group, and this is still the case today. We believed that the co-chair countries of this group should remain neutral, not support any of the parties, because otherwise their mediation mission would be called into question. Until recent events, they managed to maintain neutrality to a certain extent. We know that the Armenian lobby is strong in these countries. body: Home Azerbaijan Chronicles of Victory (October 7, 2020): President Ilham Aliyev interviewed by Euronews TV (PHOTO/VIDEO) Azerbaijan News 7 October 2026 07:00 (UTC +04:00) BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 7. President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev has been interviewed by Euronews television. Trend presents the interview. -Joining us now is the President of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev. Thank you for your time. There has been strong and repeated international pressure for a ceasefire and to de-escalate tensions. Fighting is ongoing, if not escalating. What is your objective now in the conflict? -Ceasefire cannot be achieved unilaterally. It must be a bilateral decision and also it must be implemented on the ground. As you know Armenia attacked us on the 27th of September, attacking our military positions and damaging our infrastructure, attacking civilians. So far we have almost 30 civilians killed as a result of Armenian attack, including the ballistic missiles, and the cluster bombs. So, our counter-attack was successful. We managed to liberate part of the occupied territories and our main objective is restoration of territorial integrity of Azerbaijan. Armenia must give us the time-table for withdrawal of their troops from the occupied territories and this time-table must be approved by the Minsk group co-chairs, the countries which are mediators. And after that I think the effort must be imposed on achieving the ceasefire. -The countries that you’re referencing have repeatedly asked for a ceasefire. Why isn’t that happening now? Why aren’t you pushing for that to happen immediately? -Because we have been a subject of attack for many times. During the last three months there have been three attacks on Azerbaijan. One in July, on the border between Armenia and Azerbaijan, far away from the region of Nagorno-Karabakh. The goal of Armenia was to occupy new territories of Azerbaijan. They did not manage to do it. Our army defeated them. Then, on August 23, they send a sabotage group to commit terror acts against our civilians and military personnel. That also was a failure for them, because the head of the sabotage group was detained and he gives evidences exactly about what I am saying. And in the end of September they launched a massive attack on our villages and cities. I can tell you that up to today we have almost 900 houses totally demolished, or damaged and many casualties and wounded people among civilians. And now after Armenia is suffering a very bitter defeat, they are pleading for a ceasefire. They made violation of ceasefire themselves. They ignore United Nations Security Council resolutions which demand full, complete, immediate and unconditional withdrawal of Armenian troops. They want to keep status quo unchanged, and the Minsk Group co-chairs United States, Russia and France, their presidents many times made the statements that the status quo is unacceptable. Armenia ignored it, but now Azerbaijan itself is changing the status quo, and I think that will be an important step towards the soonest resolution of the conflict. -Mr. President, civilians have been killed on both sides of this conflict. How do you reconcile that with your aims? -Of course, we regret that civilians are being killed and of course, we were not the purpose, we were not the source of this attack. Because it was a first thing in the morning on the 27th of September, what they did, they attacked our cities and villages. And we had to respond. But our response mainly is and primarily is on their military positions, on their tanks and guns and what we are doing on the battlefield is available in internet. Our drones and our other equipment demolished only military objectives on the occupied territories. Unfortunately, Armenia is using civilians in order to have more people on the ground, because their demographic situation is very bad, and we have video about these civilians being just next to the guns, and of course... -I’m sorry to interject Mr. President, that civilians on their side have been killed in this fighting and they would dispute exactly why it was on the 27th of September this violence flared up again. Let me bring you to a promise that your foreign minister made last year that said it was necessary to take concrete measures to prepare the populations for peace. What we are seeing right now is the opposite of that. How are you trying to limit the suffering of civilians? -You know we are not responsible for this outbreak. As I said, we were a subject of a physical attack from Armenian army which is situated on the occupied territories of Azerbaijan Above from that, the current Armenian regime did everything in order to destroy the negotiation process. Exactly one year ago, Armenian prime Minister at the rally in the occupied area of Azerbaijan made a statement that ‘Karabakh is Armenia’ and that statement actually destroyed negotiation process. Because the principles which are on the table and which are the basis for settlement demand the return of the occupied territories to Azerbaijan. And when Armenian prime minister says that not a centimeter of land will return to Azerbaijan, when he says that ‘Karabakh is Armenia’, when they organize illegal settlement of foreign people on the occupied territories which is a brutal violation of Geneva Convention, they destroy negotiation process. After that, in order to make us responsible for that, they attack us three times-on July, August, and September. When we beat them on the battlefield, they call everywhere, they make a plea to everyone, ‘stop Azerbaijan’. We want to stop, but we want the occupation to stop. Therefore, the main message should be to Armenia, we are not on Armenian land, we are on our land. Our land for 27 years... -One thing that Armenia will say is that Turkey is really providing quite a strong influence, including supplying things like military aid. To what extent would you say Turkey are accelerating and pushing your country and your actions in this conflict? -This is absolutely false information. Turkey for us is a strong ally, partner and brotherly country, and of course the statements expressed their position and we are very grateful to Turkish government, to Turkish President, Turkish people for this support. But Turkey in no other way is involved in this conflict. Armenia bringing such fake news to the media wants to diminish the capacity of Azerbaijani army. We are fighting ourselves. Yes, we purchased weapons from Turkey, but not only. Our main supplier of weapons is not Turkey. And probably everybody knows about that. So, the fact that we buy modern Turkish equipment including the fighter drones should not be a problem for anyone. Because Armenia gets weapons free of charge. We pay for them and Armenia gets free of charge. Turkey in no other way is involved in the conflict. -We keep talking about weapons and we keep talking about fighting here. Is diplomacy still an option? Will you sit down, have talks with the prime minister of Armenia to find a different way out of this conflict? I can tell you, that during my term as the president, I had maybe tens of talks with two former Armenian presidents and the current prime minister. During those previous debates we made a substantial progress on negotiation table. We elaborated the principles which today are the basis for the settlement of conflict. And we were constructive. Negotiations are taking place since 1992. Can you imagine? For almost 30 years. And we were living with hopes, mediators were telling us that you should wait a little bit, there will be more constructive approach from Armenian side. But when this prime minister came to power, as a result of the coup d’état two years ago, he destroyed completely negotiation process. And I had meetings with him many times. body: Home Central Asia Turkmenistan Turkmenistan, Iran discuss expanding transport and trade cooperation Turkmenistan News 8 October 2026 11:30 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Mejlis (Parliament) of Turkmenistan Fuad Namazov Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 8. Turkmenistan and Iran discussed strengthening transport, trade and economic cooperation during a meeting between the Chairperson of the Mejlis of Turkmenistan, Dunyagozel Gulmanova and Iran’s Minister of Roads and Urban Development, Farzaneh Sadegh, in Awaza yesterday. This was reflected in a press release published by the Mejlis (Parliament) of Turkmenistan. According to the publication, the sides highlighted the development of bilateral relations and cooperation in political, trade, economic and cultural-humanitarian spheres. Gulmanova also thanked Sadegh for her participation in international events held in Turkmenistan’s Awaza National Tourist Zone. The two sides also discussed cooperation between the inter-parliamentary friendship groups, relevant parliamentary committees, young parliamentarians and women parliamentarians. Farzaneh Sadegh’s portfolio includes Iran’s roads and urban development sector, making transport cooperation a key area of bilateral economic interaction between the neighboring countries. Meanwhile, Iran is one of Turkmenistan's longest-standing regional partners, with bilateral cooperation spanning energy, transport, trade, and border connectivity. The two countries share a 1,100-kilometer border and maintain an institutional dialogue through a Joint Intergovernmental Commission on Economic Cooperation, which regularly reviews progress across sectors ranging from gas and electricity to transport, customs, agriculture, and investment. During the commission's latest meeting in Tehran in 2025, the sides also discussed the creation of cross-border trade and economic zones to stimulate bilateral commerce. Energy remains a cornerstone of the relationship. In recent years, Ashgabat and Tehran have expanded cooperation on natural gas supplies, including swap arrangements and discussions on direct exports and transit through Iran to third-country markets. The two sides have also advanced cooperation in electricity transmission and maritime transport, while recent high-level meetings resulted in agreements covering natural gas, customs cooperation, port partnerships between Turkmenbashi and Amirabad, and intergovernmental cooperation plans. Transport and logistics have become another major pillar of bilateral ties as both countries seek to strengthen regional connectivity. Turkmenistan and Iran have been working to increase cargo flows across their shared border, improve road, rail, and port links, and enhance multimodal transport routes connecting Central Asia with the Persian Gulf and broader international markets. body: Home South Caucasus Georgia Missing persons cases among painful humanitarian issues – Georgian minister Georgia News 7 October 2026 12:04 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Trend News Agency Humay Aghajanova Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 7. Missing persons cases are among the most painful and enduring humanitarian issues, State Minister of Georgia for Reconciliation and Civic Equality and Head of the Interagency Commission on the Recovery and Handover of Remains of Missing Persons, Tea Akhvlediani, said at the 4th international conference on the theme "Strengthening trust and developing effective mechanisms to resolve the issue of missing persons" held within the framework of the Baku Dialogue on Missing Persons on Wednesday, Trend 's correspondent reports from the event. She pointed out that the impact of the cases is deeply felt by families who are forced to live, sometimes for decades, with uncertainty regarding the fate of their loved ones. "While various countries have their own historical experiences regarding the issue of missing persons and have developed mechanisms suited to different contexts, we are firmly united by a shared humanitarian goal: to clarify the fate and whereabouts of missing persons and, whenever possible, provide answers to their long-waiting families. Precisely this shared responsibility brings us together today to strengthen sustained commitment and multilateral cooperation, as well as to pool the expertise of states, international organizations, academia, and civil society," she noted. The minister added that, alongside improving search and forensic mechanisms, building trust and fostering close cooperation remain key steps toward achieving the goal of searching for and accounting for all missing persons, regardless of their ethnic background. The 4th international conference on the theme "Strengthening trust and developing effective mechanisms to resolve the issue of missing persons", organized by the State Commission on Prisoners of War, Hostages and Missing Persons, is being held in Gulustan Palace within the framework of the Baku Dialogue on Missing Persons. The event is attended by former heads of state and government, high-ranking representatives of international organizations and foreign countries, heads of agencies dealing with missing persons, experts, representatives of non-governmental organizations, and human rights specialists, as well as ambassadors and military attachés of foreign countries accredited in Azerbaijan and other officials. One of the main directions of this year's discussions is the formation and strengthening of trust between the parties. The purpose of the conference is not to be satisfied with discussions, but to contribute to the formation of practical and sustainable mechanisms that strengthen trust and cooperation, serve to ensure families' right to know the truth, facilitate information exchange, and expand the application of modern forensic, DNA and technological capabilities. The event will continue until October 10. body: Home Azerbaijan UN Human Rights Council adopts mine resolution co-authored by Azerbaijan Azerbaijan News 7 October 2026 18:30 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Artificial intelligence Alamda Nasib Read more BAKU , Azerbaijan , October 7 . The UN Human Rights Council has adopted a resolution titled “Impact of anti-personnel mines on the full enjoyment of human rights: Strengthening victim assistance,” which Azerbaijan co-authored and actively promoted, the Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry said. The resolution was adopted without a vote, with 70 states joining as co-sponsors. During the 63rd session of the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva, Azerbaijan organized a public dialogue to promote and keep the joint initiative on the agenda and co-hosted a side event dedicated to the issue. Azerbaijan, one of the countries most heavily contaminated by mines in the world, faces a severe challenge posed by anti-personnel mines, the ministry said. “Anti-personnel mines and unexploded ordnance have a long-term and severe impact on the full enjoyment of human rights, with serious consequences for the lives of victims and their family members. In this regard, we welcome the particular attention given to victim assistance in the resolution,” the ministry said. The ministry emphasized that mine action is a fundamental element of sustainable peace and plays an important role in post-conflict recovery. “Mine clearance not only enables the safe and dignified return of former internally displaced persons to their homes, but also makes an important contribution to the recovery of conflict-affected areas and communities, as well as ensuring socio-economic development,” it said. The ministry also welcomed the resolution's focus on the interlinkages between mine action, peace and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. “Mine clearance is also important for ensuring more effective adaptation to climate-related risks. In this regard, we consider it important that the resolution contributes to developing and deepening understanding of the link between mine action and adaptation to climate risks in the context of human rights,” the ministry said. The scale of casualties caused by mines once again demonstrates the need to mobilize stronger international support, partnerships and sustainable financing for mine action and victim assistance, according to the ministry. It welcomed the Human Rights Council's call on member states to increase financing for mine clearance and victim assistance, including through alternative sources of financing and public-private partnerships. “Azerbaijan once again emphasizes the importance of strengthening international cooperation, solidarity and sustained support in addressing the mine threat and highly values the contribution of mine action to the protection of human rights and the promotion of sustainable peace and development,” the ministry said. body: UHRP Marks 77 Years Since CCP’s Takeover of East Turkistan: Calls for Urgent International Action - Uyghur Human Rights Project Skip to content UHRP Marks 77 Years Since CCP’s Takeover of East Turkistan: Calls for Urgent International Action For immediate release October 1, 2026, 12:00 p.m. EDT Contact: Omer Kanat, +1 (202) 790-1795 On the 71st anniversary of the Chinese Communist Party’s proclamation of the “Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region,” the Uyghur Human Rights Project (UHRP) calls on governments, international institutions, and civil society to reject Beijing’s propaganda and take concrete steps to hold China accountable for its ongoing genocide and crimes against humanity against the Uyghur people. “From the very beginning, the so-called autonomy promised to Uyghurs was an illusion,” said UHRP Executive Director Omer Kanat . “What Beijing calls autonomy is a roadmap for occupation and genocide.” On October 1, 1955, the CCP claimed to grant “autonomy” to Uyghurs and other Turkic peoples. In reality, this marked the consolidation of Beijing’s control over East Turkistan and the beginning of seven decades of repression. Far from self-rule, the anniversary represents a systematic project of occupation, assimilation, and erasure. On July 1, 2026, the Chinese government’s new “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress” took effect, codifying Xi Jinping’s assimilation policies nationwide. The law expanded state control over language, religion, education, and family life while further eroding the promise of regional autonomy. While China celebrates October 1 as National Day, Uyghurs worldwide remember it as a day of dispossession and grief. In East Turkistan today, Uyghurs face internment, forced labor, surveillance, family separation, and the criminalization of religious and cultural practices. UHRP urges governments to: Publicly reject Beijing’s propaganda surrounding the so-called anniversary; Strengthen enforcement of forced labor import bans and sanctions against perpetrators; Push for international accountability mechanisms at the UN and beyond; Support Uyghur communities in exile who continue to resist cultural erasure. Read more: China’s ‘Ethnic Unity’ Law is Already Harming Uyghurs , by Omer Kanat, August 6, 2026 Forced Allegiance: Reflections on Flag-raising Ceremonies and National Anthems in Britain and East Turkistan , by Dr. Henryk Szadziewski, September 30, 2025 False “Success in Xinjiang Governance”: A Critique of the CCP White Paper “The Successful Practice of the Party’s Xinjiang Governance Strategy in the New Era, ” by Asiye Uyghur, September 29, 2025 UHRP Condemns White Paper Whitewashing 70 Years of Repression of Uyghurs , September 24, 2025 Tweets by UyghurProject
title: UHRP Marks 77 Years Since CCP’s Takeover of East Turkistan: Calls for Urgent International Action

body: China’s Uyghur crackdown has not ended — it has gone underground - Uyghur Human Rights Project Skip to content China’s Uyghur crackdown has not ended — it has gone underground September 25, 2026 | The Hill The Uyghur region has become one of the world’s most sophisticated surveillance environments. Families separated across borders therefore cannot communicate normally. As research from the Uyghur Human Rights Project has shown , Uyghur “families are prevented from normal communications both directly, through intimidation and monitored calls, and indirectly, through fear of reprisals for attempting to maintain contact.” Cited: Report by Dr. Henryk Szadziewski ( Fading Ties: Uyghur Family Separation as a Tool of Transnational Repression ) Read the full article by William Nee for The Hill : https://thehill.com/opinion/international/6109530-evolution-china-uygur-repression/amp/ Tweets by UyghurProject

body: Read RFA coverage of this story in Uyghur Chinese authorities in Xinjiang’s regional capital Urumqi on July 4 arrested two Uyghur sisters and their mother for sending goods to their eldest sister in Turkey, and a third sister was arrested a week later, the eldest told Radio Free Asia. Guzelnur Kamil said her family had been shipping ordinary household goods, including clothing, footwear, hats, daily necessities, seasonings, and packaged food items to support her business in Turkey. “They were simply miscellaneous everyday items,” she told RFA. “My mother said, ‘Even if we cannot send you cash, let us send you goods so you can do business, my child, and provide for your children,’” she said. Guzelnur, who moved to Turkey in 2016, said the shipments were assembled by her sister, Guljennet Kamil, who from 2018-2020 was detained in an internment camp . Guljennet also suffers from partial paralysis following an accident and was helped by her sister with a share of the profits from her business. However, according to Guzelnur, the police used this communication as a pretext to target the family. Investigation Guzelnur said the police interrogation of her family began on July 1, and explained that her mother, Bahargul Tohti, along with her sisters Guljennet and Gulzeper Hekim, were interrogated several times. Police used Guljennet’s shipping of goods to Turkey as a pretext, alleging suspicion of “supporting terrorists,” she said, adding that her mother and sisters were ordered to lead police to the exact shops where they purchased the goods and the logistics companies they used to ship them. “On the 4th, they spoke very politely, asking my mother to come to the police station at 9:00 AM,” she said. “After taking her in, they also brought in my sisters. They took their blood samples and photographed them from the front, back, and sides. After that, they just took them away without saying a word.” Turkey is one of 26 countries that China considers “sensitive,” along with primarily Muslim-majority nations such as Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Kazakhstan according to Human Rights Watch . Under China’s “ Strike Hard Campaign ,” those who have been to these countries, have families, or otherwise communicate with people there, have been questioned, detained, and even imprisoned. Guzelnur said her family in Urumqi has not sent her any goods for more than a year. Instead, she has been importing merchandise from Central Asian countries. The shipments from her family had already ceased long before her family was arrested by police. “We have documentation for everything—from where it was shipped, and even who received the goods,” Guzelnur said. “We provided those files, and my mother and sisters provided everything to the police. Yet the police still told them, ‘We will investigate you; there are also things going on over there in Turkey.’ What things could be going on here? We have nothing going on here. We can even present clean records from here.” According to Guzelnur, her mother and sisters were taken to the Nanjiao Police Station in Urumqi. “One is an orphan girl, one is my mother, and one is my disabled sister... What am I supposed to do now?!” she told RFA, referring to her adopted sister Gulzeper. RFA confirmed that Guljennet was moved from the police station and is currently being held at the Tianshan District Detention Center. Ethnic unity law The arrests came just days after China’s new ethnic unity law went into effect. On July 10, Norway-based Uyghur activist Abduweli Ayup posted on X , “Three Uyghurs detained in Urumqi. The National Security police didn’t tell the reasons, they put them in detention on July 4th. They are the first target we learned after China enacted the ethnic unity promotion law.” Critics of China’s ethnic unity law warn that the law brings accelerated forced assimilation and cultural erasure of Uyghurs and Tibetans . It also raises fears of Beijing’s increasing transnational repression and its ability to stifle dissident voices overseas. Guzelnur told RFA that her third sister, Gulmire Kamil, who remained at home after her mother and two sisters were arrested on July 4, was arrested by police a week later. Gulmire previously served 10 years in prison for her connection with the July 5, 2009 unrest in Urumqi. Translated by Tahir Izgil. Edited by Charlie Dharapak and Eugene Whong.
title: Chinese police arrest Uyghur sisters and mother in Urumqi for sending goods to Turkey

body: Updated June 12, 2026, 12:30 PM EDT A Bangkok court on Thursday sentenced two Uyghur men to death for triggering a bomb explosion which killed twenty and injured over a hundred others over a decade ago. “The deaths and injuries caused by the attack were a terrible tragedy, and the victims and their families deserve justice,” Rebiya Kadeer of the International Uyghur Human Rights and Democracy Foundation (IUHRDF) told RFA. “However, justice cannot be achieved through proceedings that leave significant questions unanswered regarding due process, the treatment of defendants , and the reliability of key evidence,” Kadeer added. uyghuyr-bomb-suspect-thailand-trial_0 Forensic officials and rescue foundation volunteers clean up the Erawan Shrine in Bangkok, a day after the bomb explosion killed 20 people, Aug. 18, 2015. (RFA) No group claimed responsibility for the Erawan Shrine bombing in central Bangkok on Aug. 17, 2015, but speculation called it an act of retaliation against the forced deportation of more than 109 Uyghurs from Thailand a month earlier. Shortly after the bombing, Thai police named 17 suspects. Arrested were two Uyghurs, Adem Karadag (alias Bilal Mohammed) and Yusufu Mieraili, who went on trial in 2016 for planting explosives. Both have denied all charges brought against them Upon hearing the verdict delivered by a four-judge panel on Thursday, Mieraili shouted “Injustice!” in the courtroom in both English and Thai. “RIP Thailand’s justice system. I don’t accept any of this,” Mieraili added. “I didn’t do anything wrong.” uyghur-bangkok-erawan-shrine-bombing-verdict Adem Karadag (alias Bilal Mohammed), left, and Yusufu Mieraili during a Feb.16, 2016, appearance at a Thai military court. (Nicolas Asfouri/AFP) During the trial, prosecutors presented evidence that Mieraili and Karadag had been near the shrine around the time of the explosion, that they had communicated with each other by telephone, and that a taxi driver had transported them away from the area after the incident. The judges stated that although the defendants had denied committing the crime, they had failed to refute the evidence presented against them. The court granted both men 30 days to file an appeal. Defense lawyer Choochat Kanpai told reporters they “will appeal the ruling because there are many aspects of the case that the court has not fully considered, including the treatment of the defendants during the proceedings.” The decade-long trial was beset by delays due to the coronavirus pandemic and problems securing translators. uyghur-bangkok-erawan-shrine-bombing-verdict Defense lawyers speak to reporters at Bangkok South Criminal Court, June 11, 2026, after the verdict for the Erawan Shrine bombing. (Lillian Suwanrumpha/AFP) Seven Chinese tourists were among the fatalities when explosives—apparently left in a backpack—detonated. Beijing welcomed the death sentences. “The attackers were totally inhumane and extremely heinous,” foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian told reporters. “China supports Thailand in conducting the trial in accordance with the law and severely punishing the murderers.” Bahtiyar Bora of the Australian Uyghur Association who provided assistance and translation for Karadag and Mieraili during court proceedings in Thailand, spoke to RFA about China’s response to the verdict. “These two Uyghurs fled Chinese oppression and came to Thailand. China is, of course, pleased with their severe punishment and can continue to accuse Uyghurs of terrorism internationally,” Bora said. Thailand deported 40 Uyghurs to China in February 2025 despite warnings from human rights groups that they would face persecution on their return, drawing swift condemnation from the United Nations. uyghur-bangkok-erawan-shrine-bombing-verdict Rebiya Kadeer at the fourth General Assembly of the World Uyghur Congress in Tokyo May 14, 2012. (Yuriko Nakao/Reuters) “These actions have reinforced concerns that decisions involving Uyghurs in Thailand may be influenced by political and economic considerations linked to Beijing rather than by international human rights obligations,” Rebiya Kadeer told RFA. “Against this background, it is difficult for many in the Uyghur community to have confidence that this verdict was reached entirely free from political influence,” Kadeer said. Adds quote from Bahtiyar Bora of the Australian Uyghur Association. Pimuk Rakkanam reported from Bangkok, Tahir Hamut Izgil reported from Washington. With reporting from AFP and Reuters. Edited by Charlie Dharapak.
title: Uyghur human rights activist condemns death sentences in Bangkok bombing
