body: В Дашогузском велаяте построили новый следственный изолятор | Turkmen.News В Дашогузском велаяте построили новый следственный изолятор 14.10.2026 | Важное | В посёлке Гулистан близ Дашогуза около месяца назад сдали новый следственный изолятор. Объект с несколькими корпусами огорожен как минимум четырьмя заборами и больше напоминает колонию или даже тюрьму. На одном из корпусов видны прогулочные камеры без крыши — такие же имеются в тюрьмах «Овадан-Депе» (AH-T/2) и «Абды-Шукур» (СИЗО LB-D/9 в Туркменабаде). По сообщению источника turkmen.news, объект достроили с опозданием и многочисленными недочётами. Из-за нехватки финансирования силовые чиновники искали креативные решения, как собрать нужные для строительства ресурсы. Так, каждого уличённого в получении взятки или иным способом проштрафившегося работника дорожной полиции и велаятского регистрационно-экзаменационного управления (РЭУ) заставляли отсыпать КамАЗ щебня или асфальта, привезти цемент или иные стройматериалы. «Естественно, гаишники не платили из собственных средств, а загружали этим обычных водителей», — говорит источник turkmen.news в одном из силовых ведомств велаята. В Туркменистане часто стоимость строительства может подорожать, а его длительность затянуться, что нередко происходит как раз из-за коррупции. В итоге объект приходится заканчивать всем миром. Так, в конце 2025 года под Дашогузом открылся городок на полторы тысячи квартир — подрядчики, которые в срок закончили свою часть работ, бесплатно помогали отстающим, а материалы на финальный этап предоставили десятки фирм, даже не связанных со строительством. Но это не пример кооперации, а итог принуждения со стороны руководящих чиновников города и Шабатского этрапа, которые сами же и расхитили выделенные ресурсы и сорвали сроки. Всеми исправительными учреждениями и их строительством в Туркменистане ведает МВД. Оно же руководит дорожной полицией и РЭУ. Последнее ведомство занимается (пере)регистрацией автомобилей, проведением технического осмотра, (пере)оформлением водительских прав — в Дашогузе его офис находится как раз рядом с новым СИЗО. По данным источника, старый следственный изолятор, который до 2013 года располагался в здании бывшей женской колонии по ул. Ильялинской, будет снесён. Построить больше тюрем в 2025 году предложила в своём отчёте омбудсмен Туркменистана Яздурсун Гурбанназарова . По её мнению, это поможет решить проблему перенаселённости пенитенциарных учреждений страны. Каким образом снизить само число заключённых, туркменское правительство озабочено меньше. Согласно Институту исследований политики в области преступности и правосудия, Туркменистан по состоянию на 2026 год занимает 3-е место по числу заключённых на 100 тысяч населения. В местах заключения Туркменистана эпидемии ВИЧ и туберкулеза Туркменистан остро нуждается в тюремной реформе. Вот что способно изменить ситуацию уже сейчас Оставь молодость всяк сюда входящий. body: Ливень в Дашогузском велаяте не стал преградой отправке людей на хлопок | Turkmen.News Ливень в Дашогузском велаяте не стал преградой отправке людей на хлопок 13.10.2026 | Важное | В воскресенье 11 октября в Туркменистане прошли ливневые дожди. За несколько часов выпала месячная норма осадков, вода затопила улицы городов и борозды междурядий на полях. Несмотря на это, бюджетные организации отправили своих сотрудников и наёмных сборщиков собирать хлопок . Вести работу было невозможно, так что сотни человеко-часов оказались потраченными впустую. Воскресный ливень вмешался в планы жителей Дашогузского велаята, а некоторых лишил имущества. В Болдумсазе месячная норма осадков всего за день была превышена почти вдвое — согласно архиву WeatherAPI, их выпало почти 10 мм. Затопленными оказались Куняургенчский этрап и административный центр велаята. В ТикТоке быстро распространился ролик, снятый на Бай-базаре Дашогуза: вода стоит в проходах торговых рядов, люди шагают в её потоках едва ли не по колено. Сейчас ролик удалён автором: туркменские силовики зачищают любой негативный контент из страны — даже о погоде. Впрочем, главный дашогузский базар затапливается далеко не впервые, так что подобные ролики напоминают и о недосмотре городских властей. Балканский велаят тоже залило. В районе посёлка Гумдаг дождём размыло дороги . В некоторых населённых пунктах пострадали палатки для торжеств: ковры оказались полностью под водой, сотрудники в спешке вытаскивали на возвышения аппаратуру и деревянную мебель. Празднования свадеб, дней рождения и поминок, ради которых люди их бронировали, пришлось переносить или сворачивать. Но не все организаторы трезво оценили ситуацию и скорректировали планы. Бюджетники, которые с началом хлопковой страды тратят свои официальные выходные на неоплачиваемую работу на поле, не смогли избежать её и в минувшее воскресенье. По словам одного из сотрудников в Дашогузе, сами арендаторы отказывались высылать за горожанами транспорт, понимая, что работать те всё равно не смогут. Однако чиновники всё-таки заставили людей совершить бессмысленную поездку. Приехавшим пришлось скинуться по пять манатов, чтобы отдать их водителю автобуса и доехать до нужного хозяйства. Они рассчитывали с ним же вернуться обратно, подтвердив на месте, что погода неподходящая для сбора хлопка. Но водителю было дано указание оставить пассажиров на месте и вернуться за ними не раньше пяти часов вечера. Сборщики прождали его, маясь без дела под дождём. «Мы промокли до нитки», — сообщает источник. Впрочем, по информации из других госучреждений Дашогуза , их работники, приехав на поля и увидев всю картину, всё же разворачивались и уезжали обратно. В понедельник те бюджетники, кто не смог откупиться от хлопковой барщины либо подмениться на другой день, вновь выехали на работу. Хотя дождя уже не было, всё равно условия, по словам источника, были неблагоприятные. Земля размокла — постелить плед или дастархан, чтобы отдохнуть или перекусить, было невозможно. По словам дехкан Марыйского велаята, этот год для хлопка крайне неудачный. Коробочки есть только на нижнем ярусе, близко к земле. Выше их уничтожили насекомые. Затопление полей, а дожди прошли и в Марыйском велаяте, может повредить существенную часть урожая. Штормовой ветер вызвал разрушения в Марыйском и Лебапском велаятах В Туркменистане заморозки. Фермеры пытаются спасти будущий урожай В Дашогузском велаяте ливень затопил главный рынок города В Туркменистане бюджетников вновь привлекают к сбору хлопка. body: Лента Россельхознадзор Омской области уничтожил 18 тонн зараженных томатов из Туркменистана Редакция 13 октября 2026 821 Важное ХТ Редакция - 13 октября 2026 Напасти в городе Туркменбаши Лента Редакция - 12 октября 2026 «Аркадаг» в четвёртый раз подряд досрочно стал чемпионом Туркменистана ХТ Редакция - 12 октября 2026 Меры противодействия беспилотникам предпринимались в аэропорту Туркменбаши во время прибытия Путина Лента Редакция - 11 октября 2026 Лукашенко промолчал о долге Туркменистана за строительство Гарлыкского ГОК В Омской области уничтожена партия импортных томатов весом 18 тонн из-за обнаружения вируса коричневой морщинистости плодов, сообщает Pravda.ru. Заражение было выявлено специалистами Россельхознадзора при досмотре груза из Туркменистана на складе временного хранения «ОМАС». Лабораторный анализ, проведенный в омском филиале Центра оценки качества продукции АПК, подтвердил наличие инфекции в двух партиях овощей. Для предотвращения заноса заболевания в регион груз был запрещен к ввозу и полностью сожжен под надзором инспекторов. Биологическая специфика данного вируса заключается в его высокой агрессивности по отношению к закрытому грунту: при попадании в теплицу патоген способен за семь дней поразить все растения, что ведет к потере до 80% урожая томатов и перцев. При этом для людей и животных инфекция остается безвредной. body: ICRC seeks access to Azerbaijani serviceman detained in Armenia 14 October 2026 12:49 (UTC+04:00) Akbar Novruz Read more The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is in contact with the relevant Armenian authorities regarding Azerbaijani serviceman Nasimi Musayev, who has been detained in Armenia. Zara Amatuni, head of communications for the ICRC delegation in Armenia, told Radio Azatutyun that the organisation was awaiting permission to visit the detained serviceman. "After receiving their consent, we will be able to meet him," Amatuni said. According to Armenian authorities, Musayev was detained following an incident on October 1, 2026, in the Shaki settlement of the Sisian community in Armenia's Syunik region. Armenian investigators said that at approximately 2:00 p.m., the Azerbaijani serviceman unlawfully entered a residential property at 20 Sixth Street and opened fire after being discovered. Reportedly, a woman identified as Ani Avetisyan, born in 1987, reportedly sustained injuries during the incident. According to the Armenian account, Musayev subsequently fled the property but was later located at another address in the same settlement, 26 Sixth Street. Armenian authorities initiated criminal proceedings under five articles of the country's Criminal Code, and Musayev was remanded in custody for two months. Meanwhile, Armenian media outlets published additional allegations concerning the circumstances of the incident. Arpi Avetisyan, identified as the injured woman's sister, claimed that the Azerbaijani serviceman had taken children hostage inside the house. She alleged that the woman lost three fingers on her left hand while attempting to protect the children and subsequently stabbed the serviceman with a knife as he attempted to reload his weapon. According to her account, after the woman lost consciousness, her son struck the serviceman in the head, sustaining a wrist fracture in the process. These allegations have been reported by Armenian sources and have not been independently verified. The ICRC has not announced a date for a possible visit to Musayev, with access remaining subject to approval by the relevant authorities. body: Hizb ut-Tahrir links emerge after hijab protest outside Azerbaijan’s embassy in Ankara 14 October 2026 00:53 (UTC+04:00) AzerNEWS Staff Read more Footage of a protest outside Azerbaijan’s embassy in Ankara over alleged restrictions on the hijab was first circulated by a media platform linked to the Islamist organisation Hizb ut-Tahrir, according to Azerbaijani media reports. Musavat.com investigated the platform, Köklü Değişim Medya, after it published the first footage of the demonstration on its X account, Turkustan.az reported. According to the investigation, Köklü Değişim Medya and Köklü Değişim Dergisi belong to the Turkish representation of Hizb ut-Tahrir. Hizb ut-Tahrir, whose name translates from Arabic as the “Party of Liberation”, is an international pan-Islamist and fundamentalist political organisation founded in Jerusalem in 1953 by Palestinian Islamic scholar Taqi al-Din al-Nabhani. Initially active in East Jerusalem, the organisation subsequently expanded its activities to dozens of countries, including Lebanon, Syria, Iraq, Egypt, Tunisia and Türkiye. According to publicly available sources, Hizb ut-Tahrir differs from other Islamist movements through its extensive ideological framework and its detailed vision of the political system it seeks to establish. The organisation is banned in several countries, including Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Russia, China and Uzbekistan. Members have been imprisoned in a number of these countries. Hizb ut-Tahrir is also officially banned in Azerbaijan. The protest outside Azerbaijan’s embassy in Ankara was held over claims of a hijab ban. The reported links between the platform that first circulated the footage and Hizb ut-Tahrir have drawn attention to the organisation behind the initial coverage of the demonstration. The available information does not establish whether Hizb ut-Tahrir organised the protest itself or had any direct involvement in arranging it. Tags: hijab Protests

Four major sports facilities are being built in Azerbaijan’s liberated territories to promote youth development and encourage young people to engage in sports. These include the Imarat Stadium in Aghdam, a stadium in Khankendi, and sports infrastructure in Fuzuli and Zangilan, Deputy Minister of Youth and Sports Farhad Hajiyev said at a panel session titled “Youth in Karabakh’s Revival: Initiatives and Opportunities,” held as part of the Rebuild Karabakh exhibition during Caspian Construction Week, Trend ’s correspondent reports from the event. He said Karabakh had become one of the state’s priority areas. In this regard, involving young people in discussions on the region’s revival was a logical approach, as Karabakh’s future development depended on today’s youth. Hajiyev noted that Khankendi had now become a genuine city of young people. Although Mingachevir previously held this status, the large number of students and young people in Khankendi was now a source of particular joy. According to him, Khankendi and Karabakh as a whole were experiencing a new spring. The deputy minister called on everyone to visit the liberated territories, saying that such visits evoked unique emotions and a profound sense of pride. Hajiyev emphasized that the Ministry of Youth and Sports operated within the framework of the tasks set by the state and was responsible for implementing relevant decrees, orders, and programs signed by the president. In this regard, the part of the state program outlining socioeconomic development priorities through 2030 that focuses on human capital development was particularly important. According to him, numerous events were being held in Khankendi and other liberated territories under this program. Some of these initiatives were aimed at integrating the local population. The ministry was also seeking to organize international events in these territories wherever possible, with a target of holding approximately one in every three international events there. Hajiyev recalled that in 2024, Khankendi was named the Youth Capital of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation member states, and several international events were held in the city that year. He said the organizers sought to recruit young volunteers primarily from among local residents, while giving preference to young people from Karabakh when selecting participants. This approach helped promote their integration into society and provided opportunities for personal development. The deputy minister noted that sports were another key area of the Ministry of Youth and Sports’ work, adding that sports played an important role in maintaining physical health and mental well-being. Four major sports facilities are currently under construction in the liberated territories. According to him, the historic Imarat Stadium is being built in Aghdam, while renovation work at the stadium in Khankendi is nearing completion. Hajiyev recalled that a football match was held at the Khankendi stadium in 2023 in the presence of Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev, with the team of the Karabakh Central Army Sports Club also taking part. The stadium is now undergoing a complete renovation. In addition, large sports complexes are being built in Fuzuli and Zangilan. “I believe that once these sports facilities become operational, our young people will make active use of them, because a healthy mind resides in a healthy body,” the deputy minister said. Hajiyev also highlighted the various youth programs currently being implemented in Karabakh. He welcomed a proposal by Member of Parliament Shahin Seyidzade to establish a special grant program for young people living in the region. The deputy minister said that when he and Seyidzade worked at the Youth Foundation, a grant program for individuals had been implemented, and this work was continuing. In his view, the Karabakh Revival Foundation could also contribute to such initiatives, helping integrate local young people. The Ministry of Youth and Sports was ready to play an active role in this process. He also stressed the importance of winners of the “Yukselish” competition working in Karabakh. According to the deputy minister, several competition winners were already working in the region, which was a source of pride for them. Hajiyev noted that one of the winners, who had worked for an international organization, had recently moved to Karabakh University. Despite previously working at an international organization in central Baku, the individual had decided to teach at Karabakh University, pursue educational activities, and serve as a program director. The deputy minister described this as an example demonstrating that the “Yukselish” competition had been the right choice. He said that people’s values could not be measured solely in material terms, as moral values were also important. According to him, participants representing various institutions were actively providing support. The “Yukselish” team had visited Karabakh several times with competition winners and implemented projects in the region. A forum for competition winners is also planned to be held in Karabakh by the end of this year. Hajiyev emphasized that the main goal was to keep Karabakh a constant priority and ensure the active participation of people living in the region, particularly young people, in ongoing initiatives. He said participation in the competition was voluntary and no one could be forced to take part. Nevertheless, he said, it was desirable for people living in Karabakh to participate actively in such competitions. The deputy minister expressed hope that Karabakh University would play an active role in this process. At the end of his remarks, Hajiyev said he believed the Rebuild Karabakh exhibition would become a regular event and could eventually be held in Karabakh itself. “I believe this exhibition will become an annual tradition and one day may be held in Karabakh as well. body: Home Azerbaijan Traditional war film-making to become difficult after "44" - journalist Azerbaijan News 14 October 2026 12:39 (UTC +04:00) Photo: provided by organizer BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 14. Making traditional war movies will be difficult after the film "44". This was stated by famous journalist Vyacheslav Sapunov in his post on Facebook following the grand premiere of the large-scale historical feature film "44," dedicated to the heroism of the Azerbaijani people during the Second Karabakh War, aimed at preserving historical memory and fostering patriotism among the younger generation, held at the Heydar Aliyev Center. “The premiere of the feature film ‘44’ took place at the Heydar Aliyev Center. An extraordinary audience gathered in the hall: ministers, filmmakers, architects, musicians, writers, journalists, and many other prominent figures. Films about the Karabakh War have been made here before. Perhaps not as many as one might wish, yet there have been worthy productions. However, ‘44’ is a unique, outstanding project. I cannot recall a war film of this scale ever being produced in Azerbaijan before. First and foremost, the sheer volume of work accomplished is staggering. Five years of production, over 130 filming locations, and thousands of extras, including active-duty military personnel and special forces troops. The core team numbered 455 people, while specialists from 13 countries were brought in for various stages of production. The scale of this undertaking is hard to even imagine, though it is clearly visible on screen. Anar Alakbarov, the film’s artistic director, co-wrote the screenplay with Ismayil Iman. The film was directed by Ismail Safarali and Maxim Smetana. The battle scenes are particularly impressive, featuring real tanks, armored vehicles, and weaponry, alongside numerous explosions and firefights. The production team had authentic military hardware at its disposal and worked with pyrotechnicians, stunt performers, and military consultants. Sound designer Teymur Karimov deserves special praise. It seems he meticulously crafted every gunshot, explosion, footstep, rustle, and breath. At times, one instinctively flinches at the sound of gunfire, while during moments of quiet, one hears subtle sounds that heighten the tension even further. Ruslan Aghababayev’s beautiful music, alternately lyrical, rapid, and poignant, weaves organically into the film’s symphony, unfailingly heightening the emotional impact of the action on screen. And, of course, the cinematography by Alexander Pozdnyakov is superb: sweeping mountain panoramas, rapid camera movements during combat sequences (it seems there is hardly a single static shot in the entire film), beautiful cityscapes, and intimate close-ups of the actors. The footage shot on the cliffs near Jidir Duzu is particularly striking; the camera shifts seamlessly from capturing vast expanses to positioning itself right alongside the fighters as they scramble up the rocks under enemy fire. At times, I had the uncanny sensation that I had already witnessed the events playing out on screen. Indeed, certain shots seemed to have stepped straight out of wartime documentary photographs I had seen in exhibitions, newspapers, or online, familiar angles, faces, scenes, and settings. Yet now, it all came to life and motion, filled with sounds and voices. You suddenly recognize what you had previously seen only in a still image, and this further reinforces the film’s historical authenticity. Another remarkable touch by the filmmakers relates to the tragic events in Ganja. Do you remember little Bakhtiyar Heydarli, whose photograph circulated around the world in October 2020? The boy, his face bloodied after surviving a missile strike on a peaceful city, was smiling despite the pain and the horror he had endured. Well, this episode made it into the film as well. In the movie, the boy is named Aydin, but it was obvious to me that the character was based on that very same Bakhtiyar. And what a perfect choice for the young actor! He bears a striking resemblance to the child in the famous photograph. Fortunately, the filmmakers also made room for scenes of everyday life. Characters fall in love, get married, quarrel, and await the return of their loved ones. Pre-war Baku is beautifully captured, featuring recognizable streets and stunning cityscapes. And the location shots outside the capital are magnificent: Lerik, wedding and funeral scenes, mountain landscapes, and the villages of Karabakh. Some shots are so beautifully filmed that one wants to linger over them. The protagonist, special forces officer Rashad Khalilov, is played by Ibrahim Chingiz, an actor from the Azerbaijan State Academic Russian Drama Theatre. He delivers a wonderful performance. His Rashad is vibrant and charming, far removed from any glossy or idealized caricature. He feels authentic. The same goes for his love interest, the Turkish doctor Zeynep, played by Özge Gürel. They make a beautiful on-screen couple, with their emotions ringing completely true. However, I would like to highlight two other performances in particular. The first is by Gurban Ismayilov, who plays the father of one of the special forces soldiers, a native of Lerik. He has very few lines, yet his facial expressions and range of emotion are extraordinary. The scene involving the map, where the father marks the Azerbaijani settlements that have been liberated, is brilliantly conceived. At first, he tracks the progress of his son and his comrades-in-arms; later, he continues the task as the father of a martyr. In the final moment, he drives a red thumbtack into the map at the location of Shusha. The emotion with which he performs this act is unforgettable. Without uttering a single word, Gurban Ismayilov conveys such a depth of feeling that this brief scene leaves as lasting an impression as the most spectacular battle sequences. Another standout performance comes from Hikmat Rahimov, who plays an Armenian sniper. He creates a truly chilling character, despite there being nothing outwardly demonic about his appearance. We see a man fanatically devoted to his cause, a selfless and skilled fighter ready to spare no one, not even his own compatriots, should they dare to acknowledge defeat. The battles for Hadrut and, of course, Shusha make a powerful impression. The assault on Shusha is arguably the highlight of the film’s combat sequences. Special forces soldiers scale nearly sheer cliffs meter by meter from the direction of Dashalti, fight their way into the city, and engage in fierce combat. The battle scenes in Shusha are filmed on a breathtaking scale; at times, watching them is truly terrifying. The soldiers feel authentic. They know how to fight, how to be friends, how to joke, and how to support one another. And, of course, they fear losing their comrades. These relationships are portrayed naturally, without unnecessary melodrama. We all know the historical outcome, yet that does not detract in the slightest from the suspense of the two-and-a-half-hour film. The transport infrastructure developed in Garabagh and East Zangezur connects residential settlements with one another and integrates them into the country’s unified economic space, President Ilham Aliyev said in a message to the participants of the 6th Azerbaijan International Restoration, Reconstruction and Development of Garabagh Exhibition – “Rebuild Garabagh.” "To date, nearly 1,500 kilometers of roads have been constructed, and the 11.7-kilometer Murovdag tunnel stands as an important example of engineering in complex mountainous terrain. Fuzuli, Zangilan and Lachin international airports have been commissioned, while railway construction continues. As an essential part of the Zangezur corridor, the Horadiz–Aghband railway is of strategic importance for expanding Azerbaijan’s international transport and logistics links. Energy and water supply infrastructure is also being developed to serve new residential settlements and production facilities. In the region, one new reservoir has been built and five have been restored, while 13 substations and 38 hydroelectric power plants with a total capacity of 307 megawatts have been commissioned. Developing Garabagh and East Zangezur as a “green energy zone” is one of the key priorities in building this infrastructure," the message said. Meanwhile, Caspian Construction Week, covering construction, the reconstruction of Garabagh, engineering and utility systems, the plastics and polymer industry, road infrastructure and public transport, has opened in Baku. Held at the Baku Expo Center from October 14 to 16, the event features four international exhibitions, alongside a separate international exhibition dedicated to road infrastructure and public transport. Caspian Construction Week serves as a platform for companies from various industries to showcase their products and solutions, bring together sector representatives and establish professional contacts. Its scope ranges from construction materials and heating and ventilation equipment to solutions for the reconstruction of Garabagh, plastics and polymers, road infrastructure and public transport. The exhibitions provide Azerbaijani and international companies with opportunities to present their products and technologies, keep up with market developments and discuss potential partnerships. Alongside the exhibition displays, the program includes panel discussions, innovation sessions and business presentations on a range of topics. Bilateral business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-government (B2G) meetings are also planned for exhibitors and invited companies. These meetings are intended to help participants explore cooperation opportunities with one another and with relevant government bodies. Over three days, Caspian Construction Week brings together stakeholders from construction, engineering, industry, the reconstruction of Garabagh, architecture and transport. The exhibitions and business events offer participants an opportunity to showcase products and technologies, follow industry developments and establish new business connections. body: Home Azerbaijan Chronicles of Victory: President Ilham Aliyev interviewed by France 24 TV channel on October 14, 2020 (PHOTO/VIDEO) Azerbaijan News 14 October 2026 07:00 (UTC +04:00) BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 14. President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev has been interviewed by France 24 TV channel. Trend presents the interview. -Hello and welcome to the France 24 interview. Today brought you from Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan. I am in the presence of President of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev. President Aliyev, thank you very much for accepting to answer our questions. Of course, I will be asking you about the conflict over Nagorno-Karabakh. Since the ceasefire, which was supposed to be a humanitarian truce, was signed, there has been continuing violence, continuing acts of war. I’m asking you today: is that ceasefire officially now dead, over, null, and void? -It depends on the behavior of Armenia. Because we are always committed to our responsibility, and the decision to announce the ceasefire on humanitarian grounds, as you know, came from Russia, and we supported it. Because I think it was a right decision in order to exchange the bodies of the dead soldiers and also hostages. Also to continue the activity on the negotiation table. Because the declaration that was announced in Moscow actually provided that negotiations will be based on the basic principles. That was always our position. Armenian side always tried to disrupt the process and was trying to introduce new approaches on negotiation table, which we rejected by us, and by the Minsk Group co-chairs. The most important part of the declaration along with other issues was that the format of negotiations will be unchanged. And that’s very important because for broad international audience maybe it’s not very clear what it means. I will probably give some more information about that. Because for the last two years after the new government in Armenia came to power, one of their activity was to bring the so-called "authorities of Nagorno-Karabakh" to the negotiation table and thus, to change the format. Because for more than 20 years, negotiations are being held between Armenia and Azerbaijan within the framework of the Minsk Group process. So, the attempts to bring the so-called "Nagorno-Karabakh authorities" were an attempt to change the format. So, when both sides commit that the format is unchanged that means that everything just is within the framework of what has been agreed before. We were observing the ceasefire. But as you know Armenia brutally violated it and not only in Ganja. The attack on civilians in Ganja was reflection of their aggressive policy. And also, they everyday violate ceasefire. I was informed this morning that since 7 o’clock to 9 o’clock in the morning they more than 150 times shelled the city of Tartar and Aghdam. And unfortunately, we have one victim today among civilians in Tartar. -But Azerbaijan has also continued to fire, has it not? The world has been seeing pictures of civilians under shelling in Stepanakert inside Nagorno-Karabakh. -First, since the ceasefire was announced, all the shelling from Azerbaijani side was stopped, second, we never deliberately attack civilians in any city or village on the occupied territories. Our targets were only military installations. Our military targets have been identified very carefully. Therefore, we only hit those targets, which was a threat to the lives of our people and our soldiers. But unfortunately, Armenians are using the tactics to install military equipment in the areas of the cities where people live. So, we had to protect ourselves. But since the ceasefire was established, we were committed to that, but Armenia violated it, so we had to respond. -So you are saying that there have been no strikes by Azerbaijan since the ceasefire was announced. Even on military targets? -No, on military targets there have been strikes, we do not deny it. But that’s natural, because we have to defend ourselves. Ceasefire cannot be achieved unilaterally. Otherwise, Armenia will get an advantage and will achieve its goal and actually what they are trying to do. They are trying to regain the territories that have been liberated. Particularly, they try to regain back the city of Hadrut, but they failed. My advice to them and I already publicly addressed Armenian leadership and also Armenian people, that they should stop trying to regain what has been liberated back. That will only cause new victims and will lead to bloodshed. -What about the pictures of bombings on churches inside Nagorno-Karabakh there is not military targets, surely. -Yes, you are right. We are investigating that issue, I’d like to say that Azerbaijan is a country with a very high level of religious tolerance, which was reflected by all the major international organizations, including United Nations. During the visit of His Holiness head of the Vatican, Pope Francis to Baku, he publicly declared that the level of intercultural dialogue, interreligious dialogue in Azerbaijan is very high. You have probably seen the Armenian church in the center of Baku, which was restored by us. And we protected it as the heritage of Armenian people. In that church, we keep more than 5,000 ancient books in Armenian language. But what Armenia has done to our mosques? What have they done to the mosques of Aghdam, mosque of Fuzuli, mosque of Shusha? They not only almost destroyed them, but they keep animals there. They keep pigs there, thus insulting the feelings of all the Muslims, not only us. I am not saying that we did it in revenge, no. We need to investigate this issue, we are not sure about what happened. We have doubts that could have been done by Armenians in order to blame us. If it was done, if it was done by Azerbaijani military units, that was a mistake, and we don’t have any historical or religious targets among those targets which we have. -I want to ask you about the diplomatic process now. Mediation has been ongoing with the OSCE Minsk group, the co-chairs at the moment France, US and Russia. Do you think that structure, should remain that France should remain a co-chair in those negotiations? -We are receiving some contradictory statements and messages from the very beginning of the outbreak. But I think that due to our mutual diplomatic efforts, we managed to keep the situation under control. As you know, I received several phone calls from president Macron. And our last conversation was very positive. We committed to our efforts to find a political solution to the conflict. I was informed that France as a co-chair will remain neutral, because that’s the mandate for a co-chair. This morning I was informed that the French foreign minister issued a statement that due to the fact that France is a co-chair of the Minsk Group, it must be neutral. We fully support this position and our position always was that all the co-chairs must be neutral. They should not take sides, because it’s contradicting their mandate. In a national capacity, every country has allies and friends, with some countries having more active relations, with some countries less active relations. This is normal and no one is objecting that. But if some countries have a mandate to be a mediator, of course, both sides, I am sure, Armenia and Azerbaijan expects neutrality, and we see this neutrality now. Therefore, I think the issue which you are referring to now is over. So, we have closed that page. -In previous interviews, you’ve called for an apology from Emmanuel Macron, after his remarks saying that 300 fighters from Syria have been brought to fight for your side. When you last spoke to him, did you speak about this issue-him accusing mercenaries are fighting for your side? -Yes, of course. Yes, we spoke about that and I was still waiting for evidence. President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev addressed the participants of the 6th Azerbaijan International Restoration, Reconstruction and Development of Garabagh Exhibition – “Rebuild Garabagh.” The text of the address was published on the official website of the President of Azerbaijan. "Dear exhibition participants, I sincerely welcome you on the occasion of the opening of the 6th Azerbaijan International Restoration, Reconstruction and Development of Garabagh Exhibition – “Rebuild Garabagh” and wish all participants every success. The Victory achieved in the 44-day Patriotic War laid the foundation for a new phase of construction and development in Garabagh and East Zangazur. Under the First State Program on the Great Return, our towns and villages are being rebuilt, with the safe return of our compatriots to their native lands being ensured. Azerbaijan is carrying out this work using its own financial resources. To date, 25.5 billion manats have been allocated from the state budget for restoration and reconstruction. To ensure the safe implementation of the Great Return, more than 300,000 hectares of land have been cleared of mines and unexploded ordnance, and over 40,000 people have returned to 47 residential settlements. Currently, nearly 100,000 people live, study and work in the liberated territories. The transport infrastructure developed in Garabagh and East Zangazur connects residential settlements with one another and integrates them into the country’s unified economic space. To date, nearly 1,500 kilometers of roads have been constructed, and the 11.7-kilometer Murovdag tunnel stands as an important example of engineering in complex mountainous terrain. Fuzuli, Zangilan and Lachin international airports have been commissioned, while railway construction continues. As an essential part of the Zangezur corridor, the Horadiz–Aghband railway is of strategic importance for expanding Azerbaijan’s international transport and logistics links. Energy and water supply infrastructure is also being developed to serve new residential settlements and production facilities. In the region, one new reservoir has been built and five have been restored, while 13 substations and 38 hydroelectric power plants with a total capacity of 307 megawatts have been commissioned. Developing Garabagh and East Zangazur as a “green energy zone” is one of the key priorities in building this infrastructure. Infrastructure development is accompanied by the provision of modern social services in residential settlements. Forty educational institutions and 20 healthcare facilities, as well as Garabagh University in Khankendi, have commenced operations in the region. The coverage of government, banking, postal and telecommunications services is also expanding. The administrative centers built and commissioned in Lachin, Zangilan, Fuzuli and Aghdam enable the provision of social security, employment and other services to residents under one roof. Infrastructure development is complemented by efforts to restore the historical and cultural identity of Garabagh and East Zangazur. The restoration of historical, cultural and religious monuments destroyed or damaged during the occupation, together with the development of modern tourism infrastructure, helps preserve the region’s rich heritage, revive its cultural and spiritual life, and realize its tourism potential. The revitalization of the region also involves addressing the environmental consequences of the occupation. During the occupation, 54,300 hectares of forestland were destroyed, and land and water resources were polluted. To date, 600 hectares of forestland have been restored. The restoration of forests and aquatic ecosystems, along with the application of climate-resilient construction solutions, is particularly important for the region’s long-term development. The main objective of the second phase of the State Program on the Great Return is to further expand private investment, permanent employment and export-oriented production by building on the opportunities already created, and to strengthen the position of Garabagh and Eastern Zangazur as a new growth centre in the national economy. The advanced urban planning and engineering solutions applied in the region offer experience that can be used internationally, alongside that gained in other parts of Azerbaijan. In this regard, the successful hosting of the 13th session of the World Urban Forum (WUF13) in Baku in 2026, organized by the UN Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat), helped showcase our country’s achievements in urban planning internationally and strengthen its role in global dialogue. The “Rebuild Garabagh” and “BakuBuild” exhibitions, held as part of Caspian Construction Week, provide broad opportunities to share this experience, showcase new technologies and establish business partnerships. I am confident that these partnerships will translate into concrete projects and make a significant contribution to the Great Return and the region’s long-term development. I wish the exhibition every success and each of you further achievements in your work," the address reads. body: Home Azerbaijan Politics Azerbaijan reports coordinated troll attacks from Iran, Türkiye – statement Politics News 14 October 2026 11:05 (UTC +04:00) Humay Aghajanova Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 14. Coordinated troll attacks against Azerbaijan from Iran and Türkiye have intensified. This was reflected in a statement released by the Media and Broadcasting Council. According to the statement, in recent days, there has been a clear trend of civic activists, politicians, and even officials operating abroad actively participating in targeted information campaigns against Azerbaijan. The statement noted that such activities, driven by political and ideological motives and characterized by the manipulation of public opinion and interference in the country's internal affairs, represent an unacceptable instance of abusing the information space and attempting to undermine public trust. “The mass spread of posts featuring identical spelling errors and writing styles, the repetitive ‘copy-pasting’ of similar comments, and the circulation of edited photos and videos unrelated to our country constitute primitive and easily identifiable methods of coordinated troll attacks. The fact that over 400 posts were shared in a short period using an Azerbaijani-language hashtag, despite the posters being foreign-language speakers, combined with instances where the content consisted solely of the hashtag or involved the repeated dissemination of the same material from a single account, clearly demonstrates the manipulative nature of these campaigns and provokes justified public discontent and outrage toward their organizers and participants. Making such posts via various anonymous accounts, as well as inciting citizens to disturb public order through negative comments and reactions, is entirely contrary to the requirements of both the legislation of the Republic of Azerbaijan and international law, and entails legal liability. We view the intensification of targeted information attacks originating from Iran and Türkiye, particularly via the Telegram, X, and TikTok platforms, as incompatible with the principles of safeguarding information security, mutual respect in interstate relations, and international cooperation against disinformation, and we strongly condemn them. The fact that baseless and biased material regarding Azerbaijan, as well as threats, intimidation, and insults directed at the Azerbaijani state and its people, has become commonplace in the media and social media sectors of those countries, coupled with the failure of the relevant authorities to take any action in this regard, is causing concern and serious discontent among our public. The Media and Broadcasting Council of Azerbaijan once again calls upon citizens, media entities, and social media users to remain vigilant against such manipulative campaigns, to refrain from participating in the dissemination of false information, and to demonstrate a responsible and principled stance against attempts to damage our country's reputation," the statement added. Kazakhstan's construction sector is projected to grow by 17.3% in 2029, up from 16% in 2027, as infrastructure development and modernization support economic activity, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy Serik Zhumangarin said during a Mazhilis session. This was reflected in the statement, published by the press service of the Kazakh government. "The growth rate of the manufacturing industry will outpace that of the mining industry. Metallurgy, mechanical engineering, the production of building materials, the chemical industry, and food production will make the primary contribution to growth in the manufacturing sector," he noted. Agriculture is also expected to drive economic growth, with average annual growth projected at no less than 5%. Zhumangarin said that the projected expansion would be supported by the continued development of transport and logistics, energy and water infrastructure, as well as the modernization of housing and utilities and social infrastructure. Meanwhile, inflation is expected to gradually decline, reaching 7.5-9.5% in 2027 and 6-8% in 2028-2029. The macroeconomic projections have been used to prepare the forecast budget parameters and National Fund indicators for 2027-2029. Yesterday at the government meeting Zhumangarin noted that Kazakhstan's annual inflation slowed to 9.3% in September 2026, down from 9.8% in August. "Containing inflation is one of the government's priorities in its efforts to increase real incomes. Amid slowing inflation, real household monetary incomes rose by 0.7% in the second quarter of this year, compared with 0.1% in the first quarter," he added. body: Home Azerbaijan Society Karabakh, East Zangezur emerge as new non-oil growth hubs – minister Society News 14 October 2026 09:40 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Trend News Agency Alish Abdulla Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 14. The expansion of production capacity in Karabakh and East Zangezur is turning the regions into new growth hubs for Azerbaijan’s non-oil and gas sector, Azerbaijani Economy Minister Mikayil Jabbarov said in a message to participants of the sixth Azerbaijan International Exhibition for Restoration, Reconstruction and Development of Karabakh (Rebuild Garabagh), Trend ’s correspondent reports from the exhibition. The minister noted that Rebuild Garabagh, held as part of Caspian Construction Week, is an important platform bringing together reconstruction efforts in the liberated territories and investment opportunities being created in the regions. He said that, under the leadership of President Ilham Aliyev, residential areas being developed in Karabakh and East Zangezur under the “smart city” and “smart village” concepts, along with new transport corridors, green energy initiatives, and social projects, reflect the state’s strategic vision for these territories. According to Jabbarov, consistent and systematic reconstruction efforts have created broad opportunities for sustainable resettlement and economic development in the regions. The minister emphasized that tax and customs exemptions, preferential loans, loan guarantees and subsidies, industrial parks equipped with ready-to-use infrastructure, and other incentives introduced to promote entrepreneurship in the liberated territories have created a favorable business environment. He noted that additional support mechanisms had also been established under decrees signed by the president. These include covering a significant portion of the costs of transporting goods to foreign markets, including new and alternative destinations, from the state budget, as well as compensating exporters for customs clearance costs. These and other measures will help exporters operating in the liberated territories strengthen their positions in domestic and international markets. Jabbarov said that the launch of new manufacturing facilities in Karabakh and East Zangezur, along with an increase in the number of residents at the Aghdam Industrial Park and the Araz Valley Economic Zone Industrial Park, demonstrates the rapid realization of the regions’ industrial potential. “These projects will not only meet domestic demand but also enable the export of competitive products and the development of new value chains,” the minister said. He added that the regions’ abundant natural resources, favorable geographical location, energy potential, transport and logistics capabilities, and tourism prospects offer extensive opportunities for investors. According to the minister, the regions have substantial geological reserves, and extraction has already begun at several deposits. Intensive projects are also being implemented in agriculture, particularly in horticulture and livestock farming. Jabbarov emphasized that the launch of the Zangezur Corridor would further enhance the regions’ transport and logistics potential. He also noted that Karabakh and East Zangezur offer additional investment opportunities in tourism thanks to their ancient history, scenic landscapes, rich cultural heritage, and therapeutic mineral water resources. The minister called on business representatives to explore the regions’ economic potential and launch new projects. “We are confident that the Rebuild Garabagh exhibition will help present the regions’ economic potential to the business community, generate new investment initiatives and partnerships, and accelerate regional development,” Jabbarov said. He thanked all partners involved in organizing the exhibition and wished participants and visitors success, productive meetings, and new opportunities for cooperation. body: Home Central Asia Kazakhstan Kazakhstan’s general government revenue falls to 21.2% of GDP - ADB Kazakhstan News 14 October 2026 06:12 (UTC +04:00) Photo: ADB Alyona Pavlenko Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 14. Kazakhstan's general government revenue declined by 2.5 percentage points year-on-year in the first half of 2026, according to Trend's calculations based on data from the Asian Development Bank's (ADB) Asian Development Outlook. "In the first half of 2026, general government revenue declined to 21.2% of GDP from 23.7% in the same period of 2025. Transfers from the National Fund of the Republic of Kazakhstan, the sovereign wealth fund, fell to 2.6% of GDP from 5.1%, reflecting the absence of targeted transfers", the ADB said. The bank noted that tax revenue edged up to 17.7% of GDP from 17.5%, driven by nominal increases of 41.9% in value-added tax (VAT) and 7.3% in corporate income tax, while higher oil prices boosted crude oil export duties by 23.3%. "Nontax revenue decreased to 0.6% of GDP from 1.0%. General government expenditure declined to 24.4% of GDP from 25.3%. The state budget deficit widened to 3.2% of GDP from 1.6%, while the non-oil deficit narrowed to 7.1% of GDP from 7.9%. Debt service costs rose to 3.0% of GDP from 2.7%", the ADB said. According to Trend's calculations, nontax revenue fell by 0.4 percentage points, while general government expenditure declined by 0.9 percentage points. The state budget deficit widened by 1.6 percentage points, while the non-oil deficit narrowed by 0.8 percentage points. Debt service costs rose by 0.3 percentage points. body: Home Azerbaijan Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan cooperation boosts Middle Corridor efficiency - minister Azerbaijan News 13 October 2026 20:39 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Trend News Agency Fuad Namazov Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 13. Cooperation between Azerbaijan and Turkmenistan plays an important role in enhancing the efficiency of the Middle Corridor, and transit volumes are growing year after year, the country's Minister of Economy Mikayil Jabbarov said at a gala reception in Baku marking the 35th anniversary of Turkmenistan’s independence, Trend 's correspondent reports. “Cooperation between Azerbaijan and Turkmenistan plays a key role in enhancing the efficiency of the Middle Corridor. Transit volumes are increasing year after year,” the minister noted. According to him, Turkmenistan has a modern transportation infrastructure and has made significant investments in its seaport, railways, and other logistics facilities. The international transport route across the Caspian Sea connects Central Asia with the South Caucasus and, further on, with Türkiye and European markets. The ports of Baku (Alat) and Turkmenbashi are important hubs on this route, facilitating the transshipment of cargo between maritime and land transport. In February 2026, representatives of railway companies from Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, and Georgia discussed expanding cooperation within the framework of the Middle Corridor, increasing freight traffic, and digitizing transportation. In April, during talks in Baku, representatives from Azerbaijan and Turkmenistan explored opportunities to more fully utilize the potential of seaports and increase transit shipments. In June 2025, the first freight train departed from the Chinese city of Jinhua for Baku via Turkmenistan along the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR). The train, consisting of 100 containers, traveled to the port of Turkmenbashi, from where the cargo was to be transported across the Caspian Sea to Baku. This route expands the options for delivering cargo from China to Central Asia, the South Caucasus, and onward to Europe. body: Ukraine crisis Russia to convene Arria-formula meeting on human rights violations in Ukraine on Oct. 14 The format suggests the participation of all members of the UN Security Council © Valery Sharifulin/TASS UN, October 14. /TASS/. The UN Security Council will hold an informal Arria-formula meeting at Russia’s initiative on October 14, focused on human rights violations in Ukraine, according to the Security Council’s work program. The meeting is titled "Piercing the Blind Spots of Violations of International Humanitarian Law and International Human Rights Law in the Context of the Ukrainian Crisis." The Arria-formula meetings provide interested council members an opportunity to engage in a direct dialogue with high representatives of governments and international organizations, as well as non-state parties, on matters with which they are concerned and which fall within the purview of responsibility of the Security Council. The process is named after Ambassador Diego Arria of Venezuela, who initiated the practice in 1992. The format suggests the participation of all members of the Security Council. body: Hokkaido Shimbun reporter arrested on espionage charges, taken to Moscow The Investigative Directorate of the Russian Federal Security Service has initiated a criminal case against the Japanese citizen © Russian Federal Security Service/TASS MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. A correspondent for the Japanese newspaper Hokkaido Shimbun in Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk in Russia’s Far East has been detained on suspicion of espionage, transported to Moscow and placed in custody, the FSB said. "On the eve of his departure from our country, the foreign national was detained in the Sakhalin Region and then taken to Moscow. The Investigative Directorate of the FSB of Russia has initiated a criminal case against the Japanese citizen under Article 276 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (espionage)," it said. "By a decision of the Lefortovsky District Court of Moscow, he has been placed under arrest. Further investigative and operational activities are being carried out." body: Председатель парламентского комитета по общественным объединениям и религиозным учреждениям Фазиль Мустафа считает, что ношение хиджаба в школе нужно было запретить. Фото с сайта www.gov.az Жители Азербайджана рассказывают о замедлении интернета в республике. Теперь, чтобы воспользоваться привычными социальными сетями, им приходится подключать виртуальную частную сеть. Официальный Баку не комментирует ситуацию, однако местные блогеры уверены, что это связано с массовыми протестами, вызванными запретом носить хиджаб в школе. Школьный дресс-код был утвержден правительством 21 сентября, а с 12 октября детей и учителей, которые ему не соответствуют, перестали пускать в учебные заведения. Среди недовольных новыми правилами оказались ветераны второй войны за Карабах. Они недоумевают, почему несколько лет назад они проливали кровь за свою страну, некоторые получили тяжелые ранения, в том числе лишились конечностей, а теперь их дочерям не дают учиться, потому что они мусульманки. Кроме того, в Сеть попало видео, записанное учительницей, на котором она при всем классе требует от девочки в возрасте семи-восьми лет снять платок. Ребенок плачет, но не подчиняется. На другом видео женщина стоит в школе возле доски с портретами солдат, погибших в карабахской войне, и требует либо допустить дочку к учебе, либо снять изображение ее отца. В первый же день, когда детей перестали пускать в школу, появились кадры штурма учебных заведений и как минимум одной сожженной машины директора. В результате массовых беспорядков было задержано не менее 37 человек. Им грозит до трех лет лишения свободы. «Главная цель этих мер... предотвратить перекрытие движения и нарушение нормального функционирования учебных заведений, а также обеспечить безопасность учащихся, преподавателей и других граждан», – говорится в заявлении МВД Азербайджана. Примечательно, что большинство СМИ республики полностью проигнорировали протесты. Пока в Баку дети и их родители осаждали школы, журналисты рассказывали о визите в республику премьер-министра Камбоджи Хун Манета. Однако те же самые издания во всех подробностях освещают протесты школьников во Франции, а саму Пятую республику обвиняют в империализме и неоколониализме. Тем временем председатель парламентского комитета по общественным объединениям и религиозным учреждениям Фазиль Мустафа считает, что ношение хиджаба в школе нужно было запретить, так как через него иностранные государства «отравляют» маленьких азербайджанцев своей идеологией. «После школы пусть тот, кто хочет, носит хиджаб, ведь на это нет запрета. К тому, что кто-то во дворе, дома, в месте поклонения, в мечети, на дороге, на улице носит, – к этому ведь нет возражений? Пойдите посмотрите на соседнюю страну – разве там сможешь пройти по улице без платка?» – добавил Мустафа. Глава телеканала Prime TV Айгун Мурадханли вовсе назвала протестующих родителей салафитами и агентами Ирана. «Протестующие против запрета на ношение хиджаба в школах – это в основном люди, связанные с Ираном. Другие протестующие – салафиты, и нет сомнений, что они также связаны с определенными центрами. Люди, которые раздувают эту проблему в социальных сетях, не заинтересованы в образовании своих детей, особенно девочек. Они даже не отправляют своих детей в школу. У них есть свои школы в садовых районах Баку. Все об этом знают, но почему-то правительство не знает», – сказала она. Глава центра политических исследований «Атлас» Эльхан Шахиноглу рассказал «НГ», что Азербайджан – светская мусульманская страна, в которой нет никаких проблем с исполнением религиозных обрядов, а количество мечетей постоянно растет. В то же время некоторые страны, включая Иран и Саудовскую Аравию, усиливают свое влияние на азербайджанских мусульман, подогревая среди них радикальные настроения. «В то время как Иран поддерживает шиитский радикализм в Азербайджане, Саудовская Аравия сыграла роль в формировании салафитского движения... Когда началась война в Сирии, некоторые выходцы из Азербайджана присоединились к местным террористам. В Иране сформировались радикальные религиозные группы, состоящие из бывших граждан Азербайджана, которые призывают к смене правительства в Баку и созданию исламской республики. Они пытаются влиять на религиозные семьи в Азербайджане через иранские веб-сайты... Азербайджанские власти и граждане, поддерживающие секуляризм, обеспокоены этим... С помощью запрета ношения хиджаба в школе можно идентифицировать радикальные силы. Религиозные семьи имеют два выбора: либо разрешить своим дочерям ходить в школу в форме, либо не отправлять детей в школу. Азербайджанское правительство не отступит», – сказал Шахиноглу. В свою очередь, кавказовед Владимир Новиков считает, что запрет хиджаба – часть борьбы с оппозиционными настроениями в Азербайджане. «Ранее президент Азербайджана Ильхам Алиев успешно решил для себя проблему светской оппозиции, но недовольные стали концентрироваться вокруг религии. Соответственно он атакует и в этом направлении, тем самым укрепляя свой режим. В то же время следует отметить, что этот процесс носит стихийный характер, но есть заинтересованные в нем игроки. Например, главный советник президента Турции Октай Сарал открыто выступил против запрета хиджаба. Кроме того, есть определенные брожения среди старых элит, сформировавшихся в период правления Гейдара Алиева. В целом сама по себе история с хиджабами вряд ли получит какое-то серьезное продолжение, но в Азербайджане, очевидно, сформировалась новая линия напряжения, которая еще даст о себе знать», – рассказал «НГ» Новиков.

body: Президент Касым-Жомарт Токаев объявил о проведении досрочных выборов в местные органы власти. Фото с сайта www.akorda.kz Казахстан готовится к внеочередным выборам маслихатов – местных советов депутатов. Президент Касым-Жомарт Токаев 12 октября досрочно прекратил их полномочия и поручил Центризбиркому организовать голосование. По закону оно должно пройти в течение двух месяцев. Обновление местных советов станет следующей проверкой политической реформы. Директор центра актуальных исследований «Альтернатива» Андрей Чеботарев предполагает, что голосование состоится 6 декабря: предельный срок, 12 декабря, выпадает на субботу. Пока это экспертный прогноз. ЦИК не торопится с назначением даты досрочного голосования, ожидая, вероятно, послания Токаева. Президент обещал обозначить в нем цели и задачи на предстоящий период. Политолог Эдуард Полетаев связывает необходимость досрочных выборов с изменениями партийной системы: большинство местных депутатов избиралось от AMANAT («Доверие»), объявившей о присоединении к недавно созданной партии «Адилет» («Справедливость»). «Это закономерно поднимает вопрос о легитимности значительной части действующего депутатского корпуса», – считает эксперт. Это политическая оценка, которая сама по себе не означает юридической утраты мандатов. Полетаев считает обновление своевременным: «От их вердиктов зависят бюджеты, развитие городов и районов, а также решение многих вопросов, с которыми жители сталкиваются каждый день». Перестройка партийной системы уже отразилась на составе маслихатов. По подсчетам BES.media, опубликованным до указа об их роспуске, около 13 местных депутатов перешли в Курултай, еще примерно 9 сложили полномочия по другим причинам. Четыре депутата маслихата Алматы утратили мандаты после выхода из AMANAT, став кандидатами в Курултай от «Адилет». Аналогичная ситуация возникла у депутата Западно-Казахстанского областного маслихата Турарбека Тлемисова. В области Абай прекратились полномочия Эльзиры Солтабаевой, Съезбека Ахметова и Эрлана Батырбекова, также вошедших в список «Адилета». Партийная перестройка затронула юридические основания представительства. На референдуме 15 марта была принята новая Конституция, вступившая в силу 1 июля 2026 года. Двухпалатный парламент уступил место однопалатному Курултаю. Депутаты участвуют в согласовании ключевых назначений, включая премьер-министра и вице-президента. Однако президент сохраняет право освобождать их от должности, а повторный отказ согласовать кандидатуры может стать основанием для роспуска Курултая. На выборах 23 августа «Адилет» получила, по данным ЦИК, 71,17% голосов и 110 из 145 мандатов – почти 76% депутатских мест. Большинство может обходиться без поддержки меньшинства. Но это еще не означает независимости парламента. Ее практическим показателем станет готовность депутатов оспаривать решения исполнительной власти и добиваться их пересмотра. Оценки парламентской кампании расходятся. Председатель ЦИК Нурлан Абдиров заявил, что «были созданы комплексные условия для волеизъявления граждан». Международные наблюдатели в предварительном заключении БДИПЧ ОБСЕ отметили хорошую техническую подготовку, но недостаток политического плюрализма: все участвовавшие партии поддерживали курс президента. Они также указали на ограничения независимого выдвижения и нарушения при подсчете голосов. На местном уровне пространство для самостоятельного участия шире. В областных маслихатах, Астане, Алмате и Шымкенте (прежнее название Чимкент) половина депутатов избирается по партийным спискам, половина – по одномандатным округам. В районных и остальных городских маслихатах действует одномандатная система, допускающая самовыдвижение. В Курултай кандидаты проходят только через партии. Местная кампания проверит шансы независимых участников. Проверять результат реформы придется и на повседневных конфликтах. Работники Карагандинской сельскохозяйственной опытной станции имени А.Ф. Христенко заявили о многомесячной задержке зарплаты, об этом сообщила 12 октября общественная организация Казахстана «Фонд-бюро расследования коррупции» со ссылкой на медиаресурс msu.city. Речь идет о задолженности за июль и август в 52 млн тенге (9,7 млн руб.). Не добившись решения на уровне предприятия, сотрудники попросили президента Токаева вмешаться, организовать проверку и обеспечить выплаты. Одно обращение не характеризует настроения всего общества. Однако выбор адресата показателен: сотрудники связывают восстановление своих прав с вмешательством президента. Защиту трудовых прав должны обеспечивать инспекция, суд и профильные ведомства; депутаты могут добиваться их реакции. Пока для решения такой проблемы требуется публичная апелляция к главе государства, вопрос о действенности промежуточных институтов остается открытым. Политолог Досым Сатпаев еще в сентябре 2025 года, обсуждая парламентскую реформу, предлагал учитывать социальные критерии оценки власти: «насколько успешна борьба с инфляцией, растут ли зарплаты, будет ли возможность дать своим детям хорошее образование». Выборы маслихатов возвращают дискуссию к этим вопросам. Обновление депутатского корпуса приобретет смысл, если жители смогут защищать свои интересы через избранных представителей, не обращаясь каждый раз к президенту.

body: Парламент Грузии рассмотрит поправки к закону о Национальном банке, которые определят полномочия центробанка в отношении эмиссии и обращения цифровых лари, сообщила пресс-служба парламента. «Представленный в парламент законопроект определяет статус цифрового лари – он расширяет понятия «денежные купюры» и «выпуск», а также отражает выпуск денег в цифровой форме», – говорится в сообщении. По словам председателя финансово-бюджетного комитета парламента Пааты Квижинадзе, Грузия в ближайшее время не сможет внедрить цифровую нацвалюту, но у Национального банка появится возможность приобрести все необходимые программы и инфраструктуру для выпуска цифрового лари в перспективе. Ранее президент Нацбанка Натия Турнава подчеркивала, что в Грузии формируется передовая нормативно-правовая среда для цифровых активов, а государственный проект цифрового лари развивается отдельно от частных инициатив стейблкоинов. В Грузии уже работают три цифровых банка. Кроме того, создана регуляторная база для поставщиков услуг виртуальных активов (VASP). В марте Национальный банк Грузии разрешил компаниям-резидентам выпускать стейблкоины в местной валюте – лари и иностранной валюте. В мае одна из крупнейших международных криптовалютных компаний Tether заявила, что выпустит привязанный к грузинской нацвалюте стейблкойн GELT. По информации Интерфакса
